items.text: SPEECH OF THE MINISTER FOR AGRICULTURE - FARMERS WELFARE Thiru. M.R.K. PANNEERSELVAM AGRICULTURE INTERIM BUDGET 2026 - 2027 Thiruvalluvar Aandu - 2057, Masi 05, Thiruvalluvar Aandu - 2057, Masi 05, 17-02-2026 17-02-2026 Thiruvalluvar Aandu - 2057, Masi 05, 17-02-2026 Honourable Speaker ! The farmers possess the honour of giving life to all the living beings on earth. If the farmers don’t toil in the soil, the survival of humanity itself cannot be guaranteed. Through the verse ”உழுவார் உலகத்தார்க்கு ஆணி” the poet-saint Thiruvalluvar, has emphasized that the farmers are the linchpin of the world. In the year 2021-22, the Department of Agriculture was renamed as Agriculture - Farmers Welfare Department placing greater emphasis on the welfare of farmers and several special schemes were also initiated for their upliftment. An exclusive budget for agriculture was introduc ed for the first time in the history of Tamil Nadu during the year 2021- 22. As per the guidance of the Hon’ble Chief Minister, 28 consultative meetings were held across the state with various stakeholders like farmers, farmer associations, Organic farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations, representatives of agricultural input dealers’ association, agricultural machinery manufacturers, seed producers, Traders, Egg and Dairy farmers, marine and inland fishermen, agricultural experts and people’s representatives . Their suggestions 2 were received both directly and through e -mail and petitions.

items.text: Their suggestions 2 were received both directly and through e -mail and petitions. Based on the inputs received from various stakeholders, an allocation of Rs.1,94,076 crore has been made towards the agriculture and allied sectors in the last five Agriculture Budgets with the objective of fulfilling the needs of farmers. I express my sincere gratitude to the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu for granting me the rare and esteemed opportunity to present five Agriculture Budgets endowed with various schemes aimed at uplifting the lives of the farmers on the floor of this august Assembly, and for entrusting me with the responsibility of presenting the schemes, activities and achievements of the Agriculture – Farmers Welfare Department as part of the Interim Budget for the year 2026-27. As the agriculture sector forms the foundation of Tamil Nadu’s economic growth, this Government is making sustained and determined efforts to modernize the sector, enhance the income of farmers, increase production and productivity and ensure food and nutritional security. In order t o achieve comprehensive agricultural development across all the 12,525 village Panchayats of Tamil Nadu, “ Kalaignarin All Village Integrated 3 Agricultural Development Programme ” is being implemented in con vergence with the Anaithu Grama Anna Marumala rchi Thittam since the year 2021- 22. So far, an expenditure of Rs.707 crore has been incurred, benefitting 61 lakh beneficiaries. A total of 58,712 acres of fallow land ha s been brought under cultivation including 6,048 acres under perennial horticultural crops and 52,664 acres under short duration agricultural crops.

items.text: A total of 58,712 acres of fallow land ha s been brought under cultivation including 6,048 acres under perennial horticultural crops and 52,664 acres under short duration agricultural crops. Also, 41,804 acres of individual farmers’ fallow lands have been brought into cultivation through bush clearance, levelling and ploughing . Also, 53 lakh Coconut seedlings have been distributed to encourage C oconut cultivation besides distributing and 21 lakh fruit seedling kits to ensure nutritional security in rural areas. B ore wells/ tube wells have been created to support cultivation for 2,115 Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribe farmers. A total of 10,588 minor irrigation tanks, oorunies, supply channels and water storage structures have been desilted and improved. Also, 885 drying yards with sorting and grading hall have been constructed. The implementation of various components such as the distribution of 1.32 lakh sprayers, supply of crop production inputs, technology dissemination, training programmes and creation of irrigation and value -addition 4 infrastructure has significantly benefited farmers in the selected Village Panchayats. With the objective of protecting soil fertility and promot ing organic farming practices for the welfare of the people, a flagship scheme titled “Chief Minister’s Mannuyir Kaathu Mannuyir Kaappom Scheme’’ was introduced in Tamil Nadu from 2024-25 and implemented with an allocation of Rs.178 crore, benefiting about 21.35 lakh farmers. In the year 2025 -26 also, this scheme is being implemented with an allocation of Rs.142 crore by integrating 15 components.

items.text: In the year 2025 -26 also, this scheme is being implemented with an allocation of Rs.142 crore by integrating 15 components. As a result, health of the soil, which sustains both crops and living beings has improved leading to better crop growth and enhanced human health. I am pleased to inform this August Assembly that the implementation of components such as distribution of green manure seeds, soil health management, establishment of organic input production centres, promotion of organic farming and agroforestry, with a total outlay of Rs.320 crore, has contributed significantly to the improvement of soil and human health. Nammazhwar propagated natural farming by emphasizing that “The earth is our mother, whatever 5 happens to her will happen to us tomorrow; because the earth does not belong to man; man belongs to the earth,”. Following his philosophy, various initiatives are being implemented to promote natural farming. In particular, the ‘Nammazhwar Organic Farming Research Centre’ has been established in Coimbatore in his honour. This centre undertakes research, training and demonstrations related to organic farming. Projects such as the National Mission on Natural Farming, the Organic Farming Development Scheme in the Nilgiris District, creation of model farms for organic farming, and complete exemption from registration fees for obtaining organic farming certificates are also being implemented. Under Nel Jayaraman’s Traditional Paddy Varieties Conservation Mission, 900 metric tonnes of seeds of traditional paddy varieties have been produced and distributed to 70,000 farmers. Seeds of traditional varieties of millets, pulses and traditional medicinal paddy varieties like Sivan samba have been produced and distributed.

items.text: Under Nel Jayaraman’s Traditional Paddy Varieties Conservation Mission, 900 metric tonnes of seeds of traditional paddy varieties have been produced and distributed to 70,000 farmers. Seeds of traditional varieties of millets, pulses and traditional medicinal paddy varieties like Sivan samba have been produced and distributed. The ‘Tamil Nadu Agroforestry Policy’ has been approved to promote agroforestry and will be released shortly. In order to enable the farmers to cultivate high - 6 value trees like Teak, Sandalwood, Red sanders, Mahogany etc., without apprehension, the policy provides for relaxation of rules on felling and transportation of felled trees, provision of necessary assistance for planting and maintenance, and formulation and implementation of schemes to promote Agroforestry. Mettur Dam was opened as per schedule for paddy cultivation in Kuruvai season for the past five years t o increase the area of paddy cultivation and to enhance the food grain production in the Cauvery Delta regions . Kuruvai Special Package Scheme was implemented at a cost of Rs.482 crore benefiting 19.51 lakh farmers. In the year 2025– 26, for the first time, a special package for paddy cultivation in the Kar/Kuruvai/Sornavari seasons was implemented in Non-Delta districts with an expenditure of Rs.115 crore. As a result, in the year 2025 –26, paddy is cultivated across 12.48 lakh acre across Tamil Nadu during the Kuruvai season reflecting an increase of 3 lakh acres compared to the previous year.

Guided by this principle, the scheme of m aking youth into Agri Entrepreneurs was implemented from 2021 -22 to 2024- 25 under which 456 young graduates were encouraged to establish Agriculture based enterprises with a subsidy of Rs.4.56 crore provided for this purpose. Moreover, with the objective of ensuring availability of inputs such as seeds, fertilizers, pesticides and technical adviso ry services to farmers in the vicinity of their villages, the Chief Ministers’ 1000 Farmers Service Centres Scheme has been recently launched by the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu. 8 30% subsidy ranging from Rs.3 lakh to Rs.6 lakh is extended to Agriculture, Horticulture, Agri-Engineering graduates and diploma holders for establishing the Farmers Service Centres.

With a view to strengthening nutritional security and improving public health through the promotion of traditional, nutrient -rich food practices, the Government has distributed 21 lakh nutrition kits at a total cost of Rs.21 crore during the period from 2021 –22 to 2024–25. Further, during 2025 –26, the Government has introduced the “Nutrition Farming Mission”. Under this initiative, 15 lakh vegetable seed kits, 9 lakh fruit kits and 1 lakh pulses seed kits have been distributed to a total of 25 lakh beneficiaries at a cost of Rs.19 crore. Because of this, vegetables and fruits are produced adequately thus avoiding shortage and ensuring nutritional security. Recognising the importance of fruits and vegetables in enhancing immunity and ensuring nutritional security, focused efforts are being undertaken for area expansion , promoting high-tech cultivation practices and mulching. Honourable Speaker! With the aim of increasing the production and consumption of millets that significan tly contribute to the 9 well-being of the people, Tamil Nadu Millet Mission is being implemented as a five year scheme from 2023- 24, and so far, 12.84 lakh farmers have been benefited with an expenditure of Rs. 178 crore. Millets have been cultivated in an area of 20 lakh acre. In addition, cluster demonstrations have been laid in an area of 3.36 lakh acre and 90 millet value addition centres have been established.

In addition, cluster demonstrations have been laid in an area of 3.36 lakh acre and 90 millet value addition centres have been established. As a result, at the national level, Tamil Nadu has ranked first in Ragi productivity, second in Ragi production and fifth in Minor millets production. The area under Cumbu cultivation area has increased from 1.18 lakh acre to 1.33 lakh acre. The Pulses Development Scheme has been implemented with an expenditure of Rs.174 crore in an area of 24 lakh acre benefitting 9.44 lakh farmers over the last five years, to achieve self -sufficiency in pulses and to ensure nutritional security. Redgram Area Expansion Mission and Transplanted Redgram Cultivation Scheme are being implemented to increase area under Redgram cultivation with an expenditure of Rs.6 6 crore covering 2.52 lakh acre s and benefitting 1.48 lakh farmers. 10 To achieve self -sufficiency in oilseed production, under the Oilseeds Mission, critical inputs and subsidies for advanced production technologies are being provided for the cultivation of oilseed crops such as Groundnut and Gingelly. Over the past five years, Oilseeds cultivation has been encouraged in 14 lakh acre with an allocation of Rs.229 crore benefitting 7.54 lakh farmers. Considering the heavy demand prevailing for Maize in Ethanol production and animal feed production, various scheme components have been implemented over the last five years to promote maize cultivation and enhance farmers’ income. An expenditure of Rs.7 8 crore has been incurred, benefiting 1.50 lakh farmers.

items.text: Considering the heavy demand prevailing for Maize in Ethanol production and animal feed production, various scheme components have been implemented over the last five years to promote maize cultivation and enhance farmers’ income. An expenditure of Rs.7 8 crore has been incurred, benefiting 1.50 lakh farmers. Consequently, the area under maize has increased from 10 lakh acres to 12 lakh acres and production has increased from 26 lakh MT to 27 lakh MT. To ensure timely farming operations and to address the shortage of agricultural labourers, a total of 77,499 agricultural machineries and implements have been provided to farmers. Further, 1,320 Custom Hiring Centres have also been established. A total subsidy of Rs.783 crore has been sanctioned in the past five years. It is pertinent note that, only 29,945 machineries and 11 implements were provided to farmers in the preceding five years. For ensuring uninterrupted power supply to farmers for irrigation through renewable energy, 4,150 Solar powered pumpsets have been installed with a subsidy assistance of Rs.8 3 crore. Further, 5,954 new electric motor pumpsets have been provided with a subsidy of Rs.7.67 crore. Further, 3,816 agricultural machinery and implements of the Agricultural Engineering Department are being hired out to farmers at Government fixed nominal hire charges through the “e- Vaadagai” mobile App. The fleet strength for hiring stood at only 1,265 machineries and implements during 2020 –21. The e-Vaadagai service has since been substantially strengthened through the procurement of a si gnificant number of additional machineries over the last five years.

The e-Vaadagai service has since been substantially strengthened through the procurement of a si gnificant number of additional machineries over the last five years. Honourable Speaker ! Realising the timeless wisdom of Thiruvalluvar that ”நிலத்ெதாடு நீர் இையந்து” land and water are intrinsically interconnected, the Government has undertaken concerted efforts to ensure adequate irrigation facilities for sustainable agriculture in Tamil Nadu. Accordingly, 12 2 lakh new free electricity connections have been provided to the farmers during the past five years. The Government has also sanctioned Rs.33,904 crore towards meeting the cost of providing f ree electricity to 23.86 lakh agricultural service connections. To enhance crop production through efficient use of irrigation water, the Micro Irrigation Scheme is being implemented with special focus. Under this scheme, 100 percent subsidy is provided to Small and Marginal farmers and 75 percent subsidy is provided to other farmers. Micro-irrigation systems have been installed in 5 lakh ha at a cost of Rs. 4,061 crore benefitting 5.13 lakh farmers in the past five years. Apart from opening t he Mettur Dam at scheduled times to fill the granaries with paddy grains by spreading a blanket of paddy panicles across Cauvery delta, desilting of ‘C’ and ‘D’ channels in Cauvery, Vennar and Vellar sub basins and Grand Anicut canal ayacut areas has been c arried out for a length of 8,371 km at a cost of Rs.33.77 crore in the past five years to ensure irrigation water to the tail end areas.

items.text: Through the Water Resources Department, 4,580 desilting works have been carried out in the dam ayacut areas at a cost of Rs.498 crore. 13 Watershed Development Programme is being implemented in seven districts viz., Perambalur, Thoothukudi, Dindigul, Krishnagiri, Ramanathapur am, Dharmapuri and Virudhunagar under which v arious natural resource management works are being carried in 357 watersheds covering an area of around 2 lakh ha out at an estimated cost of Rs.369 crore. I take pride in informing this august Assembly that as a result of these initiatives, an additional area of 3. 48 lakh ha has been brought under irrigation in Tamil Nadu. Horticultural crops such as vegetables, fruits, and spices generate higher income and enhance nutritional security even from smaller holdings . These are being widely promoted through various schemes such as Fruit Crops Promotion Programme , Jackfruit Mission, Moringa Mission, Chilli Zone, Onion Cultivation Mission, Curry Leaf Cluster, Area Expansion of Special Horticultural Crops and the Mukkani Development Scheme. The area of vegetable c rops like Tomato, Bhendi, Brinjal, Moringa has been expanded in an area of 1 lakh ha and permanent pandal structures have been erected in an area of 1,979 h a. A total subsidy of Rs.259 crore has been provided 1.68 lakh farmers. 14 For promoting fruit crops, area expansion of Mango, Jackfruit, Banana, Guava, and Papaya has been taken up in an area of 36,555 h a with a subsidy of Rs.72.47 crore benefiting 48,580 farmers.

To expand the cultivation of globally renowned, export-oriented spice crops such as Chilli, Turmeric, Pepper, Cardamom, Clove and Nutmeg, in an area of 22,980 ha, a subsidy assistance of Rs.32 crore has been provided to 29,855 farmers. To facilitate daily income to farmers, flower crops like Jasmine, Rose, Chrysanthemum , Marigold and Tuberose have been promoted with a subsidy of Rs.28 crore for area expansion in an area of 11,380 h a, benefiting 18,130 farmers. Protected cultivation components such as polyhouses and shadenet houses are being promoted to enable farmers to cultivate high -value horticultural crops like C apsicum and C arnation throughout the year under controlled conditions. Under this scheme, 1,756 farmers have been provided with a subsidy of Rs.91 crore to erect 23.55 lakh square meters of polyhouses and shadenet houses. 15 Considering the importance of cashew, an essential commercial crop of Tamil Nadu , 8,400 ha has been brought under cashew cultivation over the past five years at an outlay of Rs.1 2 crore, benefiting 9,687 farmers.

In order to reduce post -harvest losses, increase market value and improve the live lihood of farmers, 3,435 pack houses, 5 cold storages with a capacity of 8,218 MT, and onion storage structures with a capacity of 3.44 lakh MT have been established in the last five years at a cost of Rs.175 crore, benefiting 15,606 farmers. Coconut Development Coconut remains as the basis of livelihood of lakhs of farmers. Hence, t o enhance the production and productivity of coconut, various components such as Establishment of Regional Coconut Nurseries, Laying out of Demonstration Plots, Establishment of organic manure units, Replanting and Rejuvenation of Coconut gardens 16 have been implemented over the past five years in 17,860 ha at an outlay of Rs.54 crore, benefiting 26,800 farmers.

items.text: Under the Coconut Root Wilt Management Scheme, activities such as removal of diseased palms, free distribution of coconut seedlings and provision of inputs for rejuvenation of affected plantation have been carried out in 3,943 ha at a cost of Rs.18.48 crore during 2023 –24 and 2024–25 in Coimbatore, Tiruppur, Theni, Tenkasi and Kanyakumari districts benefiting 6,300 farmers. Moreover, advisories on technological interventions were provided to farmers through special campaigns due to which 17,816 ha of coconut area was revived from Coconut Root Wilt disease. Palmyra Development Considering the importance of Palmyrah , the State Tree of Tamil Nadu, Palmyra Development Mission is being implemented from 2021- 22 onwards . Under this scheme, over the past five years, 6 8 lakh palmyra seeds and 1.28 lakh seedlings have been distributed, 354 value- addition units have been established through the Department of Horticulture. 17 The Tamil Nadu Palm Products Development Board has provided 1, 350 individuals with training and equipments for production of palmyrah value -added products and also 650 women were provided with training and equipments for making palmyrah leaf products. This scheme has been implemented with an expenditure of Rs. 9.17 crore, benefiting 1.45 lakh beneficiaries. Further, a Common Facili tation Centre has been established for quality palm jaggery production at Veerapandiyapattinam in Thoothukudi district. In the past five years, Rs.80 crore worth palm products have been produced and sold.

Everything for Everyone The guiding principle of "Everything for Everyone" of the Government , aims to achieve inclusive growth . Accordingly, 70% subsidy is extended by the State Government for high -value components such as Integrated Farming System, Polyg reen houses, Shadenet houses, Agricultural mechanization, Value -addition machinery and Solar pump sets to the small and marginal farmers belonging to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe categories. Over the last four years, an additional subsidy amounting to Rs.62 crore has been extended , benefiting 17,340 Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe farmers across the State. 18 Borewells or tube wells along with electric motors or Solar powered pumpsets have been installed with 100 percent subsidy for 2,115 individual SC/ST farmers at an expenditure of Rs.122 Crore. items.text: A special incentive of Rs.156 per quintal for Grade A paddy and Rs.131 per quintal for Common paddy has been fixed for Kharif 2025 -2026 Marketing season. Accordingly, the procurement prices for Grade A and C ommon paddy have been i ncreased to Rs.2,545 and Rs. 2,500 respectively. In the last five years, 186 lakh metric tonne of paddy have been procured, and Rs.2,118 crore has been provided as incentive. Compared to 2020-21, the paddy procurement incentive has been increased by 123 percent for Grade A and 162 percent for common variety. 19 From the 2020-21 crop season, a special incentive is being provided for sugarcane in addition to the F air and Remunerative Price fixed by the Union Government. A special incentive of Rs.349 per MT of sugarcane has been announced for the 2024 –25 crushing season, thereby fixing the increased cane price at Rs.3,500 per MT. In the last five years, Rs.1,094 crore has been provided as incentive to 5.70 lakh sugarcane farmers. Apart from these, in order to protect farmers from income loss during periods of price fall, a total of 12,236 MT of Greengram, Black gram, and Red gram worth Rs.96.66 crore have been procured from 10,690 farmers at the Minimum Support Price (MSP). In addition, 1.47 lak h MT of Copra worth Rs. 1,600 crore have been procured from one lakh farmers at Minimum Support Price.

The Government extends steadfast support to safeguard farmers’ livelihoods whenever they suffer crop losses due to natural calamities. 20 Natural Calamity Relief During the last five years, an area of 184 lakh acre has been insured under the Crop Insurance scheme by enrolling about 80 lakh farmers and the Tamil Nadu Government has contributed Rs.6 073 crore as premium subsidy. S o far, under this scheme, an amount of Rs.6063 crore has been provided to 38 lakh farmers as compensation for crop yield loss. In Tamil Nadu , due to climate change, n atural disasters such as floods, cycl ones and droughts have become frequent . In order to safeguard the livelihoods of farmers affected by crop losses, an amount of Rs.2,045 crore has been provided over the last five years as relief assistance to 25.36 lakh farmers for Agricultural and Horticultural crop damages caused in an area of 16.20 lakh ha. Besides this, 3,765 acres of agricultural fields affected by sand deposits due to flooding by heavy downpour in Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Tenkasi Districts during the year 2023 -24 were removed by the Agricultural Engineering Department with an expenditure of Rs.6 crore benefiting 2,580 farmers.

items.text: 21 Agri Exhibitions and Seminars In accordance with the guidance of the Honourable Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Agricultural Exhibitions and Seminars were conducted at three locations, Tiruchirapalli, Perundurai in Erode district, and Tiruvannamalai and the Agribusiness Expo was organized twice at the Nandambakkam Trade Centre in Chennai. Modern technologies, innovations, agricultural machinery and tools, post -harvest management techniques, value -addition methods, and livestock and fish farming technologies were showcased. Approximately, 9 lakh farmers, students and members of the general public visited these exhibitions and benefited . In these expos, a gricultural produce and value added products worth around Rs.7 crore was sold by Farmer Producer Companies, entrepreneurs. During the last five years, a maximum of 137 lakh MT of agricultural produce has been transacted in the Regulated Markets. Infrastructure facilities including 69 storage Godowns with a total capacity of 75,500 metric tonnes, 78 drying yards, buildings for 28 regulated markets in the regulated markets and drying yard with grading and sorting facilities in the villages have been established at a total cost of 22 Rs.368 crore. Additionally, a new regulated market has been established at Alangulam in Tenkasi district and a Turmeric Export Centre has been set up in Erode district at a cost of Rs.15 crore. Further, infrastructure facilities in 200 Regulated Markets have been upgraded at an estimated cost of Rs. 97.30 crore benefiting approximately 3.57 lakh farmers. Agriculture is the primary occupation of the majority of the rural population and also 2 2 determines their livelihood. Agriculture plays a major role in the country’s food sec urity, economic growth, environmental protection, people’s standard of living and serve s as the backbone in determining the progress and development of the nation. Origin of the Agriculture and Allied Departments In 1863, the then Governor of the Madras Presidency, Sir William Denison, submitted a memorandum on agricultural practices to his Council. This initiative laid the foundation for a sustained advancement in agriculture and facilitated the adoption of development works. Based on the recommendations of the Indian Famine Commission in 1880, the Agriculture Department was established in the year 1882. Subsequently, it was reorganised as the Commissionerate of Revenue Settlement, Land 3 Records and Agriculture and in 1905, it was reconstituted as an indepe ndent department under the auspices of Director of Agriculture. In the initial years, the Department functioned under the Revenue Department at the Secretariat level, and later under the Planning and Development Department. Subsequently, the Agriculture Department was newly constituted, and its administration was brought under the control of the Secretary to Government.

items.text: In the initial years, the Department functioned under the Revenue Department at the Secretariat level, and later under the Planning and Development Department. Subsequently, the Agriculture Department was newly constituted, and its administration was brought under the control of the Secretary to Government. Over the years, the Department of sugars (1969), Department of Agricultural Marketing and Agri Business (1977–78), Department of Horticultu re and Plantation Crops (1979–80), Department of Seed Certification and Organic Certification (1979–80), and the Agricultural Engineering Department (1980–81) were carved out from the Agriculture Department separately. In 2022, the headquarters of the Seed Certification and Organic Certification Department 4 4 was shifted from Coimbatore to Chennai. In the same year, the Sugar Department was merged once again with the Agriculture - Farmers Welfare Department. Further, the Tamil Nadu Food Processing and Agri Export Promotion Corporation was separated from the Department of Agricultural Marketing and Agri -Business (since 2022) and transferred to the Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. Further, the State's first Agricultural College was started at Saidapet, Chennai, in 1876. Later, the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) was established at Coimbatore in 1971. Thus, the several specialised departments formed out of Agriculture – Farmers Welfare department have provided a strong institutional framework for agricultural growth in Tamil Nadu.

items.text: With the ambitious objective of advancing agriculture and improving farmers ’ welfare, the Government of Tamil Nadu is taking earnest efforts to in crease the agricultural production, enhance farmers income and thereby improving their livelihood through various schemes of Agriculture-Farmers Welfare Department. The Agriculture – Farmers Welfare Department is implementing a plethora of ingenious schem es based on agricultural 6 6 strategies such as, soil health management for restoring the fertil ity of mother soil given by nature, distribution of certified seeds that are the foundation of enhanced productivity to farmers , provision of irrigation water requi red for cultivation; the continuous supply of three -phase electricity required for agriculture; promoting high-yielding varieties and hybrid s as per the requirements of farmers, promoting alternate crop cultivation for water management; food and nutritional security, promoting organic farming and natural farming for preserving soil health, integrated crop management for high productivity, Micro-irrigation for conserving water and cultivate multi crops, agroforestry for climate change and environmental mana gement; agricultural mechanization to overcome labour shortages during cultivation season; value addition to supply agricultural produce without wastage and generate income; and food processing for future use. 7 Based on the principle of “Leave No One Behind” set by the United Nations , various programmes are being implemented worldwide to bring about positive changes and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. Special Scheme for providing subsidy for Paddy Seed Production and Distribution To ensure uninterrupted supply and availability of quality Paddy seeds to farmers, a Special Scheme for Paddy Seed Production and Distribution will be implemented with State fund during 2026-27. Under this scheme , it is planned to distribute 14,570 MT of certified seeds of less than 10 year and more than 10 year old Paddy varieties to farmers. By implementing this scheme, the usage of certified seeds gets 25 increased and thereby the Seed Replacement Rate is also increased. Further, the high yielding Paddy varieties will be extensively cultivated and the Paddy production and productivity of the State will be enhanced. An incentive of Rs.8 per kg will be provided to seed ryots who establish seed farms in their fields and provide the certified seeds produced to the Tamil Nadu Seed Development Agency (TANSEDA).

In Tamil Nadu, Oilseed crops are normally cultivated in an area of 4.06 lakh hectare, with an annual production of about 9. 28 lakh MT and average yield of 2,284 kg /ha. During 2026 –27, a n amount of Rs.132.11 crore has been allocated to implement the “National Mission on Edible Oils – Oilseeds” scheme across 66,850 hectare in 26 distri cts. The mission aims to achieve self - sufficiency in edible oil production by increasing domestic edible oil production, reducing edible oil 44 44 imports and conserving foreign exchange, and enhancing farmers’ income. Under the Mission, assistance is provided for Oilseed cultivation through the distribution of high-yielding and improved varieties under Value Chain Clusters, supply of seeds and other critical inputs for Block Demonstrations, and support for certified seed production. In addition, financial assistance is extended to Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), co -operatives and industry stakeholders for the establishment and upgradation of post -harvest infrastructure, thereby improving processing efficiency and enhancing oil recovery from Oilseeds. Alternate crop cultivation scheme will be implemented at an outlay of Rs.12.50 crore to mitigate crop damage s caused by climatic changes to improve soil health, and promote the cultivation of Pulses and Oilseeds as an alternative to Paddy crop. 45 1.3.5.

items.text: 1.4. Digital Agriculture The Department of Agriculture is stepping up Digital Agriculture through AI (Artificial Intelligence), Machine Learning, and farmer-centric digital platforms. The Uzhavar App provides 24 essential services, benefiting over 20 lakh farmers with weather advisories, market prices, input availab ility, AI based pest and disease diagnosis, scheme information. AgriStack forms the foundation of digital agriculture through the Farmer Registry (FR), Digital Crop Survey (DCS) and geo -referenced land records. items.text: Annually, on an average, a target of about 31,040 samples is fixed for fertilizer testing. Based on the deficiencies identified during laboratory testing, appropriate departmental and legal action as per rules in vogue are being taken against the concerned manufacturers. 59 Similarly, during 2026–27, it has been targeted to collect and test 31,040 fertilizer samples for quality standards. 1.8. Laboratories There are 37 Soil testing Laboratories and 22 Mobile Soil Testing Laboratories functioning in Department of Agriculture to encourage farmers to cultivate crops in accordance to the soil fertility, reduce the use of fertilizers and enhance the soil fertility and to create awareness through the distribution of Soil Health Cards with fertilizer recommendations. Emphasis is being given to achieve sustainable horticultural development through the promotion of micro -irrigation for efficient water use, 104  104 adoption of modern cultivation technologies, expansion of high -density cultivation, effective pest and disease manageme nt, post - harvest management and cold storage facilities. Further, the continuous availability of quality planting materials is essential for achieving higher productivity. To ensure this, action is being taken to produce high quality grafted plants, quality seeds and disease resistant planting materials to farmers, through the State Horticulture Farms and provide farmers with continuous supply. Accordingly, the Government’s primary objective is to adopt an integrated approach that focuses on improving farm ers’ livelihoods, ensuring nutritional security and contributing to the overall economic growth of the State. Agricultural Marketing and Agri Business Agricultural marketing is the foundation of profitable agriculture. It serves as a vital bridge connecting production with markets, enabling farmers to obtain a fair and profitable price for their produce. The su ccess of agriculture depends not only on increasing production but also on farmers’ ability to sell their produce at right place, at right time and at fair price. Efficient agricultural marketing brings transparency to price determination, reduces post -harvest losses, promotes value addition and increases the farmers’ share paid by consumers. Recognizing this importance, the Government of Tamil Nadu has develop ed infrastructure such as Uzhavar Sandhais, regulated markets, primary processing centres, cold st orage facilities, food parks and export-oriented infrastructure to improve farmers’ access to markets and ensure higher incomes. 179 The importance of agricultural marketing has been emphasized even in ancient Tamil literature. The world -renowned Tamil classic , Thirukkural, highlights that agriculture and trade served as the foundations of society.

Here, farmers participate in the closed bidding and obtain better prices for their produce. At Regulated Markets, farmers receive a fair price as their produce is a ccurately weighed and prices are determined according to quality. No fee is collected from farmers for this service. items.text: Accordingly, out of the 194 Uzhavar Sandhais currently functioning in Tamil Nadu, 93 Uzhavar Sandhais have obtained 194 194 certification from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). To ensure that the prices of produce sold by farmers in Uzhavar Sandhais are higher than the wholesale market prices while remaining lower than the retail prices for consumers, daily prices are fixed for vegetables and fruits. To make these prices transparent to everyone, electronic price display boards have been installed in 50 Uzhavar Sandhais. During the current year, electronic price display boards will be installed in another 59 Uzhavar Sandhais at a cost of Rs. 2.04 crore. In Uzhavar Sandhais, an average of 8,200 farmers sell around 2,500 metric tonnes of vegetables and fruits worth Rs.11 crore per day to 3 lakh consumers . The daily price details of commodities sold at Uzhavar Sandhais are made available to the public through the ‘Uzhavar’ mobile applicatio n and the website of the 195 Department of Agricultural Marketing and Agri Business: www.agrimark.tn.gov.in. items.text: Pack houses are functioning at five locations viz., Pochampalli, Hosur, Sulur, Chinnamanur and M. Puthur. ii) Gamma Irradiation Unit: It is functioning at the Pochampalli Primary Processing Centre . Under a service -fee-based model, 320 metric tones of products, including chilli, turmeric powder, papad, coriander, fenugreek, mustard, finger millet flour, moringa leaf powder, lactose powder, tea bags, groundnuts, cashews, and jaggery, have been processed and supplied. 209 iii) Individually Quick Freezing (IQF) Unit : It is functioning at the Pochampalli Primary Processing Centre . items.text: For loans of up to Rs.2 crore , interest subvention at 3 percent per annum and credit guarantee are provided for a period of seven years . The loa n component of other capital subsidy schemes can also be converged with this scheme to avail the benefits. 5.2.5.AGMARK Grading Scheme The quality and purity of agricultural and food products are ensured through appropriate testing, following which the AGMARK certification is issued by the Government. Since samples are collected and tested at the place of production 217 itself, adulteration is prevented and safe food products are made available to consumers. This also creates opportunities for farmers to obtain better market prices for their produce. The Department of Agricultural Marketing and Agri Business, Tamil Nadu , in collaboration with the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI), Government of India , is implementing the AGMARK Grading Scheme through 30 State AGMARK Quality Control Laboratories and one principal Laboratory at the State headquarters. The scheme has statutory recognition under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937 (amended in 1986) and provides quality specifications for 248 agricultural commodities. In Tamil Nadu, grading is currently carried out for 26 agricultural commodities , including ghee, edible oils, cereals, pulses, honey, whole and ground spices, butter, tamarind, health-mix flour, asafoetida, and others. 217 216 5.2.4.Providing Financial Assistance under Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) scheme Under the Union Government’s Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) Scheme, credit assistance is being provided to farmers, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), agricultural entrepreneurs, and Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Societies (PACS) for creating agricultural infrastructure.

items.text: Quality seed plays a vital role in enhancing agricultural productivity and improving farmers’ livelihoods. The use of high -quality certified seeds with assured genetic purity, germination capacity and physical purity is essential for achieving higher crop yields, increasing farm income and promoting sustainable agricultural development. 256 256 The functioning of the Department is guided by three major pillars —Assurance, Availability and Affordability. The Department implements various programmes in Seed Certification, Seed Quality Control, Seed Testing and Organic Certification to ensure the timely supply of quality seeds and organic produce. Through Seed inspection, testing, certification and regulatory measures, it ensures the quality, purity and reliability of seeds and organic produce while supporting farmers and stakeholders with dependable certificat ion services. 7.1. Seed Certification The Seed Certification wing operates within the framework of The Seeds Act, 1966, The Seeds Rules, 1968 and Seeds (Control) Order, 1983. It undertakes the certification of notified crop varieties in strict conformity w ith the Indian Minimum Seed Certification Standards (IMSCS). 257 Seed farms established by Government agencies and private seed producers undergo a series of systematic certification activities, including verification of seed source, field inspections, seed pr ocessing operations, seed quality testing and affixing certification tags to seed lots, thereby ensuring the supply of quality certified seeds to the farming community. Breeder seed plots established in Agricultural Research Stations are inspected by the B reeder Seed monitoring Team comprising an Assistant Director of Seed Certification as one of the members to ensure compliance with the prescribed field standards and maintenance of Genetic Purity. Every year, on an average, seed farms covering 68,000 hect ares are registered, and 1,25,000 metric tonnes of quality seeds are certified.

Organic Certification 7.4.1 Scope and Functions The Tamil Nadu Organic Certification Department was established by the Government of Tamil Nadu in the year 2007 as a certification body for organic farming systems. The Department is accredited by the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry for certification under the National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP). This Department is authorised to offer certification for organic crop production, processing and trading activit ies intended for export under this scheme and issues Scope Certificates to Organic farmers, Processors 270 270 and traders. The certification standards followed by the Department are equivalent to the standards prescribed by the European Union and the Swiss Organi c Farming Ordinance. The NPOP certification system facilitates marketing of organic produce both within India and abroad. Organic farming standards ensure avoidance of synthetic inputs like chemical fertilisers, pesticides, weedicides and genetically modi fied seeds. Further, the Department has also been authorised by the National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare for implementation of the Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) -India Organic and Parti cipatory Guarantee System (PGS)-Natural Farming. The PGS system functions on the principles of participation, transparency, shared vision, trust and horizontality. Through these certification systems, organic farmers are 271 enabled to market their produce in domestic markets.

Farmers sustain everyone engaged in professions other than farming, making them the very linchpin, the essential axis, upon which the world revolves. The 'Emperor of Poets' Kambar declared, "The entire world shines because of the ploughing by farmers," while the illustrious poetess Avvaiyar celebrated the virtue of the profession, stating, "There is no life comparable to living by the plough" and "Farming is always the Best." I offer my humble greetings to the Hon ’ble Chief Minister, who aspires to making Tamil Nadu a state that the world admires and a land that shines with success. I also pay tribute to the farmers who propel Tamil Nadu 2 forward in the path of success by transforming the thorns into flowers and the stones into fruits. items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: Born in Thanjavur, fondly known as the Granary of Tamil Nadu, I was nurtured in the fertile Cauvery delta, surrounded by lush fields and winding irrigation canals. My hunger was simply satiated by my mother’s loving meal. I offer my heartfelt gratitude to the Hon ’ble Chief Minister for entrusting me with the significant responsibility of serving as the Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, a role that allows me to stand in support of the very farmers who provided that sustenance. It gives me immense pleasure to present my maiden Agriculture Budget before this august House, marking the first step toward creating a “Glorious Tamil Nadu” driven by successful farmers. The Evolution of Agriculture in Tamil Nadu In Tamil Nadu, d uring the Sangam era, agriculture was practiced primarily for subsistence . F orests were cleared to establish settlements and ponds were excavated to enhance prosperity. Following India's independence, a strong foundation for modern agriculture was laid in the 1950 ’s through the expansion of irrigation facilities, land reforms, community development 3 programmes and agricultural research and extension services. The 'Green Revolution' era from 1960 to 1980 resulted in a shift towards food security, supported by the use of high -yielding varieties, fertilizers and pesticides alongside irrigation expansion, agricultural credit and government procurement policies. In the 1980’ s, agriculture moved towards mechanization and the cultivation of cash crops. The 2000 ’s saw the emergence of efficiency based and market-led agriculture with the introduction of precision farming, micro irrigation, protected cultivation, value addition and agricultural market reforms.

items.text: In the 1980’ s, agriculture moved towards mechanization and the cultivation of cash crops. The 2000 ’s saw the emergence of efficiency based and market-led agriculture with the introduction of precision farming, micro irrigation, protected cultivation, value addition and agricultural market reforms. In the 2010 ’s, agriculture was reshaped to address climate change challenges by prioritizing integrated farming, natural resource conservation, water use efficiency, soil health management, solar powered pumps, and Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs). Since 2021, AI-based advisory services, data-driven management and Uzhavar mobile application have provided agriculture with a new dimension. In essence, the sector has evolved from subsistence farming to science-based agriculture; from a focus solely on food security to one centred on farmer prosperity , and from 4 traditional methods to sustainable agriculture driven by technology, data and innovation. These transformations demonstrate the eagerness of Tamil Nadu farmers in embracing progressive changes. We have the evidence t hat entire Tamil Nadu has craved for change. Recognizing the importance of farmers, and the plethora of sectors involved in agricultural activities, the Hon’ble Chief Minister directed to continue the practice of presenting a separate budget for Agriculture. Agriculture is the sector that faces the greatest challenges among all industries. Farmers grapple with issues such as the unpredictable vagaries of monsoon , labour shortages, decline in soil health and water resources and high production costs. Despit e their commitment to feeding the world and ensuring food security, the failure to secure fair prices for their produce often makes them contemplate leaving the agriculture profession altogether. Therefore, this government is steadfast in its commitment to safeguarding both agriculture and the welfare of farmers.

items.text: Despit e their commitment to feeding the world and ensuring food security, the failure to secure fair prices for their produce often makes them contemplate leaving the agriculture profession altogether. Therefore, this government is steadfast in its commitment to safeguarding both agriculture and the welfare of farmers. Moving beyond empty promises to 5 concrete action , and guided by the Hon’ ble Chief Minister’s pronouncement that "A triumphant Tamil Nadu can only be built on the prosperity of its farmers "—we, the Ministers, Members of Parliament, Members of the Legislative Assembly and officials of the Agriculture - Farmers Welfare Department visited Salem, Thanjavur, Vellore, Tirunelveli and Chennai to have consultations with farmers. At each of these regional consultations, we deliberated extensively with farmers, representatives of farmers' associations, traders, agri -entrepreneurs, exporters etc., from the surrounding districts. I wish to inform this august House that this agricultural budget has been prepared by incorporating the suggestions and requests gathered during these consultations. In strict alignment with the Hon’ble Chief Minister’s principle that "before a government becomes a superpower, it must transform into a government for farmers", the agriculture budget for the year 2026-27 has been prepared with numerous pioneering schemes designed to meet farmers' needs to the extent possible, align with scientific advancements in agriculture and ensure their prosperity by enabling them to secur e fair prices for their produce. 6 The Hon'ble Chief Minister has formulated many excellent visionary schemes to be implemented by the department on priority basis in the next five years to improve the livelihood of the farmers .

items.text: 6 The Hon'ble Chief Minister has formulated many excellent visionary schemes to be implemented by the department on priority basis in the next five years to improve the livelihood of the farmers . From among them, schemes related to farmer s’ welfare, income enhancement, augmentation and conservation of water resources, safeguarding the produce, value addition, agricultural research, strengthening of farmer producer organizations, irrigation management, organic farming, agribusiness, etc. have been prioritized and included in this agriculture budget. To achieve this, the ongoing projects preferred by the farmers will be continued and several new initiatives will be introduced. "If agriculture goes wrong, nothing else will have a chance to go right." As insisted upon by the agricultural scientist Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, the department has started to work for farmers and for increasing agricultural production even before the preparation of the Agriculture Budget, as per the directions of the Hon’ble Chief Minister. 7 “To help every farmer prosper, irrigation water must reach the furthest tail-end areas”. Driven by this vision, 2,509 km of 'C' and 'D' irrigation channels in the Delta districts were desilted this year at a cost of Rs.10 crore. Due to inadequate storage in Mettur Dam, it could not be opened for irrigation on the scheduled date of 12 th June. To reaffirm that "even if the rains fail, our government, committed to the welfare of farmers, will not fail them," the Hon’ble Chief Minister announced the Kuruvai Package with an outlay of Rs.134.83 crore for both delta and non- delta districts .

items.text: Furthermore, the Hon’ble Chief Minister is continuously monitoring the scheme's proper implementation through review meetings. As a result, Kuruvai cultivation has been undertaken in an area of 8.26 lakh acres so far. In pursuance of the Government's long -term vision to bring 100 per cent of the cultivated area under crop insurance , the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) will be implemented during 2026–27 in 14 clusters comprising of 37 districts, covering all notified crops during the Kuruvai, Samba, and Rabi seasons for which an amount of Rs.648.55 crore has 8 been allocated from the State fund. This initiative will provide insurance coverage to 36 lakh acres of cultivated area, benefitting 15 lakh farmers . Further, adequate additional funds will be provided to facilitate the enrolment of all eligible farmers who voluntarily join the scheme. "While it is the sky that blesses the farmers, at times, it is that very same sky that brings them adversity.” Owing to the 'Super El Nino' phenomenon in the current year, severe climatic impacts are anticipated across the country, particularly during the Kuruvai season. It has been predicted that 12 districts in Tamil Nadu will experience a severe impact. Hence, the “District Agricultural Contingency Plan” prepared by the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University for all districts have been communicated to the District Collectors, and all steps have been taken up to implement the contingency measures indicated thereon holistically.

items.text: Hence, the “District Agricultural Contingency Plan” prepared by the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University for all districts have been communicated to the District Collectors, and all steps have been taken up to implement the contingency measures indicated thereon holistically. Farmers suffered significant losses this year, just as they did last year, due to the lack of remunerative prices for mangoes, specifically the ‘Banglora’ variety. To address this, a formal proposal was submitted to the Union 9 Government seeking approval to provide a price deficiency payment for this variety under the Market Intervention Scheme and the approval was secured for the first time. By the time the scheme's guidelines were finalized and operations were commenced, the harvest season for the Banglora variety had come to an end resulting in the procurement of only 6 metric tonnes. The Agriculture -Farmers Welfare Department is now fully prepared to swiftly address similar situations in the future, as the operational procedures have been completely established. To ensure the food security for the of people, a target of 131 lakh metric tonnes of food grains has been set to be achieved in five years . During 2026-27, it has been targeted to achie ve 125 lakh metric tonnes. Apart from this, targets have been set to increase the production of nutritious pulses, vegetables and fruits to achieve self -sufficiency and also nutritional security. All measures will be taken to achieve these goals by implementing suitable schemes. As this government’s prime vision is to increase the irrigated area by creating irrigation sources like farm ponds and borewells, about 2,600 acres of rainfed lands 10 will receive irrigation.

As this government’s prime vision is to increase the irrigated area by creating irrigation sources like farm ponds and borewells, about 2,600 acres of rainfed lands 10 will receive irrigation. Besides, by increasing irrigation water use efficiency through micro -irrigation systems, an additional 50,000 acres will be provided with irrigation. Our Hon'ble Chief Minister has expressed his wish to be born into a farming family in his next life. However, he already stands as a son of every farming household in Tamil Nadu. That is why, he has directed that the supply of three -phase free electricity to the farmers shall continue without interruption to enable the farmers to carry out their cultivation activities without any hindrance. Accordingly, d uring 2026- 27, an amount of Rs.7432.58 crore will be disbursed to the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation towards providing free electricity connection to farmers. To compensate for the loss of revenue caused by natural calamities, the government will continue to implement measures to ensure the livelihood of affected farmers by providing crop insurance compensation and relief for crop damage during natural calamities. Hon’ble Speaker! Above all, as advised by the Hon’ble Chief Minister, a Tamil leader who is the embodiment of both integrity 11 and fiery spirit , full focus will be given for ensuring transparency, accountability and fairness in the implementation of all schemes so that their full benefits reach the farmers and a desirable change will be brought about.

He then cross-ploughed it repeatedly, puddling the earth into a fine slurry. Time and again the field was tilled, its clods crushed, its soil compacted, and its bunds 12 carefully raised and strengthened. The land was meticulously levelled to retain water, the sluices were adjusted for proper irrigation, and only after incorporating green manure, Kol inji into the soil, were the choicest fragrant paddy seeds brought forth, sown with care, and nurtured into a thriving nursery." If the mere act of preparing the nursery involves so many tasks, we can imagine the multitude of operations required to cultivate a crop fully, harvest it, and sell the produce for realising income.

items.text: The Department of Agriculture implements various schemes to ensure the timely availability of new technologies, advisories , and quality inputs to farmers and handholding the m throughout to enhance agricultural production. 1. Tamil Nadu Soil Fertility Mission Conservation of soil, the fundamental resource for agriculture, is indispensable for ensuring sustainable food production and sustainable agriculture. Earthworms are called the farmers' friends. They help channel rainwater into the soil through the burrows they create. Therefore, it is imperative to improve the soil fertility for the earthworms to thrive. 13 Tamil Nadu has diverse soil types, comprising Red Soil, Red Loamy Soil, Black Soil, Grey Soil, Alluvial Soil and other soil types. Similar to how crops are specific to certain soils; each crop has its own ideal soil. Continuous use of chemical fertilizers, poor crop residue management, and improper biomass recycling will reduce soil organic carbon, harming soil health and crop productivity. Hence, by resorting to activities like increasing the population of soil microorganisms, reclaiming Alkaline & Saline soils, reducing the use of chemical fertilizers, and encouraging natural & organic farming practices, the Tamil Nadu Soil Fertility Mission will be launched as a five -year plan at an estimated outlay of Rs.600 crore, to ensure that future generations inherit fertile Tamil soils. i. To encourage the balanced use of fertilizers based on the soil fertility status, Soil Health Cards will be distributed to one lakh farmers with an allocation of Rs.4 crore from state fu nds.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: To encourage the balanced use of fertilizers based on the soil fertility status, Soil Health Cards will be distributed to one lakh farmers with an allocation of Rs.4 crore from state fu nds. Additionally, Soil Health Cards will be provided to about 3 lakh farmers who have obtained Farmer Identification Number (FID) at a total outlay of Rs.6.16 crore with the Union and State Government funds. 14 ii. To restore the soil fertility, seeds of green manures such as Sunn hemp, Daincha, Kolinji etc., required for covering 1 lakh acres and multi -grain crop seeds required for 22,000 acres will be distributed to farmers at subsidized cost. Further, an amount of Rs.3,000/ - per acre will be provided as ploughing subsidy for incorporation of well grown green manure crops into the soil. A sum of Rs.63.50 crore will be allocated from the state fund for this purpose. iii. To increase the population of microorganisms protecting the soil fertility and reduce the usage of inorganic fertilizers, liquid bio -fertilizers for an area of one lakh acre at a cost of Rs.4.50 crore and Water-soluble fertilizers to improve the fertilizer use efficiency, Crop boosters viz., ‘ Cotton Plus ’ for Cotton, ‘Sugarcane Booster ’ for Sugarcane to increase the crop productivity and ‘ Rice Bloom ’ to augment flowering in Paddy will be distributed at a cost of Rs.12.38 crore. iv.

items.text: With an aim to extend organic farming across the State, a special scheme of the State to provide an incentive of Rs.4,000/ - per acre to farmers 15 practicing organic farming will be implemented during 2026-27 to cover an area of 20,000 acre for which an amount of Rs.8 crore will be allocated from the state fund. In addition, a total amount of Rs.9.12 crore will be allocated from Union and State Government funds during 2026 -27 to form Organic Farming Clusters covering 7,500 acre by mobilizing farmers practicing organic farming under the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) Scheme and to form new Natural Farming Clusters in an area of 3,125 acres besides continuing with the second- year activities of Natural Farming Clusters in an area of 7,500 acre to produce safe and chemical-free food by improving the soil health through Natural Farming under the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF). v. To promote organic farming, a sum of Rs.10 crore will be allocated for establishing permanent Vermicompost production units. vi. Farmers registering newly under the National Organic Production Programme (NPOP) will be exempted from the payment of registration fees and renewal fees during the conversion period and 16 organic “Scope certificate” will be provided at free of cost to the organic farmers. Last year, the payment exemption was given only to newly registered farmers. However, this year, the exemption will be extended for renewal fees during the conversion period so as to encourage farmers to practice organic farming continuously. vii.

items.text: Last year, the payment exemption was given only to newly registered farmers. However, this year, the exemption will be extended for renewal fees during the conversion period so as to encourage farmers to practice organic farming continuously. vii. To ensure the quality of organic produce certified under the National Programme for Organic Production, a 100 per cent subsidy will be extended for undertaking Pesticide Resid ue Analysis. This initiative aims to identify pesticide residues, enabling farmers to command better prices in both domestic and export markets while providing residue-free commodities to consumers . An amount of Rs.25 lakh will be provided from the state fund. viii. To reclaim Alkali and Saline soils, demonstrations on soil amendment will be laid in 2,000 acres at an outlay of Rs.2 crore. 17 ix. Awareness and publicity activities will be taken up at a cost of Rs.2 crore to disseminate soil health improvement technologies to the farmers. x. To combat the impact of climatic changes , farmers adopting Direct Seeded Rice (DSR), Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) method of irrigation, application of slow -release fertilizers and thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions by about 50 per cent and promoting carbon sequestration in soils will be encouraged to obtain additional income through carbon trading for which an amount of Rs.60 lakh will be allocated from the state fund to conduct demonstrations in 2,000 acres and develop monitoring & verification protocols. During 2026 -27, the Tamil Nadu Soil Fertility Mission will be implemented with 10 components at a total outlay of Rs.122.51 crore. 2.

items.text: During 2026 -27, the Tamil Nadu Soil Fertility Mission will be implemented with 10 components at a total outlay of Rs.122.51 crore. 2. Special Scheme for providing subsidy for Paddy Seed Production and Distribution The Government is committed to ensure timely availability of adequate agricultural inputs to farmers 18 during every cropping season. Albeit , the production and distribution of quality seeds play a pivotal role in enhancing paddy productivity and production, the Government of India has discontinued the subsidy for paddy seed production and distribution from 2026 –27. However, the Hon'ble Chief Minister has considered the farmers requests for seed subsidy with a compassionate heart and keeping their welfare in mind. As per the Hon’ble Chief Minister’s directions, the State Government will continue to extend support by providing “Paddy Seed Production Subsidy” to farmers who register seed farms to produce 7,730 metric tonnes of certified paddy seeds, and supply them to the Tamil Nadu State Seed Development Agency. Further, “Paddy Seed Distribution Subsidy” will be provided for the distribution of 14,570 metric tonnes of certified paddy seeds at subsidised rates. During 2026 -27, an amount of Rs.34.72 crore will be allocated from the state funds to implement this scheme. 3. Uzhavar Artificial Intelligence (AI) Scheme Recognising that timely information is as vital to farmers as timely rainfall , the Government has announced a visionary scheme leveraging Artificial Intelligence to provide farmers with real -time information 19 on soil health and crop cultivation.

items.text: 3. Uzhavar Artificial Intelligence (AI) Scheme Recognising that timely information is as vital to farmers as timely rainfall , the Government has announced a visionary scheme leveraging Artificial Intelligence to provide farmers with real -time information 19 on soil health and crop cultivation. Accordingly, by integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies, comprehensive technical advisories and services related to weather forecasts, soil health and soil fertility management, pest and disease management and crop recommendations suited to prevailing agro climatic conditions covering the entire crop cycle from sowing to harvest will be provided. In addition, Farmers can easily access knowledge -based agricultural services including market intelligence, Voice -First Agriculture Services, information on Government schemes seamlessly through their mobile phones. During 2026–27, an am ount of Rs.2 crore will be allocated from the State funds towards the implementation of the Uzhavar Artificial Intelligence (AI) Scheme. 4. Mission for Self-Sufficiency in Pulses and Oilseed Crops In order to achieve self-sufficiency in the production of Pulses and edible Oilseeds by increasing the area under cultivation in Tamil Nadu in the next five years, the Mission for Self- Sufficiency in Pulses and Edible Oilseeds will be implemented with a total outlay of 20 Rs.203.64 crore out of which Rs.65.28 crore wi ll be allocated for Pulses and Rs.138.36 crore for edible Oilseeds, from the Union and State Government funds.

items.text: Under this Mission, it has been planned to increase the area of Pulses including Black gram, Red gram, Green gram and Cowpea from 15.19 lakh acre to 24.70 lakh acre and production from 3.88 lakh metric tonnes to 7.72 lakh metric tonnes. Similarly, it has been planned to increase the area of edible Oilseeds such as Groundnut, Sesame, Sunflower and Castor from 9.26 lakh acre to 14.89 lakh acre and p roduction from 8.77 lakh metric tonnes to 16.14 lakh metric tonnes. 5. Tamil Nadu Millet Mission Rich in nutrients and medicinal values, Millets are increasingly becoming a part of daily diets in both households and restaurants. Keeping in pace with the growing demand, the Tamil Nadu Millet Mission is being implemented with the objective of increasing the area, production and productivity of millets such as Pearl Millet (Cumbu), Sorghum (Cholam) and Finger Millet (Ragi). During 2026 –27, the Mission will be imp lemented at a total outlay of Rs.63.81 crore from the Union and State Government funds, covering interventions such as 21 the formation of Farmer Groups, alternate crop cultivation package subsidy, distribution of minikits, establishment of Agricultural Machinery Hiring Centres and Primary Processing Centres. About 4.75 lakh farmers cultivating millets in an extent of 11.80 lakh acre will be benefitted by this Mission. 6.

items.text: About 4.75 lakh farmers cultivating millets in an extent of 11.80 lakh acre will be benefitted by this Mission. 6. Tamil Nadu Minor Millet Mission Drought-tolerant, low water consuming, and nutrient & fibre-rich minor millets such as little millet, foxtail millet, kodo millet, barnyard millet, and proso millet are presently cultivated in an area of 61,750 acres in Tamil Nadu. With an objective of doubling the area under minor millets, the Tamil Nadu Minor Millet Mission will be implemented in 29 districts during 2026–27 at an outlay of Rs.7.61 crore allocated from the state fund. 7. Introduction of Nutrient-Rich Quinoa, Buckwheat and Brown Top Millet With a view to introduce cereals such as Quinoa, Buckwheat and Brown Top Millet, which are rich in protein, dietary fibre, Calcium, Potassium, Iron and Vitamins, low in gluten content and having less glycaemic 22 index in Tamil Nadu, demonstration plots will be laid at an outlay of Rs.30 lakh from the state fund in Nilgiris, Dindigul, Krishnagiri, Salem districts which are agro-climatically suitable for cultivation of these cereals. 8. Cotton Renaissance Mission Tamil Nadu plays a pivotal role in the growth of the country's textile and apparel sector, accounting for 46 pe r cent of India's total spinning capacity, 22 per cent of its power loom capacity, 12 per cent of its handloom capacity and 70 per cent of Cotton knitwear production.

items.text: C otton, known as 'White Gold' and called the 'King of Fibre is cultivated on an average in an area of about 3.14 lakh acres with a production of about 2.50 lakh bales in Tamil Nadu. However, 98 per cent of the 120 lakh bales required by the Cotton spinning mills operating in the State is procured from other States. Therefore, with the objective of enhancing Cotton production, the Cotton Renaissance Mission will be launched as a five -year mission from 2026 –27. This Mission will promote high - yielding production technologies such as High -Density Planting System (HDPS), Ultra High -Density Planting System (UHDPS), Integrated Crop Management and nipping, besides encouraging the cultivation of Extra Long 23 Staple (ELS) Cotton and intercropping to enhance the farmers' income. Th e Mission will be implemented during 2026–27 in an area of 73,360 acre at a t otal outlay of Rs.27.21 crore from the Union and State Government funds, benefitting 40,000 Cotton farmers. 9. Maize Production Enhancement Scheme Maize serves as a major raw material for the poultry feed and ethanol industries in Tamil Nadu. In order to meet the steadily increasing demand for maize and enable farmers to realize better incomes, the Maize Production Enhancement Scheme will be implemented during 2026–27 at a total outlay of Rs.36 crore from the Union and State Government funds. The scheme will be implemented in an area of 3.47 lakh acres, benefitting 1.39 lakh farmers. 10.

Agroforestry Scheme With a view to mitigate the impact of climatic changes, conserving the environment and creating permanent green cover in agricultural lands of Tamil Nadu, the Agroforestry Scheme will be implemented during 2026–27 at a total outlay of Rs.17.70 crore from the Union and State Government funds. Under this 24 scheme, nurseries will be established for the production of quality tree seedlings and will be distributed to t he farmers at free of cost. Under this scheme, aimed at boosting farmers' income, environmental protection, and sustainable agriculture, 12,500 acres of cultivable fallow land will be restored to cultivation. This land will be planted with high-value tree species such as Teak, Mahogany, Sandalwood, Malai Vembu, and Red Sanders at a rate of 200 saplings per acre. 11. Certified Seeds for Higher Productivity Use of certified seeds by the farmers can enhance crop yields upto 25 per cent. With this objective, the Tamil Nadu State Seed Development Agency during 2026–27 will establish seed farms in the Government State Seed Farms and farmers' field for crops such as Paddy, Millets, Pulses, Oilseeds and Cotton. A total of 43,400 metric tonne of certified seeds will be procured at a cost of Rs.250 crore by the Tamil Nadu State Seed Development Agency and distributed to the farmers at subsidised rates under various Union and State Government schemes, benefitting about 10 lakh farmers. 25 12.

items.text: 25 12. Wild Boar Damage Prevention Scheme Various methods have been adopted since time immemorial to protect the agricultural crops from wild animals. The rich literary heritage of Tamil Sangam literature bears testimony to these traditional practices. The Malaipadukadam vividly portrays women guarding Millet fields by driving away birds using slings and sounding bamboo clappers " ஒலிகைழத் தட்ைட புைடயுநர் புனம்ெதாறும் கிளிகடி மகளிர் விளி படு பூசல்" The Tamil classical work in the following verse also describes about how in anc ient times people guarded the narrow tracks frequented by boars by setting up rare traps known as adar, made of large stone slabs, designed in such a way that the boars would enter and get trapped ” விைள புனம் நிழத்தலின், ேகழல் அஞ்சி, புைழெதாறும் மாட்டிய இருங் கல் அடாஅர் அரும் ெபாறி ” In recent years, incidence of crop damages caused by wild boars has increased significantly across Tamil Nadu, resulting in substantial economic loss to 26 farmers. In response to the demand of majority of the farmers, a sp ecial scheme will be implemented during 2026–27 at a total outlay of Rs.7.35 crore to prevent the crop damages caused by the wild boars. i. The environment -friendly liquid wild boar repellent developed by the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) will be distributed to the farmers at subsidised rates. The scheme will be implemented in an area of 14,000 acres at an outlay of Rs.1.35 crore from the state fund. ii.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]

items.text: The scheme will be implemented in an area of 14,000 acres at an outlay of Rs.1.35 crore from the state fund. ii. In order to minimise the crop damages caused not only by wild boars but also by Elephants, Gaurs and Deer, solar-powered electric fencing systems will be installed in the current year at subsidised rates for 134 farmers at an outlay of Rs.2 crore. iii. In many districts, dense growth of Prosopis juliflora (Seemai Karuvelam) has become a preferred habitat for wild boars, which subsequently damage crops in the nearby agricultural fields. Therefore, with a view to not only control the wild boar population but also to restore the soil health and 27 protect the environment, the removal of Prosopis juliflora from Government and private lands will be carried out through the District Collectors at an outlay of Rs.4 crore from the state fund. 13. Annal Ambedkar Agricultural Assistance Scheme The Annal Ambedkar Agricultural Assistance Scheme will be implemented with the objective of facilitating Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe farmers to access the benefits of Government schemes seamlessly, create irrigation infrastructure for enhancing the agricultural production and improve their livelihood. i. Small and marginal farmer s belonging to the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities often find it difficult to meet the beneficiary contribution required under high- value agricultural schemes. To reduce their financial burden and facilitate them to benefit largely under various welfare schemes, an additional subsidy of 20 per cent will be provided under this Scheme.
