items.text: To reduce their financial burden and facilitate them to benefit largely under various welfare schemes, an additional subsidy of 20 per cent will be provided under this Scheme. Accordingly, 70 per cent subsidy will be provided for components such as Integrated Farming System, Greenhouses, Shade Net 28 Houses, Solar Dryers, Value Addition Machinery and Farm Machinery and 80 per cent subsidy for the installation of solar - powered pump sets under Union-State shared schemes. ii. To create irrigation facilities in rainfed lands belonging to 300 Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe farmers who do not have access to irrigation, bore wells or tube wells with electric motor pumps or solar -powered pump sets will be established with 100 per cent subsidy. During 2026–27, an amount of Rs.56.72 crore will be allocated from the state fund for the implementation of these schemes. 14. Distribution of Tarpaulins for Prevention of Post - Harvest Loss In response to the long- standing demand of the farming community, tarpaulins will be distributed to 43,500 farmers during 2026– 27 to prevent post -harvest loss and facilitate drying and safe storage of agricultural produce from natural events such as rainfall. A sum of 29 Rs.10 crore will be allocated from the State fund for this scheme. 15. Makkal Sevagar Anjalai Ammal Award for Small and Marginal farmers With a view to encoura ge small and marginal farmers, State -Level Crop Yield Competitions will be conducted during 2026 –27 in the name of "Makkal Sevagar Anjalai Ammal" .
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: The competition will be held for 10 crops, including Millets, Pulses and Oilseeds and the top three farmers achieving the highest yields in each crop category will be awarded with a prize amount of Rs.2.50 lakh, Rs.1.50 lakh and Rs.1 lakh respectively. The prize amount will be given to 30 farmers for which a sum of Rs.50 lakh will be allocated from the state fund. 16. District-Level "Vetri Vivasayi" Award The District-Level "Vetri Vivasayi” Award will be awarded to recognize farmers cultivating at least two acre and achieving the highest productivity in nine crops, namely Paddy, Millets, Pulses, Oilseeds and Cotton. The top two farmers achieving the highest yields in each crop category will be awarded with a prize amount of Rs.50,000 and, Rs.25,000 respectively. The prize amount 30 will be given to 90 farmers for which a sum of Rs.67.50 lakh will be allocated from the state fund. 17. Nammazhvar Award for Best Organic Farmer As a part of the State's effort to popularise Organic Farming, the "Nammazhvar Award" will be awarded during 2026 –27 to the Best 5 Organic Farmers recognizing their excellence in organic farming practices. A cash prize of Rs.2 lakh along with a Certificate of Appreciation will be given for which an amount of Rs.11 lakh will be allocated from the state fund. 18.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: A cash prize of Rs.2 lakh along with a Certificate of Appreciation will be given for which an amount of Rs.11 lakh will be allocated from the state fund. 18. Construction of New Buildings for Integrated Agricultural Extension Centres In order to enable far mers to access all schemes and technical advisory services of the Agriculture - Farmers Welfare Department under one roof, eight new buildings for Integrated Agricultural Extension Centres, each with a 300-metric tonne capacity godown, will be constructed in Tiruvannamalai, Katpadi and Gudiyatham (Vellore), Musiri (Tiruchirappalli), Narikudi (Virudhunagar), Bodinayakanur (Theni), Kayathar (Thoothukudi) and Thondamuthur (Coimbatore). These centres will be established at a 31 total outlay of Rs.27.82 crore from the Union and State Government funds. 19. Agriculture Expo To create awareness among farmers and the general public on modern agricultural technologies, Good Agricultural Practices (GAP), value -added agricultural products, value addition machinery, agricultural machinery, natural farming practices, an Agriculture Expo (Agri Expo) will be organised at an outlay of Rs.3 crore allocated from the state fund. The Expo will showcase improved cultivation practices, innovative agricultural technologies and successful farming initiatives, besides providing technical guidance to farmers for enhancing crop productivity and farm income. 20.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: The Expo will showcase improved cultivation practices, innovative agricultural technologies and successful farming initiatives, besides providing technical guidance to farmers for enhancing crop productivity and farm income. 20. Strengthening the Infrastructure of Liquid Bio- Fertiliser Production Units In order to strengthen the infrastructure of the 22 Liquid Bio-Fertiliser Production Units of the Department of Agriculture in Tamil Nadu, an amount of Rs.3.56 crore will be allocated for the installation of new fermenters, incubators and steam generators. 32 21. Establishment of New Seed Processing Units With a view to en hance the seed processing capacity, 3 new Seed Processing Units , each with a 250-metric tonne seed storage godown , will be installed at Gangavalli in Salem district, Killikulam in Thoothukudi district, and Iruvelpattu in Villupuram district at an outlay of Rs.7.10 crore allocated from the state fund. Department of Sugar 22. Seed Cane Subsidy Scheme The Government will implement the Seed Cane Subsidy Scheme to reduce the cultivation costs, boost productivity, and encourage mechanised harvesting. Under this sche me, farmers registered with Co-operative and Public Sector Sugar Mills willing to adopt a wider row planting system using bud chip seedlings and single - budded setts of high- yielding and high sugar recovery sugarcane varieties will receive these planting materials at 50% subsidy. The State Government will allocate Rs.9.36 crore to implement this initiative across 17,315 acres. 33 23. Sugarcane Cultivation Development Programme The Government will implement the Sugarcane Cultivation Development Programme to increa se the area under sugarcane cultivation and reduce production costs.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: The State Government will allocate Rs.9.36 crore to implement this initiative across 17,315 acres. 33 23. Sugarcane Cultivation Development Programme The Government will implement the Sugarcane Cultivation Development Programme to increa se the area under sugarcane cultivation and reduce production costs. Under this programme, subsidy will be provided for breeder seed cane, tissue culture seedlings, bud chip seedlings, single -budded setts, de -trashing, shade -net establishment, trash shredding & mulching, besides distribution of micronutrient mixtures and bio -fertilisers. An amount of Rs.9 crore will be allocated from Union and State Government funds for the implementation of this programme. 24. Feasibility Study for Ethanol Production at Kallakurichi-I Co-operative Sugar Mill The Government will allocate Rs.20 lakh from state funds to prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) and a Feasibility Report for establishing a 100 Kilo Litre Per Day (KLPD) ethanol distillery at the Kallakurichi-I Co-operative Sugar Mill under a consortium arrangement with the Kallakurichi-II and Chengalrayan co-operative sugar mills. 34 Department of Horticulture and Plantation Crops Hon’ble Speaker! The growth of horticultural crops such as vegetables, fruits, flowers, and spices & condiments plays a significant role in Tamil Nadu by providing farmers with a continuous source of income, contributing to nutritional security for the people, and serving as raw materials for the food processing industry. The Department of Horticulture is implementing various schemes to enhance the production and productivity of horticultural crops and for production of high -quality horticultural produce that meets global market standards. 25.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: The Department of Horticulture is implementing various schemes to enhance the production and productivity of horticultural crops and for production of high -quality horticultural produce that meets global market standards. 25. Drop by Drop Water Scheme for Efficient Water Management “ ெநடுங்கடலும் தன்நீர்ைம குன்றும் தடிந்ெதழிலி தான்நல்காது ஆகி விடின்” (திருக்குறள் 17) “Even the vast sea will lose its richness, If clouds cease and fail to bestow” These are the words of Thiruvalluvar. Recognizing the importance of judicious water use, the Micro Irrigation Scheme is implemented with financial assistance from the Union and State Governments to enhance water 35 management in Tamil Nadu through the effective utilization of existing resources and to maximize productivity. Under this scheme, 10 0 per cent subsidy is extended to Small & Marginal farmers and 75 per cent subsidy to other farmers. As a part of the Government's Vision Plan, during the year 2026–27, the scheme will be implemented in an area of 2,22,794 acres with a financial allocation of Rs.785 crore, benefitting 95,000 farmers. 26. Palmyra Protection Mission The palmyra tree, known as the 'Karpaga Virutcham', is deeply intertwined with Tamil heritage , history and hailed as the State Tree of Tamil Nadu. Nearly three lakh agricultural labo ur families in Tamil Nadu rely on the palmyra tree for their livelihood. To ensure the protection of palmyra trees and promote the production of palmyra and value -added palmyra products, the implementation of Palmyra Protection Mission will be continued from 2026 –27 as per the Government's Vision Plan.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: To ensure the protection of palmyra trees and promote the production of palmyra and value -added palmyra products, the implementation of Palmyra Protection Mission will be continued from 2026 –27 as per the Government's Vision Plan. Under this mission, the existing District and Block-level Committees constituted to 36 regulate the felling of palmyra trees will be strengthened and closely monitored. The mission encompasses components like e stablishment of palmyra value -addition units, distribution of palmyra seeds & seedlings, training the production of value -added palmyra products and palmyra leaf products through the Palm Products and Palmyra Development Board . The mission will be implemented during 2026 –27 with an allocation of Rs. 2.10 crore from the state fund. In addition, research on the development of dwarf and early -bearing palmyra varieties at the Palmyra Research Station, Killikulam, in Thoothukudi district will be expedited and t echnologies will be made available to the farmers at the earliest. 27. "Vetri Illatharasi Veetu Thottam " – Successful Homemaker’s Home Garden The cultivation of fruits and vegetables in home gardens using natural manures instead of chemical fertilizers ensures the production of safe, chemical -free produce, thereby enhancing nutritional security and reducing environmental pollution.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: 37 Therefore, the “ Vetri Illatharasi Veetu Thottam scheme” will be implemented during the current year at an outlay of Rs.10 crore from the state fund to encourage the cultivation of vegetables, fruits and medicinal plants through grow bag kits, vertical gardens and hydroponic gardens in apartments located in urban areas and in spaces around houses in rural areas, thereby promoting well -being of people and a healthy environment. 28. Tamil Nadu Micro Greens Scheme Microgreens are 7 to 21 day old young seedlings of Broccoli, Cabbage, Radish, G reen peas, Chickpea, Flaxseed, Onion, Green gram, Horse gram, Sesame, Wheat and L eafy vegetables. Th ese Microgreens are said to be upto 40 times more nutritious than the matured plants. Therefore, as a new initiative to promote microgreens cultivation among the public, 20,000 microgreen kits containing seeds, seedling trays, cocopeat blocks, a hand sprayer and user manual will be distributed in major urban cities such as Chennai, Coimbatore and Tiruchirappalli. The scheme will be implemented during 38 2026-27 with an allocation of Rs.1.20 crore from the state fund. 29. Enhancing Horticultural Crop Production through Promotion of High-Tech Cultivation Practices By encouraging adoption of advance technologies and necessary special infrastructure among farmers, the production and productivity of horticultural crops can be significantly increased . H ence, special schemes for this purpose will be implemented during 2026 -27 with a total financial allocation of Rs.41 crore. i.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: H ence, special schemes for this purpose will be implemented during 2026 -27 with a total financial allocation of Rs.41 crore. i. In chrysanthemum cultivation, variations in photoperiod (day length) during seasonal changes significantly influence flower production. This restricts the plant growth, resulting in smaller flowers, uneven blooming, inferior flower quality and reduced yields, thereby causing substantial economic losses to farmers. To address this challenge and in response to the demands of chrysanthemum farmers, an LED lighting scheme will be introduced in this year to provide supplementary lighting during periods of seasonal 39 variation for promotion of healthy plant growth and regulate flowering based on the market demand. The scheme will be implemented with an allocat ion of Rs.5 crore from the state fund. ii. High-value horticultural crops cultivated in greenhouses and shade net houses are protected from adverse weather such as wind, rain, and high temperatures as well as pests and diseases, while also enabling year -round production. Protected cultivation enables farmers to obtain 5 to 7 times higher yields from a smaller area and quality produce while ensuring better market prices. To popularize this initiative, Polygreen Houses and Shade-net Houses spanning 3 lakh square meters will be established during 2026 –27, with an allocation of Rs.15.55 crore from the Union and State funds. iii. The use of fruit covers and banana bunch covers improves fruit quality and appearance by protecting them from pests, diseases, birds, excessive heat, and rain. As an added benefit, pesticide usage is reduced, while the market value of the produce and 40 the income of farmers are increased.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: The use of fruit covers and banana bunch covers improves fruit quality and appearance by protecting them from pests, diseases, birds, excessive heat, and rain. As an added benefit, pesticide usage is reduced, while the market value of the produce and 40 the income of farmers are increased. Based on the farmers demand, fruit covers for M ango, Guava and bunch covers for Banana will be provided for an area of 2,500 acres during 2026–27 with a financial outlay of Rs.2.50 crore. iv. Due to the impact of climate change, natural disasters cause heavy damage to horticultural pandal crops cultivated on temporary pandals, leading to severe economic losses. Therefore, “Establishment of Permanent Pandal Scheme ” will be implemented during the current year with a financial outlay of Rs.11.73 crore to encourage the permanent pandal. v. Farmers in banana -cultivating districts have requested financial assistance for banana propping as this support helps to prevent yield losses resulting from the lodging of banana plants due to heavy fruit bunches and winds. Based on this demand, Banana propping will be promoted in an area of 6,175 acres during 2026 -27 with an allocation of Rs.6.25 crore from the state fund. 41 30. Quality Assurance; Export Promotion The farmers and exporters face monetary loss whenever the fruits and vegetables exported are rejected by the importing countries due to the presence of pesticide residues.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: 41 30. Quality Assurance; Export Promotion The farmers and exporters face monetary loss whenever the fruits and vegetables exported are rejected by the importing countries due to the presence of pesticide residues. To avoid this, as a new initiative during 2026–27, farmers cultivating mango, guava, tomato, moringa and small onion in clusters over an area of 3,000 acres will be provided with capacity -building training, technical guidance and the necessary infrastructure to produce pesticide residue -free produce through Good Agricultural Practices (GAP). By this initiative, a strong market linkage will be established with exporters and markets. On this line, a scheme will be implemented in 23 crop clusters at an outlay of Rs.8.43 c rore to increase the production of export -quality horticultural produce and enhance the income of farmers. 31. Special Scheme for Coconut “Root to crown, the coconut palm is beneficial; Always been humanity's close companion”. Coconut is cultivated in an area of about 5 lakh hectares in Tamil Nadu, with a production of 670 crore number of coconuts. At present, considering the 42 challenges faced by the farmers in coconut cultivation and marketing, a " Special Scheme for Coconut " with components such as management of pest and disease incidences, increasing the productivity, enhancing value addition will be implemented with an allocation of Rs.16 crore from the state fund. i. Application of Coconut Tonic boosts nutrient uptake from the soil, promotes palm growth, and enhances flowering and fruit set.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: Application of Coconut Tonic boosts nutrient uptake from the soil, promotes palm growth, and enhances flowering and fruit set. Based on the farmers ’ demand and to improve the health and productivity of coconut palms, Coconut Tonic will be provided for an area of 86,000 acres during 2026- 27 with a total allocation of Rs.6.20 crore from the state fund. ii. Root wilt disease and R ugose spira lling whitefly infestation in coconut palms cause yield losses from 35 to 80 per cent. To control this damage, Integrated Pest and Disease Management techniques along with sustainable biological control methods will be widely promoted among the coconut farmers for which the predatory insect Apertochrysa and the Cococon microbial mixture will be provided to farmers at 75 per cent subsidy 43 covering an area of 1,350 acres, with an allocation of Rs.1 crore from the state fund. iii. Based on the farmers request to produce & distribute bio -control agents such as Chrysoperla predatory insects, Isaria fumosorosea fungi in large scale for effective control of Rugose Spira lling Whitefly attack in coconut palms, 5 new Coconut Parasite Production Centers will be established at a cost of Rs.3 crore. The Chrysoperla Production Centres will be established at Azhiyar Nagar and Kannampalayam in Coimbatore District, Vaigai Dam in Theni District, Devathanam in Virudhunagar District, and Isaria f umosorosea Production Centre will be established at Puthalam in Kanyakumari District. iv.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: To ensure the distribution of quality coconut seedlings to the farmers, a new coconut nursery will be established in an extent of 15 acres in the State Horticulture Farm, Muthalaipatti, Karur at an estimated cost of Rs.48 lakh. 44 v. Tamil Nadu Coconut Processing Corporation To ensure a sustainable increase in the income of coconut farmers, secure remunerative prices for value -added Neera, coconut and other coconut-based pro ducts, to create sustainable market opportunities, and fulfil the long - standing demand of coconut farmers, Tamil Nadu Coconut Processing Corporation will be established by the Department of Agricultural Marketing and Agri Business with an allocation of Rs.22.30 crore from the state fund. This Corporation will provide guidance and technical support on post -harvest infrastructure, processing, quality certification, packaging and exports. Further, to render comprehensive services, the Corporation will work in tandem with the Coconut Development Board, Cooperative Societies and the Department of Horticulture & Plantation crops . This year , an amount of Rs.5.30 crore will be allocated from the state fund. vi. To prevent the price decline of copra and stabilize the market, the Price Support Scheme (PSS) to 45 procure copra at Minimum Support Price (MSP) will be notified at an appropriate time and implemented. 32. Promotion of Cultivation of High value Fruit crops In the recent days, the consumption of high -value fruit crops such as Blueberries, Rambutan, Litchi, Dragon fruit, Avocado, Kiwi, Mangosteen and Passion fruit has increased among the public.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: 32. Promotion of Cultivation of High value Fruit crops In the recent days, the consumption of high -value fruit crops such as Blueberries, Rambutan, Litchi, Dragon fruit, Avocado, Kiwi, Mangosteen and Passion fruit has increased among the public. Hence , to promote these fruits, an amount of Rs.1.87 crore will be allotted for cultivation in 930 acres as both mono and intercrops by the farmers. Besides, necessary steps will be taken to popularise Thailand Sweet Tamarind, suitable Apple varieties like KLD and HRMN -99 among farmers in non-temperate regions. 33. Promotion of Tamarind Cultivation in Rainfed Areas Promoting alterna tive crops is imperative for providing sustainable, stable income to farmers in drought-prone regions of Tamil Nadu. This is especially critical in water -scarce districts like Dharmapuri, Krishnagiri, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi, Dindigul, and Tiruchirappalli. 46 Accordingly, high -yielding grafted tamarind, which can withstand drought and thrive in areas receiving an annual rainfall of 500 to 700 mm, will be promoted for area expansion in an extent of 1,250 acres over five years with a total outlay of Rs.1 cro re, and financial assistance of Rs.20,000 per hectare. In the current year, the scheme will be implemented in 250 acres with an allocation of Rs.20 lakh from the state fund. 34. Introduction of New Varieties at Pomological Station, Coonoor.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: In the current year, the scheme will be implemented in 250 acres with an allocation of Rs.20 lakh from the state fund. 34. Introduction of New Varieties at Pomological Station, Coonoor. New varieties of Apple, Plum, Peach, P ear, Kiwi, Avocado and Persimmon will be introduced at the century- old Pomological Station, Coonoor, and a gene pool will be established at an outlay of Rs.75 lakh . By this, planting materials of these newly introduced varieties suitable for temperate regions will be produced and supplied to farmers. 35. Establishment of Mushroom Production units Mushroom cultivation is an important small -scale enterprise that generates higher income with minimal investment, and it requires a limited area. Mushrooms are increasingly gaining popularity owing to their rich 47 nutritional value, proteins , and dietary fibre essential for good health, and their taste, which is comparable to that of non-vegetarian food. To promote mushroom cultivation and ensure the uninterrupted availability of fresh mushrooms to consumers, 50 small -scale mushroom production units at a financial outlay of Rs.50 lakh will be established during 2026–27 for the benefit of rural youth and women. 36. Increasing the area under Rhizomatic Spice Crops It can be understood that the cuisine of ancient Tamils was rich in flavo ur, given that Pattinappalai explicitly highlights fragrant turmeric (Kama zh Manjal) and tender ginger ( Mulai Inji ) as valuable cash crops. In addition to these spice crops, gar lic is also cultivated extensively as a Rhizomatic spice crop in Tamil Nadu.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: In addition to these spice crops, gar lic is also cultivated extensively as a Rhizomatic spice crop in Tamil Nadu. All these crops have a high demand as food and medicine, contributing significantly to domestic and international markets and thereby increasing farmers' income. Therefore, with a view to promote the cultivation of these Rhizomatic spice crops, area expansion will be 48 taken up in an area of 2,500 acres during 2026– 27 at an outlay of Rs.4 crore. 37. Establishment of Onion Storage Structures Since onion is a seasonal crop, creating adequ ate storage facilities is essential to ensure its continuous availability to consumers throughout the year. This will address onion price volatility , supply fluctuation s and prevent sudden price hikes. Therefore, Onion storage structures with a capacity of 57,000 metric tonnes will be established during 2026-27 at an outlay of Rs.22.80 crore. 38. Promoting traditional varieties of Fruits and Vegetables It has become essential to create awareness among the present generation about the food habits of ancient people, and to revive and promote the large -scale cultivation of traditional fruit and vegetable varieties that are presently grown only in home gardens and hilly areas.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: 38. Promoting traditional varieties of Fruits and Vegetables It has become essential to create awareness among the present generation about the food habits of ancient people, and to revive and promote the large -scale cultivation of traditional fruit and vegetable varieties that are presently grown only in home gardens and hilly areas. During 2026 -27, an amount of Rs.3.88 crore will be allocated to promote the cultivation of traditional Mango varieties s uch as Sengavarukkai, Vettaiyan and Soorankudi Vettaiyan, Jac kfruit varieties such as Panrut i 49 Jackfruit, Mundan Chakka and Sembaruthi, Banana varieties such as Matti, Namaran, Sirumalai, Virupatchi, Ladan, Uthiran and tradit ional vegetable varieties by the farmers. 39. Promoting the cultivation of medicinal crops The use of medicinal crops has been highly significant since ancient times in Tamil Nadu. With the continuous increase in demand for raw materials in the modern medical sector, these crops are now cultivated commercially rather than being collected only from forests. This scheme will be implemented to further promote the cultivation of medicinal crops and expand the production of soursop, which is considered to possess potential anti-cancer properties. During 2026 –27, this scheme will be implemented in an area of 1,720 acres with a financial outlay of Rs.1.51 crore. 40. Creation of Infrastructure Facilit ies at State Horticulture Farm in Vellore district Spread over 85 acres, the State Horticulture Farm in Agaramseri, Vellore District, produces about 35 lakh horticultural planting materials annually.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: 40. Creation of Infrastructure Facilit ies at State Horticulture Farm in Vellore district Spread over 85 acres, the State Horticulture Farm in Agaramseri, Vellore District, produces about 35 lakh horticultural planting materials annually. The Protray 50 vegetable seedlings, fruit trees, tree saplings, o rnamental plants produced are supplied to farmers through Government schemes and direct sales. In order to enhance the operational efficiency of the State Horticulture Farm further, essential infrastructure facilities will be established at an outlay of Rs.2.03 crore. 41. Establishment of a Large -Scale Nursery at Putlur, Tiruvallur district A large -scale nursery will be established in an extent of 51 acres at Putlur, Tiruvallur District, for the production of quality ornamental plants and various tree species, thereby ensuring the ready availability of quality planting materials to the farmers and public. It is planned to implement this scheme over a period of five years at an outlay of Rs. 7 crore. In the first year, Rs.3 crore will be allocated for the creation of essential infrastructure facilities. 42. Establishment o f Block level Horticulture Sale Outlets In all 74 State Horticulture Farms and 24 Parks, products such as vermicompost, biocontrol agents, 51 planting materials, H orticulture tools, fruits, vegetables, and spices & condiments are being produced & made available to the public at fair prices. To facilitate the easy availability of these products, 100 Horticulture sale Outlets will be established in the Block Integrated Agriculture Extension Centres at an outlay of Rs.5 crore. 43.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: To facilitate the easy availability of these products, 100 Horticulture sale Outlets will be established in the Block Integrated Agriculture Extension Centres at an outlay of Rs.5 crore. 43. Urban Landscaping Exclusive online platform will be developed by TANHODA to facilitate the registration of requests from Government institutions, local bodies, public spaces, residential premises, and other establishments for landscape development. Through the Landscape Wing, cost-effective landscaping services, including the establishment of home gardens, lawns, and planting of ornamental and flowering plants will be provided. For this, the Landscap e Wing of the Tamil Nadu Horticulture Development Agency (TANHODA) will be strengthened to transform urban areas into greener, more attractive and environmentally sustainable spaces. 52 Agricultural Engineering Department Hon’ble Speaker! Timely execution of agricultural operations is essential to achieve optimum crop yields. To address the shortage of agr icultural labour, promote farm mechanization, conserve and augment natural resources such as soil and water, and encourage the use of renewable energy in agriculture, the Department of Agricultural Engineering is implementing multifarious schemes. 44. Distribution of Farm Machinery and Implements to individual farmers with subsidy The use of agricultural implements in agriculture can be learned through the Sangam literature. The later- period poet Kambar who wrote a book on the significance of Agriculture named it as “Aerezhupathu”, prioritized the main tool, the plough (Aer) among all implements besides eulogizing the specific accessories such as plough handle, fastener, yoke, yoke hole, yoke pin, yoke rope, plough body, plough share, plough share pin, cattle prod stick and ox separately.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: 53 To promote mechanization at the village level, agricultural machinery, implements, value addition equipment, and solar driers are provided to farmers with subsidy. During 2026 -27, Agricultural Mechanization scheme will be imple mented at an outlay of Rs.227.20 crore from the Union and State Government funds benefitting 24,000 farmers. Under this scheme, about 8,870 Power Tillers, 5,090 Power Weeders, 1,400 Rotovators, 855 Tractors will be distributed. From this year onwards, t he maximum subsidy for installation of Solar driers will be increased from Rs.3.50 l akh to Rs.4.40 lakh. In order to promote Agricultural mechanization among women farmers, priority will be given to them under this scheme. 45. Establishment of Agricultura l Machinery Custom Hiring Centres In order to facilitate farmers to easily access the agricultural machinery, implements and modern equipment such as drones for pesticide application on a rental basis and thereby execute timely agricultural operations and enhance income, Village level Agricultural Machinery Custom Hiring Centres will be established at an estimate of Rs.10 lakh each with a subsidy of 80 per cent, 54 subject to a maximum subsidy of Rs.8 lakh. A total of 50 Village level Agricultural Machinery Custom Hiring Centres will be established with a financial allocation of Rs.4 crore. Further, 30 per cent of the total outlay allocated for this scheme will be earmarked for Women Self Help Groups. 46. “Vetri Vaanmagal” Scheme Drone technology in India is creating new job opportunities in agriculture, construction, freight transport, surveillance, and disaster management sectors.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: Further, 30 per cent of the total outlay allocated for this scheme will be earmarked for Women Self Help Groups. 46. “Vetri Vaanmagal” Scheme Drone technology in India is creating new job opportunities in agriculture, construction, freight transport, surveillance, and disaster management sectors. With the United Nations having declared 2026 as the “International Year of Women Farmers” , enabling women to work as drone operators will ease agricultural activities such as fertilizer, pesticide spraying, crop monitoring while addressing labour shortages in the sector. For this, 500 eligible persons, including 100 women, will be provided drone operator training and a drone pilot license through the Remote Pilot Training Organization of the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University at State government cost of Rs.1.50 crore . Drones will be provided with 50 per cent subsidy to 50 trained women, at an allocation of Rs.2.50 crore from the state 55 fund. Our Hon’ble Chief Minister, who established the Singappen (Lioness) force to protect women, is now set to create the Vaanmagal Force to safeguard agriculture. 47. Creation and Desilting of Farm Ponds “If Rain is the gift of nature , irrigation is the preparedness by mankind”. That is why this Government, by executing the ‘ Water Governance Scheme’, is determined to maintain irrigation tanks and create new farm ponds. To augment irrigation by effectively storing rainwater, new farm ponds will be created in 5 00 farmers field with a 100 per cent subsidy. Further, to improve the rainwater storage capacity, 500 existing farm ponds will be desilted at 75 per cent subsidy using machinery from the Agricultural Engineering Department.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: To augment irrigation by effectively storing rainwater, new farm ponds will be created in 5 00 farmers field with a 100 per cent subsidy. Further, to improve the rainwater storage capacity, 500 existing farm ponds will be desilted at 75 per cent subsidy using machinery from the Agricultural Engineering Department. This initiative will be implemented during 2026 -27 with an allocation of Rs.8.50 crore. 48. Creation of Water Sources to bring 1,000 acres under Irrigation With a vision to increase the area under irrigation, water sources such as borewells or tubewells will be created for general category farmers owning land in safe 56 firkas with no assured source of irrigation. This includes 60 percent back ended subsidy assistance up to a maximum of Rs.1.20 lakh per well for small, marginal, and women farmers, and 50 percent back ended subsidy assistance up to a maximum of Rs.1 lakh per well for other categories of farmers. Further, this scheme will be dovetailed with the existing Solar Pumpset and Micro Irrigation schemes. This scheme will be implemented with an allocation of Rs.6 crore from the State fund, benefitting 500 farmers. 49. Solar Powered Pumpsets Scheme To promote renewable energy in agriculture and ensure reliable irrigation facilities to farmers, subsidized standalone solar powered pumpsets as an alternative to diesel pumpsets will be installed for 1,000 farmers who have a water source but lack an electricity connection. To avoid recurring costs for irrigation purposes for farmers, this eco -friendly scheme will be implemented during 2026 –27 with a financial allocation of Rs.23.06 crore. 57 50.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: To avoid recurring costs for irrigation purposes for farmers, this eco -friendly scheme will be implemented during 2026 –27 with a financial allocation of Rs.23.06 crore. 57 50. Integrated Agricultural Machinery Hiring Business Centre for Crop cultivation and Value addition Labour shortage, low prices for agricultural produce are the main challenges currently faced by the farmers. To address these challenges, the visionary scheme focuses on creating Integrated Agricultural Machinery Hiring Business Centres that provide farmers with rental machinery for crop cultivation and value addition. In the current year, 50 Integrated Agricultural Machinery Hiring Business Centres will be established at a unit cost of Rs.25 lakh each. A subsidy of 75 per cent will be provided to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Women entrepreneurs, youth holding a diploma or degree in Agricultural Engineering and 50 per cent subsidy for other entrepreneurs. An amount of Rs.8.13 crore will be allocated from the State fund for the implementation of this scheme. 51. Coastal Horticulture Scheme “The seashore, a precious gift to us; A loving gift that brings joy to the people” 58 To promote the cultivation of horticultural crop s in the coastal districts of Tamil Nadu through the utilization of the freshwater overlying saline groundwater and for establishing Blue Green Horticulture Parks , as a pilot project, a maximum subsidy of Rs.1.50 lakh per well will be provided to 10 farmers to construct skimming wells . In addition, standalone solar powered pumpsets and micro irrigation systems will be installed in convergence with the existing schemes. By utilizing this water source, cultivation of chilli and coriander will be encouraged i n an extent of 10 h ectares.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: In addition, standalone solar powered pumpsets and micro irrigation systems will be installed in convergence with the existing schemes. By utilizing this water source, cultivation of chilli and coriander will be encouraged i n an extent of 10 h ectares. Totally, an amount of Rs.49.40 lakh will be allocated from the State fund for the implementation of this scheme. 52. Provision of Threshing floors with subsidy assistance to farmers To thresh, sort, dry and store paddy, groundnut, pearl millet, maize, sesame and black gram produced by the farmers and to fetch fair price by minimising the post -harvest losses, 100 threshing floors will be constructed in the individual farmer ’s fields at a total outlay of Rs.2.80 crore funded by the Union and State Governments. 59 53. Strengthening Farm Machinery Hiring Services of the Agricultural Engineering Department i. To strengthen the farm machinery hiring services of the Agricultural Engineering Department through the e-Vaadagai 2.0 platform, 60 Tractors with accessories, 463 agricultural machinery and implements including Paddy Combine Harvesters will be procured during the current year at an estimated cost of Rs.19.22 crore. ii. Agricultural Machinery Sheds will be constructed in five blocks at an esti mated cost of Rs.1.08 crore. iii. To popularize the technology of bund sectioning and shaping works in paddy fields using Tractor operated ridge moulder, an amount of Rs.1.25 lakh will be allocated. A total allocation of Rs.20.31 crore will be made for the implementation of these components. 54.

items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: To popularize the technology of bund sectioning and shaping works in paddy fields using Tractor operated ridge moulder, an amount of Rs.1.25 lakh will be allocated. A total allocation of Rs.20.31 crore will be made for the implementation of these components. 54. Establishment of Agricultural Machinery Service Centres To support the increasing use of agricultural machinery and solar powered pumpsets, and to provide 60 timely repair and maintenance in rural areas through rural youth a nd entrepreneurs , an amount of Rs.1.12 crore will be allocated to establish 15 Agricultural machinery and Solar powered pumpset service centres. 55. End to E nd Mechanization in cultivation of crops End to end mechanization reduces cultivation costs by using machinery for every farm operation, from land preparation to residue management. Hence, field demonstrations on End-to-end mechanization in the cultivation of crops viz., maize, groundnut, blackgram, and coconut in farmers' fields will be taken up in an extent of 225 acres through Agri -Tech entrepreneurs with 100 per cent subsidy assistance at an outlay of Rs.46.37 lakh. 56. Construction of Agricultural Engineering Extension and Training Centres To facilitate the farmers to enhance the crop production by adopting advanced technologies in crop cultivation and post-harvest management activities and to promote the agricultural engineering technologies among farmers, Agricultural Engineering Extension and Training 61 Centres will be constructed at Thirukoilur, Karaiku di, Musiri, Dharapuram and Kumbakonam at an outlay of Rs.4.60 crore from Union and State Government fund. 57.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: 57. Mega exhibition of Modern Agricultural Machinery and Implements A mega exhibition will be organized in Thanjavur district during current year to create awareness among farmers about the benefits of modern and innovative agricultural machinery, implements and equipment suitable for various crops and agricultural operations. This exhibition will establish a link between farmers, agricultural machinery manufacturers and department officials and thus will lead to the adoption of mechanized cultivation practices by farmers on a large scale. Department of Agricultural Marketing and Agri Business Hon’ble Speaker! The journey of agricultural produce, cultivated through the unwavering dedication and hard work of our farmers, begins at farm and progress through multiple stages before reaching consumers. Beyond serving domestic markets, this journey extends to international 62 destinations through exports, enabling t he agricultural produce of Tamil Nadu establish a strong presence in global markets. The Department of Agricultural Marketing and Agri Business plays a pivotal role in facilitating and strengthening this value chain, ensuring better market access and enhanced opportunities to our farmers. In view of t his, the Department proposes to implement a series of strategic initiatives during 2026 -27. These initiatives are aimed at enhancing farmers’ incomes, promoting value addition, strengthening market linkages an d advancing the Government’s long - term vision of sustainable and inclusive agricultural development. With these farmer centric schemes of our Hon’ble Chief Minister, who is deeply committed to the welfare of farmers, no one can halt the growth of agriculture sector under this government. 58.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: With these farmer centric schemes of our Hon’ble Chief Minister, who is deeply committed to the welfare of farmers, no one can halt the growth of agriculture sector under this government. 58. Tamil Nadu Farmers' Income Enhancement Commission "Ensuring remunerative price for farmers' produce! prosperity for the State through sustainable agriculture!" 63 With the objective of sustainably enhancing farmers' income and securing their economic self -reliance, the Tamil Nadu Farmers' Income Enhancement Commission will be established with an outlay of Rs.23 crore. This year, an amount of Rs.5.20 crore will be allocated from the state fund to carry out these activities. 59. Marketing Organic Agricultural Produce With the growing awareness on organic agricultural produce in the recent times, organic farmers and interested FPOs will be linked with traders to expand market and export opportunities. Initiatives like buyer - seller meets, market linkages, participation in national and international expos, and organised marketing support, will help them fetch higher incomes. This year, necessary facilities will be created for marketing organic produce like traditional rice, chilli, pepper, turmeric etc., and a dedicated expert cell will be established for this purpose. The programme will be implemented in a 5-year period with a total State outlay of Rs.19 crore, of which Rs.3 crore will be allocated during 2026–27. 64 Further, to expand market opportunities, farmers producing organic products will be facilitated to sell their produce once a week at Uzhavar Sandhais. 60. Formation of New Farmer Producer Companies New Farmer Producer Companies will be formed by collectivizing small and marginal farmers to improve market access and increase their income.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: 60. Formation of New Farmer Producer Companies New Farmer Producer Companies will be formed by collectivizing small and marginal farmers to improve market access and increase their income. Each shareholder of a newly formed FPC will receive equity grant support of Rs. 2,000/- in the first year, followed by Rs.1,500/- each in the second and third year s, totalling Rs.5,000/- per shareholder. This scheme will be implemented with a total State outlay of Rs.30 crore, of which Rs.12 crore will be allocated this year. 61. Strengthening Farmer Producer Organisations In Tamil Nadu, 1,686 Farmer Producer Companies (FPCs) have been promoted through various agencies, with 397 FPCs promoted by the Department of Agricultural Marketing and Agri Business. To ensure their sustainable growth, a “ Farmer Producer Companies Management Cell” will be established to provide technical guidance and institutional support. Selected 65 FPCs will receive Rs.10,000/ - towards the cost incurred for online submission of ROC filings , as well as 50 per cent reimbursement on the Chief Executive Officer's salary, up to a maximum of Rs.12,500/ - per month. In addition, awareness programmes on best practices, capacity -building programmes on market linkage, value addition, and sustainable income generation, as well as regional -level exhibitions, will be organised. An amount of Rs.5 crore will be allocated from the State fund for implementing these initiatives. 62.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: In addition, awareness programmes on best practices, capacity -building programmes on market linkage, value addition, and sustainable income generation, as well as regional -level exhibitions, will be organised. An amount of Rs.5 crore will be allocated from the State fund for implementing these initiatives. 62. Establishment of “ Agri Business Guidance Bureau” An Agri Business Guidance Bureau will be established in Chennai at an outlay of Rs.50 lakh from the state fund to provide guidance to farmers, innovative agripreneurs and Farmer Producer Companies on modern technologies, credit linkage, subsidy assistance, crop insurance, investment planning, preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) etc. 66 63. Construction of 1,000 MT Storage Godown in Regulated Markets To enable farmers to store their produce during gluts and price-fall periods and to sell when market prices improve, 1,000 MT storage godowns will be established in both the Polur (Tiruvannamalai) and Ammoor (Ranipet) Regulated Markets, with an allocation of Rs.4.80 crore from Union and State funds. 64. Establishment of Cold Storage Facilities To minimise post -harvest losses, extend shelf life and preserve the quality of produce like vegetables, fruits, pulses, tamarind, dry chillies and lemons, 500 MT cold storage facilities will be es tablished through Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model in Kancheepuram, Tiruchirappalli, and Thoothukudi districts, which are strategically located near ports and airports to enable export opportunities. 65.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: 65. Upgradation of Primary Processing Centres and Specialised Market Complexes in the Union Region Primary Processing Centres established at M.Pudur for Banana, P.K. Agaram for Onion in Trichy district and Gopalpatti for tamarind, Vedasandur for moringa in 67 Dindigul district, along with the Onion Market Complex at Chettikulam in Perambalur district and Coconut Market Complex at Rajendrapuram in Pudukottai district, will be upgraded with secondary and tertiary processing facilities. Farmer Producer Companies, entrepreneurs and exporters utilising these centres will be given 50 per cent subsidy for installing machinery. A sum of Rs.3 crore will be allocated from the State Fund. 66. Additional facilities at the Pochampalli Primary Processing Centre for export. To expand the export of mangoes, pomegranates, and vegeta bles to China, South Korea, Japan, and the European Union, additional facilities including a hot water treatment unit, a grading & sorting hall, and a cold storage unit will be established at an outlay of Rs.1.94 crore using Union and State funds. 67.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: 67. Modernisation of Uzhavar Sandhais (Farmers Markets) An amount of Rs .20 crore will be allocated from the State Fund during 2026 -27 to upgrade the basic infrastructure fa cilities in 10 Uzhavar Sandhais; redeveloping Chennai's Pallavaram and Avadi Uzhavar 68 Sandhais into moderni zed integrated farmers' markets; relocation of Perambalur's non -functional Veppanthattai Uzhavar sandhai to Elambalur, and Tiruvarur's Mannargudi-I market to its earlier location with construction of new buildings. 68. Electronic Price Display Boards in Uzhavar Sandhais In Tamil Nadu, the prices of produce sold by farmers in 194 Uzhavar Sandhais are fixed on a daily basis in such a way that the price s are higher than the wholesale market price and lower than the retail price paid by consumers. To ensure that the price fixed for all vegetables and fruits is made transparent and visible to farmers & consumers, electronic price display boards will be installed in 59 Uzhavar Sandhais with an allocation of Rs.2.04 crore from the state fund. 69. Market Intervention Scheme – Price Stabilization Revolving Fund (MIS-PSRF) A Market Intervention Scheme – Price Stabilization Revolving Fund (MIS -PSRF) will be created by the Tamil Nadu State Agricultural Marketing Board with a State fund of Rs.4.26 crore to protect farmers from price 69 fall of perishable commodities like tomatoes. This scheme will help in stabilizing the market prices of tomatoes and onions. 70.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: This scheme will help in stabilizing the market prices of tomatoes and onions. 70. Agricultural Intelligence and Market Excellence Centre (AIMEC) Tamil Nadu is a leading State in agricultural marketing. To further strengthen this position, an Agricultural Intelligence and Market Excellence Centre (AIMEC) will be established. This centre will integrate data from 285 R egulated Markets, 213 e- NAM markets, 194 Uzhavar Sandhais, and 1,686 Farmer Producer Companies and all connected facilities to provide real-time market intelligence and decision support for farmers, policymakers and other stakeholders using Artificial Intelligence (AI), predictive analytics and Geographic Information System (GIS) technologies. In the current year, an amount of Rs.4 crore will be allocated from the State fund to establish this Centre. DEPARTMENT OF SEED CERTIFICATION AND ORGANIC CERTIFICATION “It is because of seeds that life and plants continue to exist on Earth even today. Since their formation, seeds 70 are naturally endowed with required nutrients and a protective outer coat. Ensuring that these seeds, which are the very foundation of crop cultivation, are of high quality” is the primary mandate of the Department of Seed Certification and Organic Certification. 71. Integrated Website for the Organic and Natural Farmers The Union Government currently maintains separate websites for the National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP), Participatory Guarantee System (PGS–India Organic), and Participatory Guarantee System (PGS–Natural Farming) schemes. The details of farmers registered under these schemes are inaccessible to consumers and traders. Therefore, an integrated website containing the data of all farmers registered under the above three schemes will be created at an estimated cost of Rs.20 lakh. 72.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: The details of farmers registered under these schemes are inaccessible to consumers and traders. Therefore, an integrated website containing the data of all farmers registered under the above three schemes will be created at an estimated cost of Rs.20 lakh. 72. Obtaining NABL Accreditation for Seed Testing Laboratories To ensure seed quality and improve the credibility of testing results, NABL accreditation will be obtained for eight Seed Testing Laboratories located in Nagapattinam, 71 Theni, Namakkal, Tiruvallur, Erode, Ramanathapuram, Dindigul, and Krishnagiri at an outlay of Rs.40 lakh. 73. Provision of QR-code -enabled certification tags for certified seeds by the Department of Seed Certification QR code-enabled certification tags will be provided for certified seeds by the Department of Seed Certification. This initiative will establish complete seed traceability, enabling end-to-end monitoring of seeds from production to distribution. This scheme will be implemented with a fund allocation of Rs.1 crore. Tamil Nadu Agricultural University The Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, by extending Agricultural Education and Extension and engaged in Research and acts as a pillar for the Agricultural growth and economic development in Tamil Nadu. 74. Establishment of an Agricultural Technology Research Centre at Ooty, The Nilgiris The Kurinji region of Nilgiris district is renowned for the cultivation of tea, hill vegetables, aromatic crops, and flowers. However, farmers in the region continue to face challenges in producing high -quality produce and 72 marketing the products. Hence, the Government has planned to encourage & enhance the livelihoods of the Nilgiris District farmers by promoting chemical -free and sustainable farming practices, and create better market opportunities for their produce.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: Hence, the Government has planned to encourage & enhance the livelihoods of the Nilgiris District farmers by promoting chemical -free and sustainable farming practices, and create better market opportunities for their produce. In the first phase, the existing Ooty Horticultural Research Station at Nilgiris will be upgraded as a state -of-the-art Agricultural Technology Research Centre at an estimated cost of Rs.10 crore . As per the Government’s long term vision plan, an amount of Rs.5 Crore will initially be allocated from the state fund to establish the centre. 75. Establishment of a new Diploma College for Organic Agriculture at Sakkottai, Thanjavur District In line with the Government’s long-term vision to make Tamil Nadu a pioneer state in organic farming, a new Diploma College for Organic Agriculture , in the name of natural farming scientist Nammalvar , will be established at Sakkottai, near Kumbakonam with a budget allocation of Rs.15 crore from the state fund. Initially, an amount of Rs.5 crore will be released from the state fund during the year 2026-27. 73 In this diploma college, students will be educated on all aspects related to organic farming through hands on experience and suitably guided on job opportunities. 76. Establishment of Export -Oriented Technology Hubs for Horticultural Crops Export-oriented technology hubs will be established for crops highly suited for export such as mango, turmeric, and chilli to promote awareness on residue -free cultivation practices among farmers and connect them with global markets. These centres will provide farmers with advanced training, proper guidance, and extensive technological support.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: These centres will provide farmers with advanced training, proper guidance, and extensive technological support. Accordingly, a Mango Technology Centre at Paiyur, Krishnagiri district, Chilli Technology Centres at Ramanathapuram and Kovilpatti in Thoothukudi district and a Turmeric Technology Ce ntre at Bhavanisagar, Erode district will be newly established. An allocation of Rs.1.50 crore from state funds will be made for each centre, amounting to a total of Rs.6 crore to establish these facilities. In the first phase, 1,000 farmers will be identified and directly linked to international export markets. 74 77. Expansion of Student Hostel Facilities at Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) admits approximately 2,400 to 3,500 undergraduate and postgraduate students annually. Most of these students come from rural backgrounds, and over 70 per cent are girls. With the objective of providing hostel rooms with the necessary infrastructure and ensuring that students pursue their education without hassles, the student hostels on the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University campus in Coimbatore will be expanded at an estimated cost of Rs.10 crore. For this, an amount of Rs. 5 crore will be provided from the state fund , and the remaining Rs.5 crore by the University fro m its own financial resources. 78. Research on Production of manure from Poultry Waste for soil health improvement Tamil Nadu is a leading state in egg and broiler production. The districts of Namakkal, Salem, Karur, Erode, Tiruppur, and Coimbatore serve as the major hubs for this industry.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: The districts of Namakkal, Salem, Karur, Erode, Tiruppur, and Coimbatore serve as the major hubs for this industry. Poultry farms in Tamil Nadu generate between 5,400 and 6,700 metric tonnes of waste every 75 day. Currently, this waste is often dumped in open areas without safety precautions, leading to environmental pollution. In response to the request of the farming community, research and demonstrations will be conducted by the Sandiyur Krishi Vigyan Kendra in Salem district on technologies to improve soil fertility by drying and powdering poultry wastes generated in Namakkal, Salem, Karur, and surrounding districts and converting them into nutrient -rich fertilizer pellets. For this, an amount of Rs.1 crore will be allocated from the state fund. 79. Providing New Buses for Tamil Nadu Agricultural University for Students’ field visits Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) offers 14 undergraduate degree programmes, with more than 3,000 students pursuing their studies at the Coimbatore main campus. As part of their academic curriculum, students regularly undertake educational visits to cooperative banks, research institutes, agricultural fields, and agricultural markets across various agro -climatic zones in Tamil Nadu to gain practical exposure and hands- on learning. 76 In order to undertake such field visits safely and in a hassle -free mann er by the students, an amount of Rs.1.50 crore from the state fund and Rs.1.50 c rore from the revenue of the TNAU will be provided for the purchase of six new buses. Tamil Nadu Food Processing and Agri Export Promotion Corporation (TNAPEx) 80.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: Tamil Nadu Food Processing and Agri Export Promotion Corporation (TNAPEx) 80. Establishment of “ Centre for Refining and Advancing Food Technology (CRAFT) ” at Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore A “Centre for Refining and Advancing Food Technology (CRAFT)” will be established through TNAPEx at Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), Coimbatore, at an estimated cost of Rs.2.62 crore . The Centre will strengthen the food processing ecosystem through innovation, value-added product development, analytical services, and technical support, thereby benefiting Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Tamil Nadu. 77 81. Support for Branding, Packaging, Marketing, Input & Output Supply Chain development and New Food Product development To strengthen Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) engaged in food processing, TNAPEx will provide a range of services, including branding, packaging, marketing, supply chain development, and new food product development. The scheme will be implemented for the benefit of food processing MSMEs with a total allocation of Rs.8.61 crore. 82. Support for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises engaged in Food Processing Support will be provided for market linkage, branding, and platform integration to encourage food processing MSMEs to join e -commerce and quick - commerce platforms. A dditionally, export readiness training, assistance for international regulatory compliance and quality certification will be extended to 100 food processing MSMEs, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), and entrepreneurs, with an allocation of approximately Rs.2 crore .
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: A dditionally, export readiness training, assistance for international regulatory compliance and quality certification will be extended to 100 food processing MSMEs, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), and entrepreneurs, with an allocation of approximately Rs.2 crore . Traceability services will also be provided for key agricultural and export-oriented commodities such as chilli, drumstick, 78 mango, coconut, banana, tomato, and shrimp. These measures will enhance global market opportunities for agricultural and value-added food products. 83. Establishment of TNAPEx Regional Centres at Tiruchirappalli and Coimbatore To enhance the regional outreach and inclusive growth of the Tamil Nadu Food Processing and Agri Export Promotion Corporation (TNAPEx), Regional Centres will be established at Tiruchirappalli and Coimbatore at an estimated cost of Rs.78 lakh. These centres will provide comprehensive support services to farmers, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), exporters, entrepreneurs, and food processing Micro, Smal l and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). 84. Co-operation, Food and Consumer Protection I. Co-operation i. During 2026-27, Crop loan to the tune of Rs.17,000 crore will be provided to meet the short -term Agricultural credit requirements for crop cultivation in Tamil Nadu. ii. To meet out the short -term credit requirements of farmers to take up Agriculture related activities like 79 Animal husbandry, Fisheries and beekeeping, working capital loan of Rs.3,000 crore will be provided during 2026-27. iii.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: To meet out the short -term credit requirements of farmers to take up Agriculture related activities like 79 Animal husbandry, Fisheries and beekeeping, working capital loan of Rs.3,000 crore will be provided during 2026-27. iii. To Purchase goats and sheep and for their maintenance, Agriculture based medium term loans and capital loans for livestock maintenance will be provided through Co -operative banks to landless people in scheduled caste category. iv. During 2026 -27, till 15.07.2026, Crop loan to the tune of Rs.159.41 crore and livestock maintenance loan of Rs.140.91 crore have been disbursed to 12,752 farmers and 19,324 individuals respectively. v. In order to waive the crop loan of eligible farmers of the year 2026, an amount of Rs.100 crore, as first instalment, R s.3,000 crore as second instalment, Rs.1,820 crore as third instalment and Rs.347 crore as fourth instalment totalling to Rs.5,267 crore have been disbursed by the Government during 2026. II. Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation Incentive for Paddy Procurement The Government of Tamil Nadu is providing an incentive of Rs.1560/-per metric tonne for Grade ‘A’ 80 and Rs.1310/- per metric tonne for common varieties of paddy procured directly from the farmers. In the current procurement season - KMS, 2025- 2026, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has procured 62,72,720 MT of Paddy from 6,14,580 farmers through direct paddy purchase centers till 29.07.2026.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: In the current procurement season - KMS, 2025- 2026, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has procured 62,72,720 MT of Paddy from 6,14,580 farmers through direct paddy purchase centers till 29.07.2026. So far, A total incentive of Rs.917 crore has been directly credited into the farmers bank account. 85. Water Resources Department The main objective of the Water Resources Department is to store rain water, which is an essential resource for irrigation and drinking purposes in Dams, Anicuts and Tanks and distribute it in an efficient manner. To ensure that the wate r released from the Dams for irrigation reaches the tail end area without any hindrance, in 2026-27, 1,161 desilting works for a length of 5 ,955 km in the Rivers, Channels, Canals and drains are taken up by the Water Resources Department at an estimated cost of Rs.125 crore. By this, the area coverage and production targets for paddy and other crops of the State can be achieved and the farmers income can also be enhanced. 81 86. Animal Husbandry Hon’ble Speaker! The Animal Husbandry Department plays a vital role in ensuring food security, nutritional security, and sustainable livelihoods, while serving as a key component of the rural economy, particularly in promoting the socio - economic empowerment of women. i. Improving Buffalo Breeding Efficiency To improve the reproductive efficiency of buffaloes, nutritional support will be provided to 1,000 buffalo heifers and 1,000 pregnant buffaloes . An amount of Rs.2.04 crore will be allocated for this scheme. ii. Revival of Tamil Nadu’s traditional cattle breeds Tamil Nadu is home for several indigenous livestock breeds.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: An amount of Rs.2.04 crore will be allocated for this scheme. ii. Revival of Tamil Nadu’s traditional cattle breeds Tamil Nadu is home for several indigenous livestock breeds. As many as 1,52,000 Kangayam cattle, 14,000 Pulikulam cattle, 42,000 Umbalachery cattle, 55,000 Bargur cattle, and 20,000 Toda buffaloes are owned by individuals. Of these, livestock maintenance assistance of Rs.5,000/ - per animal will be provided for 5,000 indigenous livestock owned by Women Self -Help Groups. A sum of Rs.2.50 crore will be allocated for this scheme. Further, appropriate convergence measures will 82 be undertaken with Government agencies such as the Tamil Nadu State Rural Livelihood Mission (TNSRLM) to enable Women Self-Help Groups to market their livestock- based products to farmers at fair prices. 87. Dairy Development With a daily milk production of approximately 3 crore litres, Tamil Nadu contributes to around 4.7 per cent of India's total milk production. Since the state’s per capita daily milk availability is 407 grams, the Dairy Development Department plays a significant role in ensuring nutritional security across the State. i. Establishment of 500 Medium Dairy Farms With the objective of promoting dairy entrepreneurship among small and marginal milk producers and ensuring a sustainable source of income, 500 medium-scale dairy farms, each comprising five milch animals (3+2 model), will be established. Under this scheme, a capital subsidy of 25 per cent of the project cost will be provided. Institutional credit at concessional interest rates will be facilitated for the remaining project cost.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27 [Agriculture and Farmers Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Agriculture Budget Speech 2026-27

items.text: Under this scheme, a capital subsidy of 25 per cent of the project cost will be provided. Institutional credit at concessional interest rates will be facilitated for the remaining project cost. This initiative will enhance milk production, ge nerate year-round employment and improve the livelihoods of 83 milk producers, particularly women. Necessary funds will be provided from the state fund for the implementation of this scheme. ii. Mini Dairies To ensure a stable year -round income for milk producers, an interest subsidy of 4 per cent is being provided for the establishment of 5,000 Mini Dairy units across the State. To ensure continued support to eligible milk producers under the Mini Dairy Scheme, the programme will be continued during 2026 –27 w ith a financial allocation of Rs.4.19 crore. iii. Supply of Cattle Feed at subsidized Price With the objective of reducing the cost of milk production and supporting economically weaker milk producers, quality balanced cattle feed will be supplied to eligible milk producers living below the poverty line at a subsidy of Rs.2/ - per kilogram, at the rate of 3 kg per animal per day for 300 days. This scheme will promote scientific feed management practices, enhance milk productivity, and improve the income of milk producers. Adequate state funds will be provided for the implementation of this scheme. 84 iv. Supply of Mineral Mixture at subsidized price Healthy heifer calves are the foundation of future milk production. With the objective of improving the growth, reproductive performance, and lifetime productivity of dairy animals, mineral mixture will be supplied for one year at 50 per cent subsidy to 50,000 heifer calves. A sum of Rs.2.76 crore will be allocated for the implementation of this scheme. 88.

Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Inland fisheries and aquaculture have emerged as vital pillars of Tamil Nadu's rural economy, contributing significantly to food security, nutritional well -being, employment generation and sustainable livelihoods. The State is endowed with an extensive network of inland water resources, covering about 3.85 lakh hectares , offering immense potential for fisheries development and enhancing the livelihoods of thousands of rural families. i. Enhancement of inland fish production in Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department tanks in Tamil Nadu through fish seed stocking Tamil Nadu has 2 1,608 tanks under the control of the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department. 85 With the objective of increasing inland fish production and enhancing fish productivity in these water bodies, quality fish fingerlings will be stocked at the rate of 2,000 fingerlings per hectare in 5,000 hectares at a cost of Rs.75 lakh. This initiative will ensure the availability of affordable, high -quality protein -rich food for rural communities. ii. Promotion of Fish Culture in Multipurpose Farm Ponds in Tamil Nadu To encourage fish farmers to undertake fish culture in farm ponds, subsidy assistance will be provided for the purchase of essential inputs such as fish fingerlings and feed for 200 farm ponds. This initiative will improve the livelihoods of fish farmers while ensuring the availability of protein -rich food for rural communities. The scheme will be implemented in selected districts at an estimated cost of Rs.80 lakh. 89.

Rural Employment Guarantee and Livelihood Mission Under the Rural Employment Guarantee and Livelihood Mission – Tamil Nadu, planned interventions 86 are being undertaken for natural resource management and water conservation. In addition, agriculture and allied activities such as drought -proofing, land development, desilting of supply channels and irrigation canals, and restoration of traditional water bodies are being carried out to improve groundwater recharge and soil moisture. To strengthen connectivity between farmers and markets in rural areas and facilitate the transportation of agricultural produce, single -layer gravel roads are being laid to unconnected Adi Dravidar habitations, tribal settlements, and hilly areas. During 2026 –27, 12,000 works including farm ponds, new ponds, percolation ponds, water recharge trenches, water recharge shafts, recharge wells, nurseries, tree planting, earthen bunds and stone bunds will be taken up at an estimated cost of Rs.1,500 crore. These initiatives enable them to adopt improved technologies on their farms and earn a sustainable year - round income. i.

During processing of applications received online, the VAO and Revenue Inspector enquire 31 and verify the eligibility and claim of the applicant and recommend to the Tahsildar (SSS) either for approval or rejection. Prior to approval of applications, each application is automatically subjected to data purity exercise by verifying the applications with the available databases such as Civil Registration System, Labour pension, Integrated Financial and Human Resources Management System (IFHRMS) etc., to ascertain their claim. The applications after data purity exercise are sent along with remarks for final disposal by Tahsildar (SSS).

Disaster preparedness saves lives. Resilience must be built through sustained investments in infrastructure and human capacity. items.text: The Tamil Nadu State Disaster Management Plan translates the Policy into a comprehensive framework for action. The State Disaster Management Plan, 2025 adopts a risk-informed development perspective by embedding disaster risk reduction considerations within planning, budgeting and governance processes. Guided by the principle of Build Back Better, the Plan recognizes river basins, watersheds and coastal systems as planning units and moots disaster risk assessment and planning at the Revenue Village level. It adopts an all-hazards, all-phases and all-stakeholders 60 60 approach, addressing both natural and human- induced hazards across the disaster management cycle. items.text: 3.4.1 Preparedness and Capacity Building Tamil Nadu's preparedness framework operates across three interconnected functions- detecting a disaster before it occurs, warning every person in its path and ensuring that trained personnel and communities are ready to act when the disaster occurs. 79 3.4.1.1 Alert Generation The State Emergency Operation Centre collects weather and disaster-related forecasts from designated nodal agencies - Indian Meteorological Department (weather forecasts), Central Water Commission (flood forecasts), Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (tsunami and storm surge forecasts), Geological Survey of India (landslides), National Centre for Seismology (earthquake), Defence Geoinformatics Research Establishment (avalanches and landslides), Forest Survey of India (forest fire), Space Application Centre- Weather Research and Forecasting (weather modeling results) and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (lightning alerts) - which 80 80 provide forecasts, warnings and reports at regular intervals, with frequency increasing during disaster events. In addition, the State receives forecast services from multiple international sources including the European Centre for Medium-range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) based in Europe and The National Centre for Environmental Prediction- Global Forecast System (NCEP-GFS) based in the United States, enabling more accurate and area-specific weather prediction. TNDRRA examines all the above to decide on the alerts that require action. 3.4.1.1.1 Seismic Monitoring Network Timely detection and analysis of seismic activity form an important component of earthquake early warning and preparedness.

items.text: 3.4.7.3 Catalytic Assistance to Drought- prone Districts Persistent water stress and recurring drought conditions in the districts of Sivagangai, 118 118 Ramanathapuram and Virudhunagar have necessitated targeted drought mitigation interventions. The implementation of the programme will commence shortly. 3.4.7.4 Mitigation Scheme for Forest Fire Risk Management Forest fires during the pre-monsoon period from February to April pose a recurring threat to forest ecosystems and biodiversity in Tamil Nadu's hill districts.
