items.text: 3.4.7.6 Scheme for the Mitigation of Coastal Erosion Coastal Erosion poses a significant challenge along several stretches of Tamil Nadu coastline. A 32-year shoreline change analysis undertaken by the National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR) for the period 1990–2022 found that 39 percent of the State's coastline is experiencing varying degrees of erosion, with the highest levels observed in Mayiladuthurai, Chengalpattu and Kanyakumari districts. Based on these findings, 15 socio-economically significant and highly vulnerable hotspots along the coasts of Tiruvallur, Chennai, Chengalpattu, Mayiladuthurai 121 and Kanyakumari have been identified for intervention. The proposed project envisages preparation and implementation of a Shoreline Management Plan combining conventional engineering measures with nature-based solutions tailored to local conditions. The proposal, with an estimated outlay of Rs.225.15 crore, under consideration of Government. 3.5 Special Initiatives 3.5.1 Landslide: Landslide Risk Mitigation Study Heavy rainfall in Tamil Nadu’s hill districts creates recurring landslide risks in the terrain vulnerable to slope failure. LAND ADMINISTRATION The Commissionerate of Land Administration was created and established in the year 1980 abolishing the erstwhile Board of Revenue so as to perform the following functions of Land Administration. Administration of Government Lands (a) Transfer of Government Lands to State Government/ Central Government Departments. Organizational setup The Commissionerate of Land Administration is headed by the Commissioner of Land Administration and assisted by the following State Level Officials.  One Additional/ Joint Commissioner in the cadre of IAS 128 128  Four Joint Commissioners in the cadre of District Revenue Officers  Joint Commissioner (Legal)  Three Chief Accounts Officers  Nine Assistant Commissioners in the cadre of Deputy Collectors 4.1 Land Transfer Government lands are transferred to Central and State Government Departments for implementation of various public infrastructure and welfare projects under the provisions of Revenue Standing Orders (RSO) 23 and 23A. The Government lands are transferred to Central Government Departments on collection of land value under RSO 23, whereas the Government lands are transferred to State Government Departments on free of cost under RSO 23A. 129 To facilitate timely execution of Government projects, powers have been delegated to District Collectors for granting Enter-Upon Permission for unobjectionable Government lands required by Government Departments, irrespective of land value ceiling limit, subject to obtaining No Objection Certificates from the concerned land-owning Departments and adherence to prescribed procedures.

items.text: 4.5 Assignment of free House Site Patta The policy of the Government is to provide decent housing facility, by granting free house- sites or houses to all the houseless poor. Accordingly, free house-site assignment is given to eligible houseless poor persons from the available Government land classified as "Natham Vacant", under the provisions of RSO 21. 140 140 The Revenue Divisional Officers/ District Collectors are empowered under RSO 21(6) to change the classification of various types of unobjectionable Government poramboke lands, where the sufficient lands classified as Natham is not available for the grant of free house site assignment to houseless poor persons. To ensure the women empowerment, the free House sites are assigned in favour of the woman member of the family. As per the existing rules, free house site patta is issued to each eligible family, one cent in Corporation areas (Except Chennai and its belt area), one and half cents in Municipal areas and three cents in rural areas are assigned subject to other conditions. 141 4.6 Special Regularisation Scheme After the formation of this Government, 3,299 free House Site pattas/ e-pattas have been issued to eligible families by regularizing the residential encroachments of people who have been residing for long period on unobjectionable Government poramboke lands. 4.7 Land Administration -Simplification and Digitisation In order to ensure better follow-up and timely action on every application relating to land transfer, land alienation and land exchange, an integrated online system will be developed covering the entire process from receipt of application to issue of final orders.

Reports and recommendations required at different stages will also be obtained through the portal. items.text: The Hon’ble Minister for Revenue and Disaster Management Department who has been allocated the Bhoodan and Gramdan portfolio is the Chairman of the Board. Both officials including, the Member Secretary and non-officials are the members of this Board. Bhoodan lands are granted to a landless poor person for agricultural purposes or to a houseless poor person as a house site or to the Government for community purposes as per Section 19(1) of the Tamil Nadu Bhoodan Yagna Act, 1958. 163 The Government may also, on the recommendation of the State Board, grant any land vested with the Board to any person or institution, for any public purpose, subject to such conditions as deem fit after collecting double the market value of such land as per Section 19(3) of the above-mentioned Act. The Guideline value of these lands has been fixed as “0” (zero), in order to curb the unauthorised sale, transfer, and registration of Bhoodan lands in Tamil Nadu. 5.5 Gramdan The ‘Gramdan’ is a development of the Bhoodan Movement and its special feature is to wholeheartedly gift the ownership of land by the landowners for common possession of a village. 163 162 These lands are being regularized and distributed as per the provisions of the Tamil Nadu Bhoodan Yagna Act, 1958, and Rules, 1959. The Bhoodan Board was established to administer the Bhoodan lands. The Hon’ble Minister for Revenue and Disaster Management Department who has been allocated the Bhoodan and Gramdan portfolio is the Chairman of the Board. Bhoodan lands are granted to a landless poor person for agricultural purposes or to a houseless poor person as a house site or to the Government for community purposes as per Section 19(1) of the Tamil Nadu Bhoodan Yagna Act, 1958. 163 The Government may also, on the recommendation of the State Board, grant any land vested with the Board to any person or institution, for any public purpose, subject to such conditions as deem fit after collecting double the market value of such land as per Section 19(3) of the above-mentioned Act. The Guideline value of these lands has been fixed as “0” (zero), in order to curb the unauthorised sale, transfer, and registration of Bhoodan lands in Tamil Nadu. 5.5 Gramdan The ‘Gramdan’ is a development of the Bhoodan Movement and its special feature is to wholeheartedly gift the ownership of land by the landowners for common possession of a village. 164 164 Gramdan village means any revenue village or villages or parts thereof in which- (i) not less than two-thirds of the number of persons residing and owning lands donated all their lands for Gramdan; or (ii) not less than one-half of the total extent of the lands owned by persons residing in such village or villages or parts thereof donating all their lands for Gramdan, and which the Government may, by notification, declare to be a Gramdan village.

items.text: Tamil Nadu possesses one of the richest traditions of land administration in India. Accurate land records constitute the foundation for secure property rights, transparent governance, effective urban planning, sustainable agricultural development and efficient implementation of welfare programmes. The Department of Survey and Settlement has continuously modernized its functioning by adopting advanced technologies such as Differential Global Positioning System (DGPS), 176 176 Electronic Total Stations (ETS), Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS), drone- based surveys and Geographic Information Systems (GIS-enabled mapping). The Department has achieved significant milestones in digitization of land records, online delivery of citizen services, implementation of the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP), establishment of GIS infrastructure and commencement of pilot implementation of the NAtional geospatial Knowledge-based land Survey of urban HAbitations (NAKSHA). This Policy Note presents the achievements of the Department, the programmes proposed for 177 2026–2027 and the long-term vision for establishing a fully digital, accurate and citizen- centric land administration system in Tamil Nadu. 7.1 Evolution and organization of the Department 7.1.1 Evolution The Department of Survey and Settlement, established in 1858, is one of the oldest technical departments of the Government of Tamil Nadu. The Department is entrusted with conducting land surveys, maintaining cadastral records, implementing settlement operations, preserving land records and supporting numerous Government departments in land acquisition and infrastructure development. 177 176 Electronic Total Stations (ETS), Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS), drone- based surveys and Geographic Information Systems (GIS-enabled mapping).

In order to augment the number of Licensed Surveyors additional survey training, centres will be temporarily established in various districts. 7.14 SETTLEMENT The procedure to determine the assessment and the ownership was known as Land Revenue Settlement. In 1802, the British Government introduced the Permanent Settlement and in the year 1879-80, the Ryotwari Settlement system was 210 210 introduced to assess taxes based on productivity, considering factors like soil type, irrigation and classification. Under this system, farmers (ryots) paid taxes directly to the Government. The Government conducted surveys for the first time, determined classifications, and created patta registries to record ownership. This system lasted for 30 years, after which Re-settlement was implemented. By the time India gained Independence, the Ryotwari Settlement had been implemented in most areas of the former Madras Presidency, except for Estates/Inam Estates/Minor Inam and similar areas. 211 7.15 Abolition of Estates/Inam Estates/ Minor Inams in Tamil Nadu and Introduction of Ryotwari Settlement The main goal was to establish its land rights directly with the ryots and also to reduce the burden of land tax on Ryots (cultivators). To achieve this, the Government enacted various Abolition Acts and introduced Ryotwari settlement. 7.15.1 Ryotwari Settlement in Estates The Tamil Nadu Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, allowed the Government to take over Estates and introduce Ryotwari Settlement.

items.text: To achieve this, the Government enacted various Abolition Acts and introduced Ryotwari settlement. 7.15.1 Ryotwari Settlement in Estates The Tamil Nadu Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, allowed the Government to take over Estates and introduce Ryotwari Settlement. The Act was later repealed on 04.05.2023 as per Government Gazette Notification No.165. 211 210 introduced to assess taxes based on productivity, considering factors like soil type, irrigation and classification. Under this system, farmers (ryots) paid taxes directly to the Government. The Government conducted surveys for the first time, determined classifications, and created patta registries to record ownership. This system lasted for 30 years, after which Re-settlement was implemented. By the time India gained Independence, the Ryotwari Settlement had been implemented in most areas of the former Madras Presidency, except for Estates/Inam Estates/Minor Inam and similar areas. 211 7.15 Abolition of Estates/Inam Estates/ Minor Inams in Tamil Nadu and Introduction of Ryotwari Settlement The main goal was to establish its land rights directly with the ryots and also to reduce the burden of land tax on Ryots (cultivators). To achieve this, the Government enacted various Abolition Acts and introduced Ryotwari settlement. 7.15.1 Ryotwari Settlement in Estates The Tamil Nadu Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, allowed the Government to take over Estates and introduce Ryotwari Settlement. The Act was later repealed on 04.05.2023 as per Government Gazette Notification No.165.

items.text: The Act was later repealed on 04.05.2023 as per Government Gazette Notification No.165. 212 212 7.15.2 Ryotwari Settlement in Inam Estates Inam Estates which were granted to religious, charitable institutions, warriors, Government officers and others without levying land revenue assessment or at concessional rates, were taken over by the Government under the Tamil Nadu Inam Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1963 (Tamil Nadu Act 26/1963) and Ryotwari settlement was introduced. Settlement work was over in all villages taken over under this Act, except in the four villages namely, ArayapuramThattimalPadugai in Papanasam Taluk of Thanjavur District and Chennasandiram, Uliyalam and Thimmasandiram villages in Hosur Taluk of Krishnagiri District. 213 7.15.3 Ryotwari Settlement in Minor Inams Ryotwari Settlement was introduced in all Minor Inams were granted to religious and charitable institutions. This was done under the Tamil Nadu Minor Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1963 (Tamil Nadu Act 30/1963). Settlement work is completed in all villages except the 7 villages namely, Sooriyanarayanapuram in Pattukottai Taluk of Thanjavur District, Marasandiram, Elayasandiram, Bairasandiram in Hosur Taluk of Krishnagiri District and Kazhanivaipatti, Nilayapatti and Karanapatti Villages in Pudukottai District.

items.text: 7.15.4 Ryotwari Settlement in Gudalur Janmam Estates Tamil Nadu Gudalur Janmam Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) 214 214 Act, 1969 (Tamil Nadu Act 24/1969), introduced Ryotwari settlement in Janmam Estates of Gudalur and Pandalur Taluks in the Nilgiris District. The goal was to acquire the rights of Janmies. However, various court cases by way of civil appeals and writ petitions filed in the Hon’ble High Court and Hon’ble Supreme Court by Janmies and leaseholders questioning the inclusion of the entire Act in the 9 th Schedule of the Constitution. The Hon’ble Supreme Court ultimately upheld the inclusion in 2010. So far, 45,101.46 acres of land have been settled. The break up details are tabulated as follows:- 215 Table – 7.1 Sl. items.text: இ[unclear figure]வ.எண்‌-06 நாள்‌- 03.08.2026 பத்திரிக்கைச்செய்தி பிரதம மந்திரி பயிர்க்‌ காப்பீட்டுத்‌ திட்டத்தின்‌ கீழ்‌ 2026-27 ஆம்‌ ஆண்டு காரீப்‌ பருவ பயிர்களைக்‌ காப்பீடு செய்ய விவசாயிகளுக்கு மாவட்ட ஆட்சியர்‌ வேண்டுகோள்‌ தமிழ்நாட்டில்‌ 2026.27 ஆம்‌ ஆண்டில்‌ பிரதம மந்திரி பயிர்க்‌ காப்பீட்டுத்‌ திட்டம்‌ (PMFBY) Kharif பருவத்திற்கான அறிவிக்கை பெறப்பட்டு, திட்டம்‌ செயல்படுத்தப்பட்டு வருகிறது. கோயம்புத்தூர்‌ மாவட்டத்தில்‌ பயிர்க்‌ காப்பீட்டுத்‌ திட்டம்‌ அக்கிரிகல்ச்சர்‌ இன்சூரன்ஸ்‌ கம்பெனி ஆஃப்‌ இந்தியா லிட்‌. காப்பீட்டு நிறுவனம்‌ மூலம்‌ செயல்படுத்தப்படுகிறது. தற்போது காரீப்‌ பருவ சாகுபடி முழுவீச்சில்‌ நடைபெற்று வரும்‌ வேளையில்‌, விவசாயிகள்‌ அறிவிக்கை செய்யப்பட்ட (நெல்‌ I, மக்காச்சோளம்‌ 1, சோளம்‌, உளுந்து, பச்சைப்பயறு, கொள்ளுப்பயறு) பயிர்களைக்‌ காப்பீடு செய்வதற்கான கடைசி தேதி வரை காத்திருக்காமல்‌ முன்னதாகவே காப்பீடு செய்ய கேட்டுக்கொள்ளப்படுகிறது. தற்போது கோயம்புத்தூர்‌ மாவட்டத்தில்‌ காரீப்‌ பருவத்தில்‌

items.text: காப்பீடு செய்யப்படும்‌ பயிர்களான மக்காச்சோளம்‌, சோளம்‌ மற்றும்‌ கொள்ளுப்பயிரினை 16.09.2026 தேதிக்குள்ளும்‌ காப்பீடு செய்ய கேட்டுக்கொள்ளப்படுகின்றனர்‌. பயிர்க்‌ காப்பீட்டுத்‌ தொகையில்‌ விவசாயிகள்‌ 2.0 சதவீதம்‌ மட்டும்‌ காப்பீட்டுக்‌ கட்டணமாக ஏக்கர்‌ ஒன்றிற்கு நெல்‌ பயிருக்கு ரூ.786.யும்‌, மக்காச்சோளத்திற்கு ரூ.740.யும்‌, சோளத்திற்கு ரூ.282.64யும்‌, உளுந்திற்கு ரூ.374.யும்‌, பச்சைப்பயறுக்கு ரூ.374.யும்‌ மற்றும்‌ கொள்ளுப்பயறுக்கு ரூ.238.-யும்‌ மட்டுமே காப்பீட்டுக்‌ கட்டணமாக செலுத்தினால்‌ போதுமானது. எனவே, கார்ப்‌ பருவத்தில்‌ சாகுபடி மேற்கொள்ளும்‌ கடன்‌ பெறும்‌ விவசாயிகள்‌ அறிவிக்கை செய்யப்பட்ட பயிர்களை தொடக்க வேளாண்மை கூட்டுறவுக்‌ கடன்‌ சங்கங்களிலோ , தேசியமயமாக்கப்பட்ட வங்கிகளிலோ, கடன்‌ பெறா விவசாயிகள்‌ பொதுச்‌ சேவை மையங்களிலோ (இ-சேவை மையங்கள்‌) / தேசிய பயிர்க்‌ காப்பீட்டு இணையதளத்தில்‌ உள்ள “விவசாயிகள்‌ கார்னரில்‌” (www.pmfbygovin) நேரிடையாகவோ

The 45" State Level Coordination Committee on Crop Insurance meeting for notifying Rabi Crops during 2019-2020 under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) was held on 6.11.2019 and the Committee accepted to notify the Crops, Districts, Firkas and Revenue Villages for Agricultural and Horticultural Crops, for notification of Insurance Units and publication in the State Gazette. 3. In his letter third read above, the Director of Agriculture, based on recommendation of the 45" State level Co-ordination Committee on Crop Insurance meeting to notify crops during Rabi season, 2019-2020 held on 06.11.2019 under the Chairmanship of Agricultural Production Commissioner and Principal Secretary to Government, Agriculture Department has sent the proposal for notification of Crops, Districts, Firkas, Revenue Villages, Insurance Units and Approved Premium Rates for Agriculture and Horticulture Crops during Rabi, 2019-2020 and requested the Government to issue orders and also publish the notification in the Government Gazette. 4. The Government, after careful examination of the proposal of the Director of Agriculture, accept the same and accordingly notify the Crops, Districts, Firkas, Revenue Villages, insurance units and approved premium rates for Agricultural and Horticultural Crops for the effective implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana during Rabi, 2019-2020 season as detailed in the Annexures , ||, Ul, IV and V to this order. 5.

AN யூ PRADHAN MANTRI FASAL BIMA YOJANA (PMFBY) NOTIFICATION FOR RABI SEASON 2019-2020 ANNEXURE | [G.0.(D).No.256, Agriculture (AP2) Department, Dated: 19.11.2019] Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) will be implemented in all the districts of Tamil Nadu (except Chennai) during Rabi, 2019 - 2020 season as per the Revised Operational Guidelines of Government of India (Government of India Letter No.13015/03/2016—Credit II, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Department of Agriculture, Co-operation & Farmers Welfare, Krishi Bhavan, New Delhi, dated 28.09.2018). OBJECTIVES OF PRADHAN MANTRI FASAL BIMA YOJANA: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana aims at supporting sustainable production in agriculture by way of- a) Providing financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of unforeseen events. b) Stabilizing the income of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming. c) Encouraging farmers to adopt innovative and modern Agriculture practices. d) Ensuring flow of credit to the agriculture sector, which will, contribute to food security, crop diversification and enhancing growth and competitiveness of agriculture sector besides protecting farmers from production risks. COVERAGE OF FARMERS:

items.text: COVERAGE OF FARMERS: All farmers including share croppers and tenant farmers growing the notified crops in the notified areas are eligible for coverage. e Compulsory for Loanee farmers. உ Optional for Non - Loanee farmers. COVERAGE OF RISKS AND EXCLUSIONS: The following stages of the crop and Risks leading to crop loss are covered under the scheme: 1. PREVENTED SOWING/ PLANTING / GERMINATION RISK - If Insured area is prevented from sowing / planting / germination due to deficit rainfall or adverse seasonal weather conditions. 2. STANDING CROP (SOWING TO HARVESTING) - Comprehensive risk insurance is provided to cover yield losses due to non - preventable risks viz. Drought, dry spells, flood, inundation, wide spread pests and diseases, landslides, fire due to natural causes, lightening, storm, hailstorm and cyclone. V. 3. LOCALIZED CALAMITIES - Loss/damage to notified insured crops resulting trom occurrence ot identified localized risks of hailstorm, landslide, inundation (except Paddy, Sugarcane), cloudburst and natural fire due to lightening affecting isolated farms in the notified area. 4. ON ACCOUNT PAYMENT OF CLAIMS DUE TO MID-SEASON ADVERSITY - Insurance cover will be provided to the farmers to provide immediate relief in case of adverse seasonal conditions viz. floods, prolonged dry spells, severe drought etc., during the crop season wherein expected yield during the season is likely to be less than 50% of Normal Yield. 5.

items.text: SUM INSURED: The Scale of Finance approved by State Level Technical Committee for the year 2019-2020 and notified vide G.O.(Ms).No.78, Agriculture (AP2) department, dated 11.04.2019 should be adopted as Sum Insured for the crops notified during Rabi, 2019-2020 season as per Para No.12.1 of the Revised Operational Guidelines of Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana .The Sum Insured will be same for both loanee and non-loanee farmers. CLUSTER-WISE, DISTRICT-WISE APPROVED PREMIUM RATE AND THE PREMIUM RATE FOR FARMERS FOR RABI, 2019-2020 SEASON As approved in the tender agreement, the crop-wise, cluster-wise, district-wise approved premium rate and the premium rate for farmers are notified as per Annexure ||| for Rabi, 2019-2020 Season (rate of Insurance Charges payable by the farmer is 1.5% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate, whichever is less for all food grain (Cereals, Millets & Pulses) & Oilseed crops and 5% of sum insured or actuarial rate whichever is less for Annual Commercial / Annual Horticultural crops and Perennial Horticultural Crops). NOTIFICATION OF THRESHOLD YIELD FOR THE NOTIFIED UNITS IN THE HIERARCHY AS PER NOTIFICATION The Insurance Companies have to calculate and upload the threshold yield at Insurance unit level on the National Crop Insurance Portal. The Insurance Companies shall also furnish the Threshold yield to Government after receipt of Crop Cutting Experiment Yield data from Department of Economics and Statistics.

XIV. SEASONALITY DISCIPLINE FOR PREVENTED SOWING / GERMINATION RISK The District Level Monitoring Committee under the Chairmanship of District Collector is authorized to fix the seasonality discipline for prevented sowing / failed sowing by adopting the conditions formulated in the Revised Operational Guidelines. The Insurance Companies are also directed to make an appeal to invoke prevented sowing / germination risk only within prescribed period with proper evidence (i.e.) not later than 15 days from cut off date for enrolment of farmer for prevented sowing (Para 21.3.2.4 of Operational Guidelines) and not later than 3 weeks after peak sowing period in case of germination risk (G.O.(Ms).No.293, Agriculture (AP6) Department, dated 12.09.2016). The Insurance Companies shall also not make an appeal at any date later than the timeline fixed or after the receipt of yield data from the Department of Economics and Statistics. In case, this provision is not invoked by the District Level Monitoring Committee / District Level Joint Committee, Insurance Company may escalate the same in writing to State Government within the stipulated timeline (Para 21.3.2.5. of Operational Guidelines).

items.text: The principal Secretary/ Commissioner of Revenue Administration has stated as follows: i. The Director, Horticulture has stated that the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) norms and guidelines are specified in the Government Order first read above, there is no limitation on land holding to the individual farmer, to claim input subsidy for > 33% affected Horticultural Crops under SDRF in the event of natural calamities. ii. He has also been informed that during the Drought year (2015-16) and in the Gaja cyclone (2018) the input subsidy was restricted to 2 Ha. of the affected area for the individual farmer. However, during Nivar, Burevi and the unseasonal rain in January 2021, input subsidy was extended to the affected area without any limitation. ii. He has been further informed that as on 15.12.2021, affected Horticulture crops due to the heavy downpour of North East Monsoon (NEM) was 1795.09 Ha which has been covered under the net sown area. iv. Further, the Director of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has stated that the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) norms and guidelines are specified in the Government Order first read above, in which no limitations on land holding to the individual farmers to claim input subsidy for the affected Agricultural crops under State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) in the event of Natural Calamities. 5 However, during the Drought year (2015-16) and in the Gaja cyclone (2018) the input subsidy claim was restricted to 2 ha of the affected area for individual farmers.

items.text: The fisheries sector is a key driver of the State's economy, contributing significantly to food and nutritional security, employment, exports and rural livelihoods. The sector sustains 10.84 lakh marine fisherfolk and 2.40 lakh inland fisherfolk (2025-26), with the State achieving an annual fish production of 10.24 lakh MT 1 (2025-26). Recognising the sector's strategic importance, the Government of Tamil Nadu is committed to its sustainable and inclusive development through scientific 1 Department of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare, GoTN 2 2 management of fisheries resources, conservation of marine and inland ecosystems, modernisation of fisheries infrastructure, promotion of sustainable fishing and aquaculture, enhancement of value addition and market access and comprehensive welfare and social security measures. The Government also remains steadfast in safeguarding the traditional fishing rights and livelihood interests of fishermen while ensuring that the sector continues to be a catalyst for economic growth, employment generation and rural prosperity. The Government of Tamil Nadu is committed to promote Blue economy while improving the livelihood of fishers. 1.1. Global Fisheries Scenario The fisheries sector has emerged as one of the fastest growing food production sectors globally, making a significant contribution to 3 3 food and nutritional security, employment, livelihoods and international trade. India has established itself as a global leader in fisheries, supported by its vast marine and inland water resources, favourable climatic conditions and rapidly expanding aquaculture sector. During 2025–26, India ranked as the second -largest fish-producing country in the world and the largest producer in inland capture fisheries, accounting 8% of global fish production 2. This achievement reflects the country's growing prominence and expanding role in the global fisheries economy.

items.text: During 2025–26, India ranked as the second -largest fish-producing country in the world and the largest producer in inland capture fisheries, accounting 8% of global fish production 2. This achievement reflects the country's growing prominence and expanding role in the global fisheries economy. 1.2. Overview of the Fisheries Sector in Tamil Nadu Tamil Nadu occupies a prominent position in the fisheries sector owing to its rich and 2 Government of India – Press Information Bureau,2026 4 4 diverse marine and inland fishery resources. With the second longest coastline in the country, the State possesses immense potential for marine fisheries, inland fisheries, coastal aquaculture and mariculture. During 2025 -26, Tamil Nadu recorded a total fish production of 10.24 lakh MT, comprising 7.24 lakh MT from marine fisheries and 3.00 lakh MT from inland fisheries. The State ranked second in marine fish production in the country. Fish and fishery products continue to be one of the major export commodities of the State. During 2025 -26, Tamil Nadu exported 1.52 lakh MT of fish and fishery products, generating valuable foreign exchange earnings of Rs.7,660.48 crore3. 3 Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) 5 5 The State is also endowed with nearly 3.85 lakh hectares of inland water resources, comprising rivers, reservoirs, tanks, lakes and ponds, besides about 56,000 hectares of brackish water resources consisting of estuaries, backwaters, lagoons and creeks. These diverse aquatic ecosystems provide substantial opportunities for sustainable fisheries, aquaculture and livelihood generation . 1.3.

Brackish Water Fisheries Tamil Nadu possesses approximately 56,000 hectares of brackish water resources, accounting for nearly 4 percent age of the country's total brackish water area. These ecologically rich ecosystems serve as important breeding, nursery and feeding grounds for a wide range of finfish and shellfish species, while also offering immense potential for sustainable fisheries and aquaculture.

items.text: These ecologically rich ecosystems serve as important breeding, nursery and feeding grounds for a wide range of finfish and shellfish species, while also offering immense potential for sustainable fisheries and aquaculture. Major brackish water ecosystems such as Pazhaverkadu, Ennore, Adyar, Muttukadu, 11 11 Pichavaram, Kollidam, Muthupet and the estuaries of Punnakayal, Manakudi and Thengapattanam provide significant opportunities for the development of environmentally sustainable coastal aquaculture and mariculture. 1.6. Coastal Aquaculture and Mariculture Coastal aquaculture and mariculture have assumed increasing importance in recent years owing to the plateauing of marine capture fisheries and rising operational costs in the fishing sector. These activities complement marine fisheries by enhancing fish production, creating employment opportunities, supporting livelihood diversification and contributing substantially to export earnings. Shrimp farming remains the dominant coastal aquaculture activity in Tamil Nadu, while open-sea cage farming of marine finfishes and 12 12 seaweed cultivation have emerged as important mariculture enterprises. With its favourable coastline and coastal ecosystems, the State offers considerable potential for the expansion of sustainable coastal aquaculture and mariculture. 2. VISION “To sustainably conserve, develop and manage the fisheries resources of Tamil Nadu through scientific, responsible and climate -resilient approaches, ensuring food and nutritional security, enhancing fish production and value addition, promoting economic prosperity and employment generation, safeguarding the traditional rights and livelihoods of fishermen and improving the quality of life of fishermen and fish farmers.” 13 13 3.

items.text: MISSION To achieve maintainable growth of the fisheries sector by promoting responsible fisheries and aquaculture, enhancing fish production and productivity, strengthening infrastructure and value chains, ensuring safety and social security of fishing communities, fostering technological innovation and research, and creating diversified livelihood opportunities for inclusive socio-economic development. 4. POLICY PRIORITIES The Government shall pursue the following policy priorities: i. Protecting the rights and livelihoods of fishermen by safeguarding their traditional fishing rights and strengthening social security and welfare measures. 14 14 ii. Promoting sustainable fisheries and aquaculture through scientific management, conservation and optimum utilisation of marine, inland and brackish water resources while ensuring ecological sustainability. iii. Enhancing fish production and productivity by expanding inland aquaculture, mariculture and other sustainable fish production systems, improving fish seed availability and encouraging adoption of modern technologies. iv. Strengthening fisheries infrastructure and value chains through the creation and modernisation of fishing harbours, fish landing centres, Government fish farms, hatcheries, cold chain facilities, processing units, value addition and market linkages. 15 15 v. Improving income and employment opportunities by promoting entrepreneurship, diversified livelihood activities, rural employment and economic empowerment of fishermen, fish farmers and fisherwomen. vi. Conserving fishery resources through stock assessment, stock enhancement, scientific resource monitoring and effective enforcement of fisheries laws and regulations. vii. Promoting exports and value realisation by improving fish quality, hygiene, traceability and compliance with international standards, while expanding access to domestic and global markets. viii. Building human capital and institutional capacity through research, innovation, technology adoption, skill development and continuous capacity 16 16 building of fishermen, fish farmers and department personnel. ix.

Strengthening governance and service delivery by leveraging e -Governance, digital technologies and transparent monitoring systems for efficient implementation of developmental and welfare programmes. 5. ADMINISTRATIVE SETUP The Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department is headed by the Director, who is undertaking overall planning, implementation and monitoring of fisheries development, resource management and welfare programmes across the State. The Director also functions as the Managing Director of the Tamil Nadu Fisheries Development Corporation (TNFDC) Limited, the Functional Registrar of all Fishermen and Fisherwomen Co-operative Societies, including 17 17 the Tamil Nadu State Apex Fisheries Co-operative Federation (TAFCOFED) Limited and the Member Secretary of the Tamil Nadu Fishermen Welfare Board (TNFWB). These institutions work in close coordination to implement developmental, commercial and welfare initiatives aimed at ensuring the sustainable growth of the fisheries sector and improving the livelihoods of fishermen and fish farmers across Tamil Nadu. Key divisions of the department DoF&FW TNFDC TNFWB MEWTAFCO FED FHPC 18 18 The major activities of the Department are aligned with policies of the Government. The Government is promoting the welfare of fishermen through developing marine , inland fisheries, coastal aquaculture, mariculture activities, conserving fishery resources and creating essential fisheries infrastructure. 6.

The Government adopts an integrated approach to marine fisheries development by balancing resource conservation with livelihood security, infrastructure development and welfare measures. Sustainable utilisation of marine resources, stock enhancement, promotion of responsible fishing practices, disaster preparedness, fishermen safety and expansion of export-oriented fisheries continue to be the key focus areas of the Government. Tamil Nadu has been a pioneer in implementing several path -breaking fisheries development and fishermen welfare initiatives, many of which have served as models for other States. The Government has consistently expanded the scope and scale of welfare measures to improve the socio- economic conditions of marine fishing communities. During 2025-26, an amount of Rs .729.85 crore was 20 20 sanctioned under various welfare schemes benefiting marine fisherfolk, as detailed in Table – 1 of the annexure. Protection of Traditional Fishing Rights of Tamil Nadu Fishermen The Palk Bay region, comprising the districts of Nagapattinam, Tiruvarur, Thanjavur Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram and supports 2,478 mechanised fishing boats, 33 33 10,559 motorised fishing crafts and 550 non - motorised fishing crafts, with a fisherfolk population of about 2.09 lakh living in 286 fishing villages. Nearly 80,000 fishermen directly depend on fishing for their livelihood. Protecting the traditional fishing rights and livelihood of Tamil Nadu fishermen, particularly those operating in the Palk Bay, continues to be one of the foremost priorities of the Government. Fishing communities in the Palk Bay region have traditionally depended on these waters for their livelihood. However, frequent apprehension of fishermen and seizure of fishing boats by the Sri Lankan Navy on allegations of crossing the International Maritime Boundary Line (IMBL) have caused considerable hardship and insecurity among the fishing community. The Government has, therefore, consistently pursued legal, diplomatic and administrative measures to safeguard the interests of 34 34 Tamil Nadu fishermen and secure a permanent solution to this persistent issue. 6.2.1 Efforts to Safeguard Traditional Fishing Rights through Retrieval of Katchatheevu The Government of Tamil Nadu has consistently maintained that the restoration of the traditional fishing rights of Tamil Nadu fishermen in the Palk Bay requires the retrieval of Katchatheevu, which was ceded to Sri Lanka in 1974.

items.text: 6.2.2 Efforts for the Release of Apprehended Fishermen and Fishing Boats The Government has been consistently pursuing the release of Tamil Nadu fishermen and their fishing boats with the Government of India. The Hon'ble Chief Minister has repeatedly taken up the matter with the Ministry of External Affairs and the Hon'ble Prime Minister, besides 35 35 raising the issue during the 11 th Governing Council Meeting of NITI Aayog held on 11.06.2026, seeking urgent intervention for securing the release of apprehended fishermen and fishing boats. Between 01.01.2021 to 28.08.2026, 1,691 Tamil Nadu fishermen were apprehended by the Sri Lankan Navy. Of these, 1,653 fishermen have been released and repatriated. Continuous efforts are being made to secure the release of the remaining 38 fishermen and 26 9 fishing boats presently under the custody of the Sri Lankan Government. 6.2.3 India–Sri Lanka Joint Working Group on Fisheries The India –Sri Lanka Joint Working Group (JWG) on fisheries serves as an important bilateral mechanism for addressing the issues 36 36 faced by fishermen of both countries. The JWG facilitates discussions on the release and repatriation of apprehended fishermen and fishing boats, formulation of maritime protocols and adoption of a humanitarian approach in dealing with fishermen detained on either side. Six rounds of the Joint Working Group meetings have been held so far. The 6 th Joint Working Group meeting, held at Colombo on 29 .10.2024, reviewed the challenges faced by fishermen from both countries and reaffirmed the commitment to ensure the early release and repatriation of Tamil Nadu fishermen and their fishing boats.

The Government continues to urge the Central Government to facilitate the reconvening of the JWG. 3737 6.3. Fishing Regulation and Law Enforcement Sustainable development of the marine fisheries sector requires effective regulation, conservation of fishery resources and strict enforcement of fisheries laws. The Government has therefore strengthened monitoring and surveillance mechanisms to ensure responsible fishing practices, prevent illegal and destructive fishing, maintain law and order at sea and enhance coastal security. 6.3.1 Registration of Fishing Vessels To facilitate effective monitoring of fishing operations and strengthen coastal security, all fishing vessels operating in the State are registered through the ReALCraft online portal. A total of 5,0 45 mechanised fishing boats, 36,489 motorised traditional crafts and 3838 2,848 non-motorised traditional crafts have been registered online (up to 30.08.2026). 6.3.2 Marine Enforcement Wing An exclusive Marine Enforcement Wing (MEW) has been established in the Department to enforce the Tamil Nadu Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1983 and its Rules, besides addressing inter-sectoral conflicts and law and order issues arising from fishing activities. The wing comprises 112 personnel, including 92 police personnel. The Marine Enforcement Wing undertakes regular sea patrols to enforce fishing regulations, prevent illegal and destructive fishing practices, curb the use of banned fishing gear and gather intelligence relating to anti- social activities.

items.text: The wing comprises 112 personnel, including 92 police personnel. The Marine Enforcement Wing undertakes regular sea patrols to enforce fishing regulations, prevent illegal and destructive fishing practices, curb the use of banned fishing gear and gather intelligence relating to anti- social activities. Information collected during patrols is shared with the Indian Coast Guard 39 39 and local police authorities for appropriate follow-up action. The Government proposes to strengthen this wing to safeguard the interests of the fishermen and coastal communities. 6.4. Disaster Preparedness, Rescue and Rehabilitation Ensuring the safety and security of fishermen at sea is one of the foremost priorities of the Government. The Department has established a comprehensive Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for disaster preparedness and emergency response, comprising dissemination of weather advisories, round- the-clock communication systems, coordinated search and rescue operations and timely rehabilitation measures during natural calamities and adverse weather conditions. 40 40 6.4.1 Measures for Communication and Safety of Fishermen at Sea To ensure continuous communication between shore stations and fishing vessels, communication infrastructure has been established across all 14 coastal districts . A Central Control Room functioning round -the- clock at the Office of the Director of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare coordinates dissemination of weather warnings and emergency communication with fishermen and security agencies. 6.4.1.1 Installation of Transponders in Fishing Boats To enhance safety and enable real -time tracking of fishing vessels, Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) developed transponders are being installed in mechanised fishing boats. These transponders facilitate communication and monitoring of fishing vessels 41 41 up to 200 nautical miles and enable timely assistance during emergencies.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: These transponders facilitate communication and monitoring of fishing vessels 41 41 up to 200 nautical miles and enable timely assistance during emergencies. Government of India has sanctioned Rs.18.01 crore for i nstallation of transponders in 4,997 mechanised fishing boats, of which 3,884 boats have already been fitted. Installation in the remaining boats is under progress. In addition, installation of 7,373 transponders in motorised fishing crafts is in progress under PMMSY. 6.4.1.2. Supply of Satellite Phones (PMMSY scheme) Satellite phones are being provided to deep-sea fishing vessels to strengthen communication and improve fishermen safety , while operating in offshore waters. During 2025-26, sanction has been accorded for the supply of 500 satellite phones under PMMSY , of 42 42 which 169 satellite phones have been supplied and scheme is in progress. 6.4.1.3. Easing of Search and Rescue of stranded boats and fishermen In order to facilitate the ease of immediate rescue of fishermen/boats stranded at sea due to adverse weather condition , engine failure, boat collisions or other marine emergencies, the Government have issued orders in July-2026, by authorizing coastal District Collectors to meet expenditure towards boat hire charge, remuneration to fishermen engaged in rescue operations and other admissible incidental expenses for search and rescue operations under Revolving Fund for Disaster Response (RFDR). 43 43 6.4.2 Relief Assistance for damaged fishing boats/fishing implements/huts To provide immediate relief to fishermen whose boats, fishing implements or houses are damaged due to unforeseen incidents, the Government has established a revolving fund for all 14 coastal districts.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: 43 43 6.4.2 Relief Assistance for damaged fishing boats/fishing implements/huts To provide immediate relief to fishermen whose boats, fishing implements or houses are damaged due to unforeseen incidents, the Government has established a revolving fund for all 14 coastal districts. During 2026 -27 (up to July-2026), a sum of Rs. 51,250/- has been released as relief assistance for three fishermen families. 6.4.3 Role of Fishermen d uring Natural Calamities Fishermen play a vital role in disaster response during floods and other natural calamities. The Department coordinates the deployment of fishermen, fishing boats and essential equipment to assist Government agencies in rescue operations. During the North- 44 44 East Monsoon of 2025 and “Ditwah” Cyclone, 158 fishermen along with 79 fishing boats were deployed as a precautionary measure to assist rescue operations in vulnerable areas. 6.5 Marine Fishery Resource Enhancement 6.5.1 Deployment of Artificial Reefs (PMMSY scheme) Artificial reefs are deployed to conserve and enhance marine fishery resources , by providing breeding and nursery habitats for marine organisms, improving juvenile fish survival and increasing fish production. They also discourage bottom trawling in nearshore waters. Under PMMSY for the year 2024 -25, deployment of 217 units of artificial reefs at a cost of Rs. 62.27 crore in 43 fishing villages of Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram and 45 45 Nagapattinam districts have been completed by July-2026. 6.5.2. Sea Ranching Declining marine fish stocks, particularly in nearshore waters, necessitate scientific interventions for resource enhancement and long-term sustainability.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: 6.5.2. Sea Ranching Declining marine fish stocks, particularly in nearshore waters, necessitate scientific interventions for resource enhancement and long-term sustainability. Sea ranching is an important resource conservation strategy involving the release of hatchery produced juveniles of commercially important marine species into their natural habitat to replenish depleted fish stocks. The Department has already deployed artificial reefs along the Tamil Nadu coast to enhance marine biodiversity and create suitable habitats for fish aggregation. Sea ranching of economically important finfish and shellfish species is being undertaken in these artificial 46 46 reef locations to improve stock enhancement and maximise ecological benefits. The programme will be expanded in a phased manner across coastal districts through stocking of commercially important candidate species, in convergence with artificial reef deployment and habitat restoration programmes. The initiative is expected to improve marine fish stock abundance, enhance catch rates, strengthen ecosystem resilience and directly benefit coastal fishers across the State. 6.6. Conservation of Sea Turtles To protect endangered sea turtles and their nesting habitats, installation of Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) has been made mandatory in trawl nets. Fishing is also prohibited within 5 nautical miles of identified nesting and breeding grounds from 1 st January to 30th April every year. 47 47 A Nodal Task Force comprising of Fisheries, Forest Department and Costal Security Group periodically reviews conservation measures. Under PMMSY and State scheme for the year 2025 -26, a total of 2,663 TEDs have been distributed and installed in trawl nets. 7. COASTAL AQUACULTURE AND MARICULTURE The Government is promoting coastal aquaculture and mariculture as important growth drivers for increasing fish production, enhancing exports, generating employment and diversifying the livelihoods of coastal communities.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: 7. COASTAL AQUACULTURE AND MARICULTURE The Government is promoting coastal aquaculture and mariculture as important growth drivers for increasing fish production, enhancing exports, generating employment and diversifying the livelihoods of coastal communities. Sustainable development of these sectors, supported by scientific planning, appropriate regulation and modern technologies, will play a crucial role in augmenting the State's fisheries economy. 48 48 7.1. Coastal Aquaculture Coastal aquaculture in Tamil Nadu has evolved from a traditional activity into a commercially important sector. The introduction of Litopenaeus vannamei (White Leg Shrimp) in 2008 has significantly enhanced shrimp production owing to its rapid growth, higher productivity and adaptability to diverse farming conditions. During 2025-26, Tamil Nadu produced 41,000 MT of shrimp, accounting for an important share of the national production of 13.74 lakh MT and ranked 5 th among shrimp - producing States 4. The State presently has 2,418 shrimp farms covering 4,609.89 hectares and 80 registered shrimp hatcheries. 4 Marine Products Export Development Authority 49 49 Regulatory guidelines governing white leg shrimp farming outside the jurisdiction of the Coastal Aquaculture Authority have been revised in response to the requirements of farmers. To support long -term growth, scientific mapping and assessment of coastal resources will be undertaken for the creation of dedicated Aquazones. The proposed study will identify suitable coastal lands, including Government poramboke lands and salt lands proposed to be acquired, for the development of aquaculture farms, hatcheries, nurseries, feed mills, processing units and cold -chain infrastructure.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The proposed study will identify suitable coastal lands, including Government poramboke lands and salt lands proposed to be acquired, for the development of aquaculture farms, hatcheries, nurseries, feed mills, processing units and cold -chain infrastructure. The Department also proposes to adopt the successful Chilika Lake model of community - based brackish water fisheries management and develop a comprehensive Geographical Information System (GIS) based digital inventory of coastal and brackish water resources to facilitate scientific planning, 50 50 resource assessment and sustainable expansion of the sector. 7.2. Mariculture 7.2.1 Seaweed Culture Seaweeds are a valuable marine bioresource with high nutritional value and wide ranging applications in the food, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, cosmetic, agricultural and bio-energy sectors. In Tamil Nadu, seaweed cultivation has emerged as an important alternative livelihood activity, particularly for coastal fisherwomen, while also contributing to the growth of the blue economy. Tamil Nadu possesses favourable coastal conditions for large -scale seaweed cultivation and has a tradition of seaweed collection spanning over five decades. The commercial cultivation of Kappaphycus alvarezii, introduced 51 51 in 1995, has provided a sustainable supplementary source of income to coastal communities. At present, nearly 2,000 families are engaged in seaweed farming across the coastal districts of Nagapattinam, Thanjavur, Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi and Kanniyakumari . During 2025-26, the State produced 18,240.45 MT 5 of seaweed, retaining its position as the leading seaweed producing State in the country.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: During 2025-26, the State produced 18,240.45 MT 5 of seaweed, retaining its position as the leading seaweed producing State in the country. Tamil Nadu is also home to more than 20 seaweed processing industries, reflecting the growing importance of the sector. To further expand seaweed cultivation, Fisheries Co-operative Societies will be identified and provided subsidy assistance for establishing seaweed rafts and monoline culture units in suitable coastal districts, along with support for essential farming inputs. The Department also 5 Department of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare, GoTN 52 52 proposes to import high yielding and climate resilient seaweed germplasm through the TNFDC to overcome productivity stagnation in the existing Kappaphycus stock and enhance farm productivity. A phased action plan for enhanced seaweed production will be implemented with the objective of doubling the State's seaweed production in the next five years . Species diversification will also be promoted by encouraging the cultivation of commercially important seaweeds such as Gracilaria, Gelidiella, Hypnea, Ulva and Sargassum species. 7.2.2 Establishment of Multipurpose Seaweed Park To unlock the full potential of the seaweed sector and establish an integrated value chain from seed production to processing and 53 53 marketing, the Government has accorded administrative sanction for Rs.127.71 crore towards the establishment of a Multipurpose Seaweed Park in Ramanathapuram and Pudukkottai districts. The project comprises: • Hub-I: Seaweed Seed Production Park at Valamavur, Ramanathapuram District . • Hub-II:

items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The project comprises: • Hub-I: Seaweed Seed Production Park at Valamavur, Ramanathapuram District . • Hub-II: Seaweed Processing Park at Gandarvakottai, Pudukkottai District. • Spoke infrastructure in villages with high seaweed production potential. While an estimated annual industrial demand is 1,15,150 MT, the current production is only 18,240.45 MT . The Seaweed Park will address the critical shortage of quality planting material by multiplying high yielding germplasm sourced both locally and internationally and supplying it to seaweed farmers. Industrial plots under Hub -II will be leased to private 54 54 entrepreneurs for processing, value addition and product development. To strengthen farmer participation, three Fish Farmers Producer Organisations (FFPOs) have already been formed through Cluster Based Business Organisations (CBBOs) for organised seaweed production. On completion, the project is expected to produce 49,000 MT of seaweed over a period of three years, generate employment for local fishers and act as a preferred destination for investment. 7.2.3 Open Sea Cage Culture Open Sea Cage Culture is an environmentally sustainable mariculture technology for farming marine species such as Cobia, Asian Seabass, Pompano and Lobster in floating cages installed in coastal waters. The technology supplements marine capture 55 55 fisheries, enhances seafood production and provides an alternative source of livelihood to coastal fishing communities. Open sea cage culture has been promoted through various schemes. The Department envisages a phased expansion of cage farming by next five years through strengthening seed production and supply, promoting cluster -based cage farming, providing capacity building to fish farmers.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Open sea cage culture has been promoted through various schemes. The Department envisages a phased expansion of cage farming by next five years through strengthening seed production and supply, promoting cluster -based cage farming, providing capacity building to fish farmers. 7.3 Policy Framework for Brackish Water Aquaculture and Mariculture With growing interest from entrepreneurs and investors, the Government proposes to formulate a comprehensive Brackish water Aquaculture Policy and Mariculture Policy through extensive stakeholder consultations and expert inputs. The policy framework will provide a clear roadmap for the sustainable development of the sector by establishing transparent 56 56 regulatory mechanisms, streamlining approvals, promoting modern technologies and strengthening environmental and biosecurity safeguards. The proposed policies will facilitate scientific allocation and leasing of suitable coastal lands and water areas, promote the planned development of Aquazones, mariculture parks, hatcheries, cage farming and seaweed cultivation and create an enabling ecosystem for private investment and innovation. The initiative is expected to enhance investor confidence, accelerate sustainable sectoral growth , direct and indirect livelihood opportunities. 8. INLAND FISHERIES SECTOR The inland fisheries sector plays a pivotal role in enhancing food and nutritional security, improving rural livelihoods and generating 57 57 employment. The Government is committed to developing an ecologically sustainable, economically viable and socially inclusive inland fisheries sector. The key focus areas of inland fisheries development include scientific assessment and sustainable management of inland fishery resources, conservation of indigenous fish species, expansion of aquaculture, promotion of scientific stocking of fish seed in suitable water bodies, development of ornamental fisheries and recreational fisheries, creation of rural employment through innovative fish culture practices, strengthening fisheries education and skill development and promoting value addition to enhance domestic consumption. 58 58 8.1.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: 58 58 8.1. Inland Fisheries Activities The Department implements a comprehensive range of developmental, technical and extension activities to promote sustainable inland fisheries and aquaculture across the State. The major activities include: i. Promotion of Inland Fisheries through District Fish Farmers Development Agencies (DFFDA): District Fish Farmers Development Agencies have been established in all districts, except Chennai, to provide technical guidance, register fish farms and fish seed farms and promote scientific aquaculture practices. ii. Scientific Management of Reservoir and Tank Fisheries: Fisheries in reservoirs and irrigation tanks are managed through 59 59 licensing, share fishing and leasing in accordance with Government policy, with priority accorded to Inland Fishermen and Fisherwomen Co-operative Societies, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes engaged in fishing activities. iii. Production and Supply of Quality Fish Seed: The Department operates Government fish seed production and rearing centres while encouraging private investment to ensure timely availability of quality fish seed for aquaculture development. iv. Promotion of Species Diversification: Fast growing and high-value species such as Amur Carp, Jayanti Rohu, GIF Tilapia, Murrel, Pearl spot and Calbasu are 60 60 being promoted to enhance productivity and diversify aquaculture. The Department also proposes to establish hatcheries for Pacu and freshwater prawn to strengthen seed production and support future expansion of inland aquaculture. v. Strengthening Fish Seed Infrastructure: New fish seed farms are being established and existing Government farms are upgraded to increase the production and timely supply of quality fish seed across the State. vi. Promotion of Fish Feed Production: The establishment of private fish feed mills is being encouraged to ensure the availability 61 61 of scientifically formulated quality feed for cultured fish species. vii.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Promotion of Fish Feed Production: The establishment of private fish feed mills is being encouraged to ensure the availability 61 61 of scientifically formulated quality feed for cultured fish species. vii. Promotion of Cage Culture: Cage farming has been introduced in selected reservoirs to improve fish production and productivity. At present, cage culture is being practised in five reservoirs (Krishnagiri, Chittar, Anaimaduvu, Bhavanisagar and Sathanur) in Tamil Nadu. viii. Fish Seed Stocking in Inland Water Bodies: Fish seed stocking programmes are being implemented in rivers, reservoirs and Panchayat tanks to augment fish stocks and improve inland fish production. ix. Adoption of Advanced Aquaculture Technologies: Modern production systems such as 62 62 Biofloc and Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS) are being promoted to maximise fish production with efficient utilisation of limited water resources. x. Strengthening Fish Marketing: Hygienic fish markets, fish kiosks, insulated vehicles and cold -chain infrastructure are being established to improve fish handling, minimise post-harvest losses and enhance market access. xi. Capacity Building and Extension: Regular training programmes, exposure visits and extension activities are organised to strengthen the technical capacity of fish farmers, entrepreneurs and department personnel and facilitate 63 63 the adoption of modern aquaculture technologies. 8.2. Promotion of Fish Culture The Government envisages increasing the State's inland fish production from 3.00 lakh MT6 in 2025-26 to its potential of 4.50 lakh MT over the next five years , through scientific management and optimum utilisation of all suitable inland water resources.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: This will be achieved by improving fish seed availability, enhancing stocking density, promoting scientific aquaculture practices and strengthening the capacity of fish farmers. 8.2.1. Enhancing Fish Production in Riverine Systems Tamil Nadu has 17 river basins, comprising the Cauvery as the major basin, 13 medium and 3 minor river basins, which offer considerable 6 Department of Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare, GoTN 64 64 scope for inland fisheries development. To conserve native fish diversity, enhance fish stocks and improve the livelihoods of inland fishing communities, the Department will undertake river ranching by releasing quality fingerlings of indigenous fish species in suitable river stretches. The programme envisages stocking of fingerlings in 2,000 km of river stretches, with an estimated additional fish production of 400 MT. 8.2.2. Enhancing Fish Production in Reservoirs Reservoir fisheries constitute one of the major inland fishery resources of the State. At present, the Department manages fisheries in 63 reservoirs covering 56,782 hectares, where fish production is supported through regular 65 65 stocking of quality fingerlings produced in Government fish seed farms. To further enhance reservoir productivity, additional reservoirs under the Water Resources Department will be brought under organised fisheries management. Scientific stocking of advanced fingerlings, improved fisheries management practices and habitat enhancement measures are expected to increase fish production by 600 MT annually. To ensure uniformity, minimise litigation, safeguard the interests of traditional fishing communities and promote sustainable fisheries management, the Government also proposes to implement a uniform leasing policy for fisher y management in water bodies administered by different departments. 66 66 8.2.3.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: To ensure uniformity, minimise litigation, safeguard the interests of traditional fishing communities and promote sustainable fisheries management, the Government also proposes to implement a uniform leasing policy for fisher y management in water bodies administered by different departments. 66 66 8.2.3. Enhancing Fish Production in Panchayat Tanks The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department administers about 21,608 minor irrigation tanks, which represent a vast untapped resource for inland fisheries. The Department has initiated large scale stocking of quality fish seed in suitable Panchayat tanks to augment fish production and improve the availability at affordable price. Every year, fish seed will be stocked in 5,000 hectares of suitable Panchayat tanks, with an estimated additional fish production of 2,000 MT annually. 8.2.4 Enhancement of Freshwater Prawn (Scampi) Resources Freshwater prawn ( Macrobrachium rosenbergii), commonly known as Scampi, is a high-value species with strong demand in both 67 67 domestic and export markets. However, natural populations have declined due to overfishing, habitat degradation and pollution. To restore natural stocks and enhance inland fisheries productivity, the Department proposes to implement a focused Scampi stock enhancement programme by stocking quality juveniles in selected reservoirs and river stretches across the State. 8.2.5. Promotion of Cage Culture in Selected Reservoirs Reservoir cage culture offers significant potential for enhancing fish production without increasing water use and provides substantial scope for scientific intensification. The Department proposes to establish grow-out cage culture in selected reservoirs through installation of floating cages with the 68 68 assistance of PMMSY .
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Promotion of Cage Culture in Selected Reservoirs Reservoir cage culture offers significant potential for enhancing fish production without increasing water use and provides substantial scope for scientific intensification. The Department proposes to establish grow-out cage culture in selected reservoirs through installation of floating cages with the 68 68 assistance of PMMSY . Supported by the availability of quality GIFT seed s, the initiative is expected to substantially enhance reservoir fish production while generating employment and improving rural livelihoods. 8.2.6. Promotion of Murrel and GIF Tilapia Culture in Farm Ponds To improve the income of inland fish farmers, the Government proposes to promote the culture of high value Murrel and fast growing GIFT in multipurpose farm ponds across the State. Subsidy assistance will be provided for essential aquaculture inputs such as fish seed and feed to encourage farmers to adopt scientific fish culture practices. The initiative will enhance farmers income and create self employment opportunities. 69 69 8.2.7. Expansion of Fish Culture Area Expansion of aquaculture into new farming areas will contribute significantly to increased inland fish production, rural employment and farmers' income. The Department proposes to bring an additional 250 hectares under fish farming over the next five years through financial assistance, technical guidance and supply of quality fish seed. Fish farmers will be encouraged to adopt high value species such as Murrel and fast growing GIFT to improve productivity and profitability. The programme will also support scientific farming practices, input supply and capacity building. 70 70 8.2.8. Strengthening Government Fish Farms Government fish farms play a n important role in ensuring the availability of quality fish seed for inland fisheries development.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The programme will also support scientific farming practices, input supply and capacity building. 70 70 8.2.8. Strengthening Government Fish Farms Government fish farms play a n important role in ensuring the availability of quality fish seed for inland fisheries development. These farms comprise breeder ponds, nursery ponds, rearing ponds, conditioning ponds, eco -carp hatcheries and other supporting infrastructure required for fish seed production. To strengthen fish seed production capacity and meet the growing demand from fish farmers, the Government is investing in development, modernisation and strengthening of Government fish farms every year . 8.3. Ornamental Fisheries Sector Tamil Nadu is the leading State in ornamental fish production, contributing nearly 30 percentage of the country's ornamental fish 71 71 trade and playing a significant role in both domestic and international markets. The sector offers considerable potential for entrepreneurship, employment generation and income diversification. To promote and popularise ornamental fish culture, the Government has established a state- of-the-art Ornamental Fish Trade Centre in Chennai. In addition, initiatives are underway to establish an Ornamental Fish Brood Bank in Madurai District. These facilities will ensure the availability of quality broodstock, improve the production of indigenous and exotic ornamental fish varieties, promote entrepreneurship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for ornamental fish farmers, traders and allied industries. 72 72 8.4. Cold Water Fisheries Tamil Nadu is one of the few States in India endowed with cold water fisheries resources, with considerable potential in the hill regions of the Nilgiris owing to their favourable climatic conditions and pristine water resources. The Government Trout Hatchery at Avalanche, established in 1907, plays a pioneer ing role in trout seed production and conservation.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Government Trout Hatchery at Avalanche, established in 1907, plays a pioneer ing role in trout seed production and conservation. The hatchery produces quality trout seed for stocking in the upstreams of the Nilgiris, thereby replenishing natural trout populations, improving genetic quality. To harness the potential of cold water fisheries, the Department proposes to adopt an integrated approach encompassing the establishment of trout hatcheries, nurseries and Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS). Capacity building and skill development 73 73 programmes will be organised for fish farmers, entrepreneurs and fisheries personnel to promote sustainable, resource efficient and climate resilient trout farming practices, positioning the Nilgiris as a centre for cold water aquaculture. 9. FISHERIES INFRASTRUCTURE Recognizing the pivotal role of the fisheries sector in the economy, the Government is making significant investments in fisheries infrastructure development. These initiatives include establishment and upgradation of Fish Landing Points (FLP), Fish Landing Centres (FLC), Fishing Harbours (FH), Fish farms and other infrastructure facilities . These investments are aimed at improving fish quality and hygiene, reducing post-harvest losses, strengthening the cold chain and value chain and improving market access. Besides enhancing the safety 74 74 and efficiency of fishing operations, these initiatives are expected to provide better price for the fish catch . The details of marine infrastructure facilities developed are given in Table – 2 in Annexure. The required financial resources are being mobilised through multiple funding sources, including the Fisheries Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) and State Funds.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The required financial resources are being mobilised through multiple funding sources, including the Fisheries Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) and State Funds. The Government accorded administrative sanction for fisheries infrastructure projects amounting to Rs.1,161.18 crore and works are being carried out. The details are given in the Table – 3 in Annexure. 75 75 9.1 Development of Fishing Harbours Fishing harbours are provided with essential marine infrastructure such as breakwaters, jetties, whar fs, auction halls, net mending sheds and other amenities. Fifteen fishing harbours have been established along the coast of Tamil Nadu. 9.2 Development of Fish Landing Centres Fish Landing Centres are designed to provide safe berthing facilities for fishing vessels, along with essential infrastructure for fish landing, auctioning and net repair activities. There are 149 Fish Landing Centres along the coast of Tamil Nadu. 9.3 Shore Protection Works Shore protection works are of critical importance in addressing coastal erosion caused 76 76 by climate change and high wave activity. Anti-sea erosion structures such as bait arches, groynes, Rubble Mound Seawall (RMS) and training walls at river bar mouths are constructed along the coastline to mitigate erosion and safeguard coastal infrastructure. 9.4. Development of Climate Resilient Coastal Fis hing Villages Recognising the increasing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change and extreme weather events, the Government has launched an initiative to develop selected fishing villages as Climate Resilient Coastal Fish ing Villages (CRCFV) under PMMSY.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Development of Climate Resilient Coastal Fis hing Villages Recognising the increasing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change and extreme weather events, the Government has launched an initiative to develop selected fishing villages as Climate Resilient Coastal Fish ing Villages (CRCFV) under PMMSY. Under this initiative, 16 coastal fishing villages across the State have been selected for integrated development with an allocation of Rs.2.00 crore per village, involving a total investment of Rs.32.00 crore. 77 77 The programme adopts a balanced approach, with 70% of the project cost earmarked for fisheries infrastructure and 30% for livelihood and economic development activities. Infrastructure components include construction of multipurpose community halls with training centres and control rooms, net mending sheds, fish drying yards and other essential fisheries facilities. The livelihood component includes assistance for ice boxes, life buoys, bivalve culture, brackish water fish culture in ponds and other income generating fisheries activities. So far, an expenditure of Rs.15.96 crore has been incurred under the scheme and implementation is progressing across all the selected villages. 78 78 9.5. Project Design and Management Unit for Fisheries Infrastructure To strengthen planning, execution and monitoring of fisheries infrastructure projects, a dedicated Project Design and Management Unit (PDMU) comprising of experts from various departments will be established. The PDMU will provide technical and project monitoring support to ensure effective planning, timely implementation and continuous monitoring of fisheries infrastructure projects. 10. FISHERIES CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES Fisheries Co -operative Societies (FCS) constitute an important institutional framework for the socio -economic development and empowerment of fishermen and fisherwomen in Tamil Nadu.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: 10. FISHERIES CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES Fisheries Co -operative Societies (FCS) constitute an important institutional framework for the socio -economic development and empowerment of fishermen and fisherwomen in Tamil Nadu. These societies play a pivotal role in implementing welfare and development 79 79 programmes, strengthening community participation, facilitating access to institutional credit and marketing services and improving the overall livelihoods of fishing communities. At present, about 7.10 lakh fishermen and fisherwomen are enrolled as members in 1,513 Primary Fishermen and Fisherwomen Co-operative Societies functioning across the State. Ornamental, Marketing and other types of Fisheries Co- operative Societies 65 11,298 Total 1,513 7,09,620 These societies are supported by 12 District Fishermen Co -operative Federations and the Tamil Nadu State Apex Fisheries Co-operative Federation (TAFCOFED), which coordinate co- operative activities and facilitate effective implementation of welfare programmes.

items.text: 10.1 Marine Fishermen and Fisherwomen Co-operative Societies The Government is extending relief assistance to the members, under the schemes such as, Savings -cum-relief scheme for Marine 81 81 Fishermen/Fisherwomen, Fishing ban relief assistance, Special Allowance during fishing lean months, Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS), etc., These societies also contribute significantly to the socio -economic welfare of their members through a range of financial and marketing services. Members are provided access to microcredit through TAFCOFED, Co -operative Banks and other Nationalised Banks. Several societies also operate co-operative marketing outlets in Fishing Harbours for the supply of fishing gear and accessories. Further, Jewel loan facilities are provided through the Colachel, Vallavilai Fishermen Co -operative Societies in Kanniyakumari District and Thoothukudi Fishermen Co -operative Society and so far, a sum of Rs.16.22 crore loan disbursed to the FCS members (up to July-2026). 82 82 10.2 Inland Fisheries Co -operative Societies Inland Fisheries Co -operative Societies play a vital role in promoting fisheries activities in rivers, reservoirs, irrigation tanks and Panchayat tanks. Besides undertaking capture fisheries, several societies are engaged in the marketing of fresh fish, dried fish and value added fish products within their operational areas. 10.3 Kisan Credit Card (KCC) for Fisherfolk and Fish Farmers To improve access to institutional credit and meet the working capital requirements of fisherfolk and fish farmers, the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) has been extended to the fisheries sector and is being implemented across all districts of the State.
