ORDER: National Agriculture Development Programme / Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana is an important Centrally Sponsored flagship Programme implemented with an aim to make farming a remunerative economic activity through strengthening farmers’ efforts, risk mitigation and promoting agri business entrepreneurship. National Agriculture Development Programme is being implemented in the State since the year 2007-08 through 15 implementing departments pertaining to agriculture and allied sectors. Project proposals under National Agriculture Development Programme (60:40 sharing basis) are put forth before the State Level Sanctioning Committee chaired by the Chief Secretary to Government for approval. 2. Accordingly, in the letter 1 read above, the 19" State Level Sanctioning Committee in its meeting held on 21.4.2021, has approved 74 project proposals worth Rs.361.485 crore on priority and 27 projects worth Rs.77.142 crore under shelf of projects and 3 projects worth Rs.4.532 crore from earlier shelf of projects totalling Rs.443.15 crore under National Agriculture Development Programme for the year 2021-22. = Dx 3.

By adding the corresponding 40% State share of Rs.127.29 crore, the total allocation is worked out as Rs.318.22 crore. 4. For the first time in the History of Tamil Nadu, the Hon'ble Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has presented a separate Budget for Agriculture on the floor of Legislative Assembly on 14.08.2021 and among others the following announcements relating to the Department of Horticulture and Plantation Crops have been made:- Announcement No.3 Organic Farming Development Scheme The Farmers who adopt organic farming will be encouraged with provision of inputs subsidy. Announcement No.7 Palmyra Development Mission Action will be taken to distribute one lakh palmyra seedlings to farmers during the year. Announcement No.28 Promotion of fruit cultivation for fruitful income At National Level, Tamil Nadu stands seventh in production and eleventh in area under fruit crops. The present area of 3.13 lakh hectare under the cultivation of fruits will be increased to 3.30 lakh hectare during this year. The required planting materials of 80 lakh fruit plants will be produced in State horticulture Farms and distributed to farmers. Announcement No.29 Chief Minister’s Nutritive Vegetable Garden Scheme An area of 1,250 Ha in 2000 villages where the vegetable cultivation is meager will be brought under vegetable cultivation by enhancing the soil fertility. Pandal structure will be promoted in an area of 638 Ha for cultivation of gourds and greens in an area of 1000 Ha in all districts. Announcement No.31 Focus on Prime Horticulture Districts Horticulture Godown will be constructed in the districts where horticultural crops are predominantly grown.

items.text: (G.0.(2D) No.155, Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (AP1) Department, dated 13.10.2021) IMPLEMENTATION GUIDELINES FOR 2021-22 National Agriculture Development Programme for Department of Horticulture and Plantation crops Government of Tamil Nadu General guidelines: 6 The beneficiary selection should be done mainly through Priority register and Uzhavan App. . Application Mela should be fixed in every block by 7 days of communication of the targets. . The Joint / Deputy Director of Horticulture in the district is the implementing head in implementation of every component in the right direction. The Assistant Director of Horticulture in the block is the accepting authority for the selection of beneficiary in implementing the scheme. The Assistant Horticulture Officer and the Horticulture Officer of the block are jointly responsible for the selection of farmers after ascertaining their social status / category, gender with all the eligibility norms. . The selected farmer should have own land/ leased land (10 years registered lease) to the eligible extent to avail the benefit of the scheme. The selected farmer should be an account holder with any of the nationalized /scheduled / co-operative banking organizations in order to facilitate the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) through Public Finance Management System (PFMS) of Government of India or through Electronic Clearing Service (ECS). The selected farmer should have enrolled himself in the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) programme of Government of India and should link his Aadhar number with his bank account (Aadhar seeded beneficiary).

items.text: ABSTRACT Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Department — Distribution of Tarpaulin to reduce Post Harvest Losses in food grains — Financial Sanction for Rs.5.00 crore - Accorded - Orders - Issued. AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE (AP1) DEPARTMENT திருவள்ளுவர்‌ ஆண்டு 2052,பிலவ வருடம்‌, புரட்டாசி - 26 ஆம்‌ நாள்‌ G.0.(2D).No. 152 Dated:12.10.2021 Read: From the Director of Agriculture, Letter No.P&M 3/72330/2021, dated 2.9.2021. ORDER: For the first time in the History of Tamil Nadu, the Hon'ble Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has presented a separate Budget for Agriculture on the floor of Legislative Assembly on 14.08.2021 and among others, he has made the following announcement:- 8. Special Paddy Production Plan "XXxxx...Tarpaulins will be provided to farmers to reduce Post- Harvest Losses”. 2. Based on the above announcement, in the letter read above, the Director of Agriculture has submitted the proposal for sanction of Rs.5.00 crore to reduce Post Harvest Losses to Government as detailed below:- 0 In Agriculture, after harvest, nearly 10 % of the produce are lost as Post Harvest Losses either by Biotic factors like insects, rodents, fungi and bacteria or by abiotic factors such as moisture, humidity, temperature etc., Post Harvest Losses are a major area of concern since agricultural production is seasonal while the demands for agricultural commodities are more evenly spread throughout the year.

items.text: Further, at many times, it has been noticed that during the peak harvest the quantum of paddy arrivals to Direct Purchase Centres are high and due to less protected storage facilities the lots are damaged due to unpredicted rains, wind, etc., In order to satisfy the demand for a plentiful supply, grains must be stored throughout the year. A substantial amount of food grains is being damaged after harvest due to lack of adequate storage. Storage இ plays a vital role in the food supply chain. Post harvest handling aims to minimize losses at the least possible cost. Poor handling of agricultural produces can result in quality deterioration and losses. Therefore, it becomes essential to focus on reducing Post Harvest Losses. Tarpaulin plays a significant purpose to address this issue. > Role of Tarpaulin for storing Food Grains o Tarpaulin is a traditional method of food grains preservation and storage. In order to reduce the loss of grains, use of Tarpaulins significantly serves as mobile thrashing floor and provides an excellent ground cover. Tarpaulins are used as shelters during natural calamities and also used to cover heaps of produce and help the farmers for marketing their produce in Direct Purchase Centres. o This movable storage structure is cheap, eco-friendly and imparts high shelf life to the stored commodities. Besides this, it saves high investment and maintenance cost on construction of permanent storage. > Objective of the scheme: 0 To protect and strengthen food safety and security. 0 To reduce loss between harvest and consumption in terms of quantity and value. 0 Tosecure farmers livelihood. > Area of Operation:

items.text: Besides this, it saves high investment and maintenance cost on construction of permanent storage. > Objective of the scheme: 0 To protect and strengthen food safety and security. 0 To reduce loss between harvest and consumption in terms of quantity and value. 0 Tosecure farmers livelihood. > Area of Operation: This scheme will be implemented in 2500 villages covered under Kalaingnarin All Village Integrated Agriculture Development Programme 2021-22. > Scheme details: o Tarpaulin scheme will be implemented in Kalaingnarin All Village Integrated Agriculture Development Programme districts comprising of 2500 villages and benefit 20000 farmers. Tarpaulin is used as a protection for storing food grains and acts as a water resistant as well as heat specific radiator. Since Post Harvest Losses remain a challenge among the farmers, distribution of tarpaulin will serve as a protective tool for the storage of food grains and enable the prevention of grain loss to a significant extent. > Total Budget Requirement o Assistance for distribution of Tarpaulins to 20000 farmers at the rate of Rs.2500/- per number at 50 % subsidy at a total outlay of Rs.5.00 Crore through State Fund. 4. He has, therefore, requested to sanction a sum of Rs.5.00 crore for distribution of Tarpaulin to 20,000 farmers @ Rs.2500/- per Tarpaulin or 50% cost whichever is less. 5.

The district Joint Directors of Agriculture (JDAs) should also give wide publicity about the scheme. The JDAs and ADAs should preposition the material in the Agricultural Extension Centre (AECs) concerned, verify the quality and distribute to the farmers in time. Proper on-line billing should be done in the Agricultural Extension Centre and record of the transaction should be maintained. The basic details of the beneficiary should be uploaded in AGRISNET portal. Fund flow should be strictly adhered to category viz., Gen (80%), SC (19%) and ST (1%) farmers and preference should be given to small, marginal and women farmers. -6- To ensure’ proper implementation, the AOs/Dy.AOs/block ADAs/District level DDAs and JDA should verify the beneficiaries as per the norms in existence. Specification of Tarpaulin -HDPE laminated synthetic tarpaulin of 6 Mts X 8 Mts size, thickness of 250 GSM Tarpaulins should be procured by floating e-Tender and distributed to the farmers through the respective AECs. The registers should be maintained in the scheme implementing block AECs viz., Priority registers and Beneficiary registers. The AAOs should ensure that Proper Documentation (including Photo, video clippings and impact of the interventions) is done. Zonal officers from State Headquarters will also randomly verify the beneficiaries and _ utility of tarpaulins and ensure proper implementation of the scheme.

FRP of sugarcane for 2020-2021 sugar season at Rs.2850/- per M.T. for a basic recovery rate of 10%. 2. A premium of Rs.28.50 per M.T. for every 0.1% increase above 10% in the recovery and 3. Reduction in FRP by Rs.28.50 per M.T. for every 0.1% decrease in recovery, in respect of those mills whose recovery is below 10% but above 9.5%. However, for mills having recovery 9.5% or below, the FRP is fixed at Rs.2707.50 per M.T. Only those mills who have achieved a sugar recovery of 10% and above will get the Fair and Remunerative Price of Rs.2850/- and a premium of Rs.28.50 per M.T. for every 0.1% increase in recovery above 10%.

OBJECTIVES OF RPMFBY: RPMFBY aims at supporting sustainable production in agriculture by way of Providing financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of se) — unforeseen events. ம ~— Stabilizing the income of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming. (ஆ) — Encouraging farmers to adopt innovative and modern Agriculture practices. இ Ensuring credit worthiness of the farmers and their continuance in the farming activities, crop diversification and enhancing growth and competitiveness of agriculture sector besides protecting farmers from production risks. COVERAGE OF FARMERS: All farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing the notified crops in the notified areas are eligible for coverage. However, farmers should have insurable interest for the insured crops and lands. Scheme is optional for all loanee and non-loanee farmers. COVERAGE OF RISKS AND EXCLUSIONS: 1. BASIC COVER: The basic cover under the scheme covers the risk of loss of yield to standing crop (sowing to harvesting). This comprehensive risk insurance is provided to cover yield losses on an area based approach basis due to non- preventable risks like drought, dry spells, flood, inundation, wide spread pest and disease attack, landslides, natural fire due to lightening, storm, hailstorm, and cyclone. 2. ADD-ON COVERAGE: a. PREVENTED SOWING/ PLANTING / GERMINATION RISK - If Insured area is prevented from sowing / planting / germination due to deficit rainfall or adverse seasonal / climatic conditions.

items.text: 2. ADD-ON COVERAGE: a. PREVENTED SOWING/ PLANTING / GERMINATION RISK - If Insured area is prevented from sowing / planting / germination due to deficit rainfall or adverse seasonal / climatic conditions. MID-SEASON ADVERSITY - Insurance cover will be provided to the farmers ta provide immediate relief in case of adverse seasonal conditions viz. floods, prolonged dry spells, severe drought etc., during the crop season wherein expected yield during the season 6 likely to be less than 50% of Normal Yield POST-HARVEST LOSSES - Coverage is available only upto a maximum period of two weeks from harvesting, for those crops which are required to be dried in cut and spread / small bundled condition in the field after harvesting against specific perils of hailstorm, cyclone, cyclonic rains and unseasonal rains. LOCALIZED CALAMITIES - Loss / damage to notified insured crops resulting from occurrence of identified localized risks of hailstorm, landslide, inundation (except Paddy, Sugarcane), cloudburst and natural fire due to lightening affecting isolated farms in the notified area. GENERAL EXCLUSIONS - Losses arising out of war and nuclear risks, malicious damage and other preventable risks shall be excluded. NOTIFICATION OF IMPLEMENTING AGENCY The following Insurance Companies are recommended for notification to implement the Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana adopting the Co-insurance model of 80:20 proportionate sharing basis during Kharif and Special seasons, 2021-2022 as per the tender agreement in all the districts except Chennai.

ON = ORDER: The Government of India communicated the policy changes and requested the States to implement Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana from Kharif 2020 onwards. However, in response to the request made by the State Government, the Government of India permitted the Government of Tamil Nadu to implement Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana adopting existing premium rates for Kharif 2020 alone and negotiate with the existing Insurance Companies or invite fresh bid from Rabi 2020-2021 onwards. 2. In the Government Order first read above, the Government have accorded administrative approval for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana in all the districts of Tamil Nadu except Chennai from Kharif 2020 season as per the Government of India guidelines (revised). =p. 3.

items.text: 3. In the Government Order second read above, the Government have directed to implement the Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana in all the districts of Tamil Nadu except Chennai during Special season (Samba) and Rabi season 2020-2021 by adopting new Co-Insurance Model on 80:20 proportionate sharing basis as permitted by the Government of India subject to the conditions mentioned in their letter dated 30.09.2020. 4. In the Government Order third read above, the Government approved the Cluster-wise Implementing Agencies for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (RPMFBY) during Special and Rabi season 2020-21 in all the districts of Tamil Nadu except Chennai and issued notification of Agricultural & Horticultural Crops, Districts, Insurance Units and also Actuarial Premium Rate. 5. As the tender contractual period (Rabi season, 2020-2021) for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana with the empanelled Insurance Companies of Government of India ended by March, 2021, in G.O. fourth read above, orders were issued permitting the Director of Agriculture to call for a short tender of 15 days instead of 30 days as per Rule No.20 (2) of Chapter - V of Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tender Rules, 2000 for selection of Insurance Companies for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (RPMFBY) for a period of 3 years commencing from 2021-2022 to 2023-2024 in all the districts of Tamil Nadu except Chennai. 6.

items.text: 6. Subsequently, the Director of Agriculture in his letter 21.05.2021, has sent the proposal to Government for approval of the Actuarial Premium Rates quoted by the selected Insurance Companies and permission to issue work orders to L1 Insurance Companies for the e-bids opened on 10.05.2021. 7. In the Government Order fifth read above, the Government directed the Director of Agriculture to cancel the bids already called for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (RPMFBY) from 2021-22 to 2023-24 and call for retender based on reorganized clustering, since the Actuarial Premium Rates quoted by the Insurance Companies were very high. The Government also permitted the Director of Agriculture to call for a short tender of 7 days instead of 30 days as per Rule No.20 (2) of Chapter-V of Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tender Rules, 2000 for selection of Insurance Companies for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana for a period of 3 years commencing from 2021-2022 to 2023-2024 in all the districts of Tamil Nadu except Chennai. 8. Further the Government of India in their letter sixth read above, has also conveyed that in this case since retender is necessitated because of inadequate participation and higher Actuarial Premium Rates (APR) quoted by the Insurance Companies, the State Government may proceed with retendering for Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (RPMFBY) for the period 2021-22 to 2023-24. 9.

items.text: 9. Subsequently, the Director of Agriculture in his letter 29.07.2021, has sent the proposal to Government for approval of the APRs quoted by the selected Insurance Companies and permission to issue work orders to L1 Insurance Companies for the e-bids opened on 12.07.2021. 10. Meanwhile as per the advice of Finance Department, Government in the D.O. letter seventh cited, addressed Government of India seeking permission to obtain revised Actuarial Premium Rates from the L1 bidders for implementing Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (RPMFBY) by adopting either of the -3- coinsurance models of 80:20 or 60:40 based on the fair revised premium rates furnished by the L1 bidders. 11. In the letter eight cited, the Government of India has permitted the State Government to invite fresh bids for implementing the Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana adopting Co-insurance mode! of 80:20 for the year 2021-2022 stipulating certain conditions. 12. Accordingly, the Director of Agriculture in his letter dated 3.8.2021, requested the Government to issue orders for cancellation of tender called for on 02.07.2021 and inform the L1 bidders about the cancellation besides permitting to call for a short fresh e-bid from the empanelled Insurance Companies for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (RPMFBY) during 2021-2022 adopting the Co-insurance model of 80:20 proportionate sharing basis. 13.

items.text: 13. In Government letter dated 03.08.2021, the Government issued orders to cancel the tender invited on 02.07.2021 and call for a short fresh e-bids to implement Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (RPMFBY) during 2021-2022 by adopting the co-insurance model of 80:20 proportionate sharing basis for selection of Insurance Companies from the empanelled list of Government of India. 14. Accordingly, the Director of Agriculture in the letter dated 12.8.2021, has sent the proposal to Government for approval of the Actuarial Premium Rates (APRs) quoted by the selected Insurance Companies and permission to issue work orders to L1 Insurance Companies for the e-bids opened on 10.08.2021. Out of the 18 empanelled Insurance Companies, Agriculture Insurance Company of India Limited (AICIL) and IFFCO TOKIO General Insurance Company Limited (IFFCO TOKIO GIC) alone submitted their bids. items.text: ABSTRACT Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare - Sugarcane - Fixation of mill-wise Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for 2019-2020 and 2020-2021 sugar seasons in respect of sugar mills in Tamil Nadu — Approved—Notification — Issued. AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS’ WELFARE [$1] DEPARTMENT திருவள்ளுவராண்டு 2052, பிலவ ஆடி திங்கள்‌ 18-ம்‌ நாள்‌ G.0.(Ms).No.108 Dated: 03.08.2021 Read: 1. From the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, Department of Food and _ Public Distribution, Government of India, New Delhi, Letter No.3(2)/2018-SP-I, dated the 6" August, 2019. 2. Press Release dated 19.08.2020 approval of Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), Government of India. 3. Government of India, Ministry of Consumer Aftairs, Food and Public Distribution, Notification pubiished in the Gazette of India Extraordinary No.541, dated 22.10.2020. 4. From the Commissioner of Sugar, Letter Rc.No.5548/ Cane2/2020, dated:19.12.2020 and 15.03.2021. KKKKKK ORDER: The Government of India announces Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane, every year on all India basis under the provisions of Clause 3 of Sugarcane (Control) Order 1966, which the sugar mills are bound to pay within 14 days of purchase of cane. The Government of India fixed the Fair and Remunerative Price for each sugar mill separately through a Gazette Notification up to 2018-19 sugar season based on previous crushing season average sugar recovery obtained by the sugar mills. 2.

items.text: The Government of India fixed the Fair and Remunerative Price for each sugar mill separately through a Gazette Notification up to 2018-19 sugar season based on previous crushing season average sugar recovery obtained by the sugar mills. 2. The Government of India vide its letter 1° read above has determined the Fair and Remunerative Price of sugarcane payable by Sugar Mills for 2019-2020 sugar season as detailed below:- (i) Fair and Remunerative Price of sugarcane for 2019-20 sugar season at Rs. 2750/- per Metric Tonne for a basic recovery rate of 10% : [21.0] ape (ii) A premium of Rs.27.50 per Metric Tonne for every 0.1% increase above 10% in the recovery ; and (iii) Reduction in Fair and Remunerative Price by Rs. 27.50 per Metric Tonne for every 0.1% decrease in recovery, in respect of those mills whose recovery is below 10% but above 9.5 percent. However, for mills having recovery 9.5% or below, the Fair and Remunerative Price is fixed at Rs. 2612.50 per Metric Tonne. 3. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs vide reference [unclear figure] read above has approved the Fair and Remunerative Price of Sugarcane payable by sugar mills for 2020-2021 sugar season (October 2020 to September 2021) on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) as under :- (i) Fair and Remunerative Price of sugarcane for 2020-21 sugar season at Rs.2850/- per Metric Tonne for a basic recovery rate of 10% ; (ii) A premium of Rs.

In continuation, the Government of India, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution in its notification 3 read above has delegated the powers conferred on it by clause 3(1) of Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966 for fixing mill-wise Fair and Remunerative Price to be exercisable by the State Government / Union Territory from the sugar season 2019-20 onwards for the sugar mills wherein the concerned sugar mills is located. 5. Consequently, the Commissioner of Sugar in his letter 4" read above has stated that, as per the above norms, he has worked out the mill-wise Fair and Remunerative Price based on the average recovery of the sugar mills for both Public and Co-operative and also in respect of private sugar mills for 2019-20 and 2020-21 sugar seasons and requested to approve the same and to notify in Tamil Nadu Government Gazette as per the powers delegated in the Government of India, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Notification 3° read above. items.text: The Government, after careful examination, have decided to accept the proposal of the Commissioner of Sugar in para 5 above. Accordingly, the Government approve the mill-wise Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) calculated by the Commissioner of Sugar based on the average recovery of the sugar mills for 2019-20 and 2020-21 sugar seasons and also decided to notify the same in the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette as per the powers delegated in the notification third read above. 7. The Notification appended to this Government Order shall be published in the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette. 8. The Works Manager, Goverment Central Press, Chennai-600 079 is requested to send 100 copies of the Notification as published in Tamil Nadu Government Gazette to the Government in Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Department, Secretariat, Chennai-9 and to send the bill of cost towards publication of Notification to the Additional Chief Secretary / Commissioner of Sugar, Chennai-600 035 for settlement. 9. The Additional Chief Secretary / Commissioner of Suqar is directed to pursue further action accordingly (BY ORDER OF THE GOVERNOR) C.SAMAYAMOORTHY. items.text: ORDER: The Hon'ble Chief Minister has opened the shutters of Mettur dam on [unclear figure] June and announced that Kuruvai Paddy area would be increased beyond the targeted coverage and paddy production would surpass the previous years. 2. The Director of Agriculture has submitted proposal along with guidelines for implementation of Kuruvai package in Delta Districts during 2021 to increase the area under Kuruvai Cultivation using the available water in the current Kuruvai Season 2021 and to protect the livelihood of the delta farmers and farm labourers at an outlay of Rs.50.00 Crore in seven Delta Districts of Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai and parts of Cuddalore, Trichy and Ariyalur as follows:- Area coverage Cauvery Delta region includes entire Thanjavur, Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam Mayiladuthurai districts and parts of Cuddalore, Trichy, Karur, Ariyalur and Pudukkottai Districts. In this zone, Rice is the principal crop. The normal area under Kuruvai Paddy in delta region is around 3.50 Lakh acre in the districts viz., Thanjavur, Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai, Cuddalore, Trichy and Ariyalur. During the current Kuruvai season, so far, an area of 1.693 Lakh acre is covered. Cauvery Delta districts are mainly dependent on the release of water in the river Cauvery from Mettur dam.

items.text: During the current Kuruvai season, so far, an area of 1.693 Lakh acre is covered. Cauvery Delta districts are mainly dependent on the release of water in the river Cauvery from Mettur dam. The onset of South West Monsoon in the catchment area will feed the dam, which would help in taking up normal Kuruvai cultivation in delta districts. Hence, to increase the area under Kuruvai using the available water in the current Kuruvai Season 2021 and to protect the livelihood of the delta farmers and farm labourers, a package of assistance may be given with an outlay of Rs.50.00 crore (Rs.45.00 Crore from State fund and Rs.5.00 crore by dovetailing) as detailed below in seven Delta districts Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapatinam, Mayiladuthurai and parts of Cuddalore, Trichy and Ariyalur wherein Kuruvai cultivation is taken up:- Total Budget Requirement S.No Component Assistance in Area in Finance Rs. items.text: Objectives: e To increase the area under cultivation during Kuruvai season in the Delta districts of Thanjavur, Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai and delta parts of Cuddalore, Trichy and Ariyalur utilizing the filter point bore wells and Cauvery River water. e To augment the rice production through adopting yield influencing recommended technologies. e To protect the livelihood of the farmers in New Delta and Grand Anaicut regions. e To sustain and increase the income of farmers and farm labourers. B. Area of Operation: This scheme would be implemented in all the blocks of the Cauvery Delta Districts viz.,. Thanjavur, Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai and delta blocks of Cuddalore, Ariyalur and Trichy. The villages where this scheme is to be implemented the input requirement and timeline for execution of different activities would be identified by extension functionaries. C. Package of Assistance to Cauvery Delta Districts for Kuruvai Cultivation during 2021 Promotion of Paddy Cultivation a. Distribution of Paddy Seeds b. Assistance for Fertilizers c. Assistance for Green Manure Seeds D. Component wise funding proposal of Agricultural Department for promotion of Paddy cultivation a. Distribution of Paddy Seeds Quality seed plays an important role in the cultivation of any crop. The farmers need to be provided with good quality seeds to ensure better yield. Seeds will be distributed to the Delta District farmers under National Food Security Mission - Rice and Sub - Mission for Seed and Planting Materials - Seed Village Scheme. The funds for the distribution of seeds will be dove-tailed from the said schemes as detailed below:

Assistance for Fertiliser Fertiliser plays an important role in the plant metabolic process. The requirement of major nutrients such as Nitrogen, Phosphorous and Potassium are essential for plant growth both directly and indirectly. This helps in increasing the crop yield to a great extent. Deficiency of these nutrients results in substantial yield reduction. The major nutrients are applied as basal and top dressing. Therefore, it is proposed to extend 100% subsidy @ Rs.2,185 per acre (which is inclusive of GST) for an area of 1,90,000 acres, with a budget outlay of Rs. 4151.50 Lakh. c. Assistance for use of Green Manure Seeds: In order to improve the soil health through increasing the organic content, it is appropriate to adopt green manure crop on rotational basis.

Assistance for use of Green Manure Seeds: In order to improve the soil health through increasing the organic content, it is appropriate to adopt green manure crop on rotational basis. Intermittent growing of green manure crop and in-situ ploughing help in enriching the native soil to provide good nutrition and efficient uptake of applied nutrients to the crop. With this objective, distribution of green manure seeds will be taken up with 100% subsidy @ Rs.1,400 per acre (which is inclusive of GST) for an area of 24,000 acres with a budget outlay of Rs.336.000 Lakh. d. items.text: 2. The Government of India have fixed the Minimum Support Price for Milling Copra as Rs.103.35 and Ball Copra as Rs.106.00 per Kg for 2021 copra season. 3. The Director of Agriculture has reported that in Tamil Nadu, Coconut is cultivated in an extent of 4.97 lakh hectares with an annual production of 50,663 lakh nuts with the productivity of 8,519 nuts per hectare. The coconut farmers prefer selling their produce in the form of Coconut, Tender coconut and Copra. The market price of Milling Copra in major Copra Markets is now prevalling bétween Rs.130.00 to Rs.135.00 per Kg which is subjected to variation in the course of year. There is a possibility that the price may go down in the later part of the year. In the event of fall in price of Copra, to ensure that the farmers are getting remunerative price for their Copra produced, Price Support Scheme has to be implemented. Therefore, there is need for implementation of Price Support Scheme (PSS) to help the coconut growers. (P.T.O) NO [unclear figure]. 4. The Director of Agriculture has also stated that normally, in the previous years, the Copra Procurement season was notified for six months from June to November. The Director of Agricultural Marketing and Agri Business has requested the Director of Agriculture that based on the farmers’ demand and seasonal benefits of Copra production, the procurement period of Copra may be changed to first half of the year (January to June) or throughout the year for the betterment of farmers through Price Support Scheme. 5.

The market price for Copra many times tends to be unstable and volatile resulting in undue losses to the growers /farmers as well as discourages adoption of the modern technology and required inputs. The Government's. price policy for agricultural commodities seeks to ensure remunerative prices to the growers for their produce with a view to encourage higher investment and production and to safeguard the interest of consumers by inaking availabie supplies at reasonable prices with iow cost oi intermediation. The price policy also seeks to evolve a balanced and integrated price structure in the overall perspective of the needs of the economy. Towards this end, the Government announces Minimum Support Price (MSP) for major agricultural commodities each year in both the Crop seasons after taking into account the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).

Custom Hiring Centres (CHC) are basically a unit comprising a set of farm machinery, implements and equipment meant for custom hiring for the needy farmers. It is proposed to form 36 Custom Hiring Centres in the needy blocks of Tamil Nadu with a project cost of Rs.25.00 Lakh per CHC. Out of Rs.25.00 Lakh, an amount of Rs.10.00 Lakh is Government assistance in the form of 40% subsidy and the remaining amount of Rs.15.00 Lakh towards 60 % Rural Entrepreneurs (Rural youth and farmer as an entrepreneur) / Cooperative Societies of farmers / Registered Farmers Societies / Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) contribution.

items.text: Agricultural Mechanization is an effective method to reduce the cost of cultivation considerably besides eliminating the drudgery of farm operations. Promotion of suitable machinery for dry (கார்‌ and wet land cultivation by establishing far machinery banks ts imperative in iow farm power availability districts where the farm powel availability is iess than 2.5 kW/Ha. The crop specific machinery avaliable in farm machinery banks ts of immense use to the farming community and ts established by the Co-operative Societies of farmers, Registered Farmers Societies, and Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) etc., The farmers groups should have a minimum of 8 members. The farm machinery bank possessed by the farmers groups use its machinery for hiring activity to the needy farmers in addition to their own use. It is proposed to establish farm machinery banks (Custom Hiring Centres) upto a project cost of Rs.10.00 Lakh each in 126 villages through Co-operative Societies of farmers/Registered Farmers Societies/ Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) etc., or any such entities on village basis, in low farm power availability districts as per Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) guidelines. Financial assistance of 80% of the project cost of Rs.8.00 Lakh will be provided to such farm machinery banks and for which the farmers groups should have minimum of 8 members. An amount of Rs.1008.00 Lakh under General Category is required for establishing 126 village based farm machinery banks during the year 2020-2021 under SMAM. Preference will be given to the villages comes under clusters formed in Tamil Nadu Mission for Sustainable Dry land Development scheme (TNMSDD) for the establishment of farm machinery banks at village level.

items.text: Out of the total funds of Rs.19.93 Crore available, an amount of Rs.9.93 Crore is earmarked for the procurement of machinery / equipment. 2) In Government Order 273 read above orders have been issued to utilize the Watershed Development Fund (WDF), Revolving Fund Recovery Amount and Funds of Consolidation phase under Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) to the tune of Rs.103 Crore for procurement of New Agricultural machinery / equipments by Agricultural Engineering Department for Maintenance of Watershed assets created and to increase the cropping area through mechanization. Out of the total funds of Rs.103 crore available, an amount of Rs.50 Crore was earmarked towards maintenance of watershed assets created under Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP)/Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) — Watershed Development Component (WDC) and Rs.53 Crore was earmarked in order to increase the cropping area through mechanisation. (P.T.O) 2: 3) The Chief Engineer (Agricultural Engineering) has stated that based on the Government Orders the following machinery have been procured duly following th Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tender Act, 1998. 1. Crawler excavator — 10 Nos 2. Backhoe with Front end Loader — 60 Nos i. Crawler excavator Excavators (hydraulic) are heavy construction equipments consisting of a boom, dipper (or stick), bucket (a large shovel) and cab on a rotating platform known as the "house", usually with tracks or wheels.

items.text: Crawler excavator Excavators (hydraulic) are heavy construction equipments consisting of a boom, dipper (or stick), bucket (a large shovel) and cab on a rotating platform known as the "house", usually with tracks or wheels. All movement and functions of a hydraulic excavator are accomplished through the use of hydraulic fluid, with hydraulic cylinders and hydraulic motors. As the name suggests, the excavator is used for excavating and lifting the material. This heavy machinery can move ina 360-degree radius around the machine to move material. The arm articulates out, left or right, and down via hydraulic pistons. The bucket, which can be swapped with several styles for different digging applications, moves vertically around its axis, bringing in material. It works for digging holes and trenches, depending on the job. This machine is very much essential for maintenance works of watershed assets. ii. Backhoe with front end loader The Backhoe with front end loader is a combination of a front loader and an excavator, A bucket at the front of the machine allows it to scoop up earth by backing over loose top soil with the tip of the bucket placed on the ground. On the back. an excavation unit consists of an arm and articulating bucket. This feature allows the operator to dig down and remove materials. The excavator can be fitted with different rear buckets for digging large holes, narrow trenches or gripping loose materials with a grappling hook, making it a versatile earth-moving machine. A backhoe can rotate 200 degrees side to side.

items.text: The excavator can be fitted with different rear buckets for digging large holes, narrow trenches or gripping loose materials with a grappling hook, making it a versatile earth-moving machine. A backhoe can rotate 200 degrees side to side. Its front and back buckets can be used to excavate silted earth, load waste and drag debris towards the vehicle and load the desilted materials. 4) The Chief Engineer (Agricultural Engineering) has further stated that in Tamil Nadu, most of the farmers are small and marginal farmers, who have less investing capacity to purchase of machinery with high cost for different farming operations. During the peak season, the private hirer's hiring charges are of exorbitant value for which these farmers cannot afford. In order to assist small and marginal farmers who cannot afford to pay higher hire charges of private crawler excavator owners, these farm machinery are proposed to hire out to the needy farmers with nominal hire charges by Agricultural Engineering Department. The above said machinery have been procured from the Watershed Development Fund (WDF) collected from the user groups. Hence, these Agricultural Machinery and Implements are to be hired out to the needy farmers in IWMP watershed areas at subsidized hire charges. Compared to private hirers, usually the Agricultural Machinery and Implements are hired out at concessional rate by Agricultural Engineering Department (AED) which is much less than the hire charges of private hirers. (P.T.O) pole 5) The Chief Engineer (Agricultural Engineering) has reported that at present, the hire charges for the machinery hired under Tractor hiring scheme and Minor irrigation scheme have been fixed by the Government.

items.text: (P.T.O) pole 5) The Chief Engineer (Agricultural Engineering) has reported that at present, the hire charges for the machinery hired under Tractor hiring scheme and Minor irrigation scheme have been fixed by the Government. These machinery are hired to farmers by Agricultural Engineering Department (AED) at Government fixed nominal hire charges for the benefit of farming community. As per G.O (Ms) No.2174, Agriculture (AE-1) Department, Dated 24.9.1981, the Agricultural Engineering Department is not a profit earning department but a department providing service to farmers. The above said new machinery procured through the Watershed Development Fund (WDF) collected from the user groups of IWMP watershed areas are proposed to be hired to small and marginal farmers of the IWMP Watershed areas and _ this unprivileged farming community could not pay higher rates for their farming operations charged by the private hirers. The private hirers exorbitantly fix the hire charges based on the season and demand. Hence, it is crucial to fix nominal hire charges to these machinery to control private operators role. Further the hire charges fixed by Agricultural Engineering Department will be referred as Bench mark price for all district level development activities. Hence, the Chief Engineer (Agricultural Engineering) has proposed the nominal hire charges at the rate of 60% of the operational cost of above said machinery, since ([unclear figure] Agricultural Engineering Department is rendering services to the poor and unprivileged farming community to improve their livelihood and Agricultural production.

ORDER: Tamil Nadu Cooperative Oil seeds Growers’ Federation Limited (TANCOF) was started in the year 1981 with a view to promote the interests of the farmers and its objective was to organize effective production, procurement and marketing of Oilseeds. The scheme was proposed to be implemented in 2 stages. In the first stage, high yielded Oilseeds production districts such as Thiruvannamalai, Vellore, Thiruvallur, Cuddalore and Villupuram were identified and 335 Oilseeds production Co-operative societies were formed. Simultaneously, 2° Oil crushing units were formed at Thiruvannamalai and Virudachalam.

items.text: Simultaneously, 2° Oil crushing units were formed at Thiruvannamalai and Virudachalam. An Oil packing unit at Guindy was also established. Due to Globalization, competition from private companies, high overhead and administrative costs, Tamil Nadu Co-operative Oilseeds Growers’ Federation Limited was functioning on continuous loss. Since, all steps taken to revive Tamil Nadu Co-operative Oilseeds Growers’ Federation Limited were proved to be futile. [p.t.o] -2- 2) In the Government Order 1! read above, the Director of Agriculture / Registrar of Oilseeds Growers Co-operative societies was directed to take appropriate proceedings under section 137 of the Tamil Nadu Co-operative Societies Act, 1983 to wind up the activities of Tamil Nadu Cooperative Oilseeds Growers’ Federation Limited. Following this, the Government decided to liquidate the Tamil Nadu Co-operative Oilseeds Growers’ Federation Limited and all operations were wound up with effect from 31.03.2002 and liquidator was appointed vide proceedings dated 22.12.2004 of the Commissioner of Agriculture. இ In the letters [unclear figure] and 3 read above, the Director of Agriculture has stated that after winding up of the activities of Tamil Nadu Co-operative Oilseeds Growers’ Federation Limited, the plants and machineries of the oil packing unit at Guindy, Oil processing units at Thiruvannamalai and Virudachalam have been kept idle for more than 16 years. As such, the plants and machineries have been damaged/rusted/worn out and thus become useless.

General Guidelines:- > > Districts with larger extent of paddy cultivation followed by fallow area are selected for this programme. The Block level ADAs should effectively utilize the FCMS / AGRISNET / Uzhavan App in sending messages to ail farmers in that block to register with Block ADA to avail the benefit of the scheme. Wide publicity shall be given on implementation of various components of the scheme through Newspapers, AIR and meeting with farmers of villages. The name of the farmers expressing willingness shall be entered in a priority register and based on the seniority, the application may be obtained in the prescribed format from the farmer along with the following documents. Extract of chitta adangal/Voter ID card / Ration card / Aadhaar card / Driving Licence /Passport may be considered for identification.

Preference shall be given to SC/ST, SF/MF, Women farmers, in that order for various components of the scheme. At least 20% for SC / ST(1.1%),33% for small and marginal farmers and 30% for Women farmers. Identified villages in selected districts and the list of beneficiaries shall be uploaded in the NFSM portal. Online billing of inputs shall be done in the AECs and record of the transaction shall be maintained. TRFA oilseeds implemented villages during 2019-20 would be continued this year. Demonstration of improved production technologies of Oilseeds would be organized in a cluster of around 50 ha for Gingelly & 25 ha for Groundnut in each village continuously for 3 years. In case of non availability of 50 ha area in a village, the cluster will be contiguous in the neighbouring villages. The other Production Inputs would be distributed to Oilseed crops growing farmers of the above selected villages.

In Government Order first read above, the Government have accorded administrative approval for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana in all the districts of Tamil Nadu except Chennai from Kharif 2020 season as per the existing Government of India guidelines and among others, orders have been issued:- - 2: i. to implement Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana as per old tender rates for Kharif, 2020 with the existing tenderers viz., Agriculture Insurance Company of India Limited (AICIL) and Oriental Insurance Company Limited (OICL) in all the districts of Tamil Nadu except Chennai and ii. to renegotiate the premium rates with the Insurance Companies for remaining part of the tender period from Rabi 2020-2021 or call for fresh bids for implementation of the scheme in case of disagreement by the existing tenderers by following the Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tenders Act, 1998 and the Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tenders Rules, 2000. 3. The Agriculture Insurance Company of India Limited, Chennai & Oriental Insurance Company Limited (OICL) have declined to concede the request of the Department of Agriculture for renegotiating the existing Actuarial Premium Rates (APR). Based on the request of Director of Agriculture, in Government Order second read above, the Government have permitted the Director of Agriculture to call for short tender for selection of Insurance Companies for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana for a period of 3 years commencing from Special Season (Samba) 2020-2021 to 2022-2023 in all the districts of Tamil Nadu except Chennai. 4.

As there was no adequate participation of Insurance Companies for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantr Fasai Bima Yojana from Speciai Season 2020-2021 after calling for tenders (2 times), the Government of Tamil Nadu have requested the Government of India’s permission to consider the New Co-Insurance model on 80:20 proportionate sharing basis for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Manitri Fasal Bima Yojana during Special & Rabi Seasons of 2020-2021. Based on this, the Government of India in their letter dated 30.09.2020 have permitted the State Government to initiate retender on the basis of the proposed model subject to certain conditions. 5. Accordingly, in Government Order third read above, the Government have directed to implement the Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana in all the districts of Tamil Nadu except Chennai during Special season (Samba) and Rabi season 2020-2021 by adopting new Co-Insurance Model on 80:20 proportionate sharing basis as permitted by Government of India subject to the conditions mentioned in their letter dated 30.09.2020 and permitted the Director of Agriculture to call for a short tender for selection of Insurance Companies for implementation of Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana for Special Season and Rabi season 2020-2021 in all the districts of Tamil Nadu except Chennai. 6.

items.text: REVAMPED PRADHAN MANTRI FASAL BIMA YOJANA (RPMFBY) NOTIFICATION FOR SPECIAL SEASON 2020-2021 Revamped Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (RPMFBY) will be implemented in all the districts of Tamil Nadu (except Chennai) during Special season as per the Revamped Operational Guidelines of Government of India (Government of India Letter No. 13015/02/2015- Credit - || dated 24.03.2020 & Letter No.13012/06/2020 Credit — II (FTS 8398) dated 19.5.2020. OBJECTIVES OF RPMFBY: RPMFBY aims at supporting sustainable production in agriculture by way of a) Providing financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of — unforeseen events. ம — Stabilizing the income of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming. Encouraging farmers to adopt innovative and modern Agriculture practices. a 6 வவ — Ensuring credit worthiness of the farmers and their continuance in the farming activities, crop diversification and enhancing growth and competitiveness of agriculture sector besides protecting farmers from production risks. COVERAGE OF FARMERS: All farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing the notified crops in the notified areas are eligible for coverage. However, farmers should have insurable interest for the insured crops and lands. Scheme is optional for all loanee and non-loanee farmers. COVERAGE OF RISKS AND EXCLUSIONS: 1. BASIC COVER : The basic cover under the scheme covers the risk of loss of yield to standing crop (sowing to harvesting).

items.text: Scheme is optional for all loanee and non-loanee farmers. COVERAGE OF RISKS AND EXCLUSIONS: 1. BASIC COVER : The basic cover under the scheme covers the risk of loss of yield to standing crop (sowing to harvesting). This comprehensive risk insurance is provided to cover yield losses on an area based approach basis due to non- preventable risks like drought, dry spells, flood, inundation, wide spread pest and disease attack, landslides, natural fire due to lightening, storm, hailstorm, and cyclone. 2. ADD-ON COVERAGE: a. PREVENTED SOWING/ PLANTING / GERMINATION RISK - If Insured area is prevented from sowing / planting / germination due to deficit rainfall or adverse seasonal / climatic conditions. . MID-SEASON ADVERSITY - Insurance cover will be provided to the farmers to provide immediate relief in case of adverse seasonal conditions viz. floods, prolonged dry spells, severe drought etc., during the crop season wherein expected yield during the season is likely to be less than 50% of Normal Yield. POST-HARVEST LOSSES - Coverage is available only upto a maximum period of two weeks from harvesting, for those crops which are required to be dried in cut and spread / small bundled condition in the field after harvesting against specific perils of hailstorm, cyclone, cyclonic rains and unseasonal rains. , LOCALIZED CALAMITIES - Loss / damage to notified insured crops resulting from occurrence of identified localized risks of hailstorm, landslide, inundation (except Paddy, Sugarcane), cloudburst and natural fire due to lightening affecting isolated farms in the notified area.

items.text: 23.01.2020 & 20.05.2020 8. From the Commissioner of Sugar letter Rc.No.73/Cane1/ 2020, Dated: 07.10.2020 & 12.10.2020 1ஓ ORDER: In the Government Order 1” read above, the Government have sanctioned a sum of Rs.134.50 crore for the timely transfer of Transitional Production Incentive to the farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer due to switch over to the revenue sharing based sugarcane price fixation policy for the crushing season 2017-18. 2. In Government Order 2"? read above, the Government have permitted the Commissioner of Sugar to transfer the difference amount between the State Advised Price for 2016-17 crushing season and the Fair and Remunerative Price for 2017-18 crushing season of Rs.200/- per MT as Transitional Production Incentive to the farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer. 3. In Government Order 3 read above, the Government have sanctioned an additional amount of Rs.11.82 Crore for timely transfer of Transitional Production Incentive to sugarcane growers through Direct Benefit Transfer for the special crushing season 2017-2018. Thus, a total sum of Rs.146.32 Crore was sanctioned for payment of Transitional Production Incentive to sugarcane growers for 2017-18 season. 4. In the Government Order [unclear figure] read above, a sum of Rs.150.00 Crore was sanctioned for the timely transfer of Transitional Production Incentive to the farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer for 2018-19 season. த.

items.text: 4. In the Government Order [unclear figure] read above, a sum of Rs.150.00 Crore was sanctioned for the timely transfer of Transitional Production Incentive to the farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer for 2018-19 season. த. In the letter 5'" read above, the Commissioner of Sugar has inter-alia stated that for the sugar season 2019-20, the Government of India announced Fair and Remunerative Price for Sugarcane at two scales :- (i) Fair and Remunerative Price of sugarcane for 2019-20 sugar season at Rs.2750/- per MT for a basic recovery rate of 10% with a premium of Rs.27.50 per MT for every 0.1% increase above 10% recovery. Further, Fair and Remunerative Price will be proportionately reduced by Rs.27.50 per MT for 0.1% decrease in recovery in respect of those mills whose recovery is below 10% but above 9.50%. (ii) Fair and Remunerative Price of sugarcane for mills having recovery of 9.50% or less at Rs.2612.50 per MT. There is no change in the cane price of 2019-20 crushing season announced by the Central Government as compared to Fair and Remunerative Price of 2018-19 crushing season. The difference between State Advised Price for 2016-17 crushing season (Rs.2750/- per MT) and the Fair and Remunerative Price for 2019-20 crushing season is Rs 137.50 per MT. The average recovery of Tamil Nadu State is below 9.50% only.

items.text: The difference between State Advised Price for 2016-17 crushing season (Rs.2750/- per MT) and the Fair and Remunerative Price for 2019-20 crushing season is Rs 137.50 per MT. The average recovery of Tamil Nadu State is below 9.50% only. As per the Order of the Government of India, the Tamil Nadu sugarcane farmers will get only Rs.2612.50 per MT as Fair and Remunerative Price for 2019-20 crushing season which is below the present cane price of Rs.2750/- per MT received by the farmers including the Transitional Production Incentive of Rs.137.50 per MT. 6. The Commissioner of Sugar has pointed out that in Tamil Nadu State, sugarcane production, productivity and sugar recovery % have been worst affected by drought due to failure of monsoons in the last three years. Due to severe drought in the last year (2019), the Tamil Nadu state witnesses sharp decline in sugarcane and sugar production in the ensuing 2019-20 crushing season. Further, the market price of sugar has not increased in the last three years. The South Indian Sugar Mills Association (SISMA) has submitted memorandums to the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu and the Chief Secretary of Tamil Nadu seeking various support measures including the extension of Transitional Production Incentive @ Rs.137.50 per MT to save the sugar industry and sugarcane farmers of Tamil Nadu.

items.text: Further, various Sugarcane Farmers Associations also frequently representing the State Government to extend the Transitional Production Incentive for 2019-20 crushing season also as announced during 2017-18 and 2018-19 crushing seasons considering the escalation of cost of cultivation of sugarcane, no increase in the cane price announced by the Government of India and crop failure due to severe drought. 2 7. Further, the sugar mills are facing acute shortage of cane to their capacity utilization and the sugar recovery is also worst affected. Some of the sugar mills in Cooperative and Private Sector Sugar mills are not able to commence their 2019-20 crushing season due to meagre quantity of cane available for crushing. Considering the welfare of the sugarcane growers, the Commissioner of Sugar has requested that the transitional production incentive may also be extended for the crushing season 2019-20. Hence, to implement this payment of Transitional Production Incentive for 2019-20 crushing season, he has requested the Government to allocate Rs.150 Crores during 2020-21 budget. 8. items.text: 8. The Commissioner of Sugar in his letters 8"" read above, has informed that the 2019-20 crushing season has been concluded on 30.09.2020 with a crushing of 92.20 LMT of sugarcane by 27 sugar mills viz. 11 Cooperative Sector Sugar Mills, 2 Public Sector Sugar Mills and 14 Private Sector Sugar Mills and requested the Government to sanction a sum of Rs.126.65 crore (inclusive of Rs.60 lakh required for data base preparation and contingency) for payment of Transitional Production Incentive to sugarcane growers for 2019-20 crushing season and to permit the Director of Agriculture to draw the money and to transfer to the Commissioner of Sugar and further to approve the guidelines for the successful implementation of timely transfer of Transitional Production Incentive to the farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer scheme with a view to pave the way for the improvement both in sugarcane production and productivity in Tamil Nadu. 9. The Government have examined the proposal of the Commissioner of Sugar and decided to accept the same, subject.to restricting the amount sought for by him. Accordingly, the Government sanction a sum of Rs.126.65 Crore (Rupees One hundred and twenty six crore and sixty five lakh only) for the timely transfer of Transitional Production Incentive to the farmers during 2019-20 crushing season through Direct Benefit Transfer due to switching over to the revenue sharing based sugarcane price fixation policy from 2017-18 crushing season. 10. The Commissioner of Sugar is also permitted to incur expenditure of Rs. 60.00 Lakh (Rupees Sixty lakh only) (i.e Rs.25.00 Lakh for data preparation and Rs. 35.00 Lakh for contingency) from the savings expected out of total sanctioned amount of Rs. 126.65 Crore (Rupees One hundred and twenty six Crore and sixty five lakh only) due to ineligible quantum of cane crushed by the sugar mills in 2019-20 season. 11. The expenditure sanctioned in paragraph 8 above shall be debited to the following head of account:- 2401 — 00 — Crop Husbandry—108 Commercial Crops - State’s Expenditure - LA Production Incentive to Sugarcane Farmers — 309 Grants — in - Aid — 03 Grants for Specific Schemes. (IFHRMS 2401 00 108 LA 309 03). 12. The Director of Agriculture is authorized to draw and disburse the expenditure amount sanctioned in para-10 above to the Commissioner of Sugar. 13. The Government also direct that the Sugar Mills shall continue to bear the transportation costs. 14. The Commissioner of Sugar is requested to implement the scheme of sanction of transitional production incentive directly to the farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer as per the detailed guidelines appended to this order. The Commissioner of Sugar is requested to ensure transfer of incentives to farmers in time by strict adherence to the above guidelines in implementation of the scheme. 15. The Commissioner of Sugar is also requested to send a status report on the implementation of the scheme periodically. 16.

items.text: Rs.2300+Rs.96.80 for additional % of recovery in 2016-17. State Advised Price was declared by Government of Tamil Nadu for 2016-17 as Rs.450 per MT and accordingly State Advised Price for Dharmapuri Cooperative 5 Sugar Mills was fixed at Rs.2846.80 and accordingly the sugar mills cleared the cane dues. On the same basis, the Transitional Production Incentive may be extended at Rs.137.50 per MT of cane for all these sugar mills also without linking recovery and hence uniformly across to all sugar mills. 2. Exemption : As the Tamil Nadu Government has enacted the Sugarcane (Regulation of Purchase Price Act 2018) and under the said Act, the Rules are being framed. Hence exemption from applicability of said Act and Rules for disbursement of Transitional Production Incentive may be given as done in the last year. 3. Data Entry of the Farmers : Huge time and effort of all the officials of the sugar mills, Government Data Centre and Department of Sugar is highly consumed for the processes such as making data entry of the farmers’ details provided by the sugar mills, making correction in the details of the farmers’ data base at the Government Data Centre (GDC), providing inputs to the District Level Committee (DLC) and verification of data for the disbursement of the Transitional Production Incentive in their bank account. Even for verification of private sugar mills’ data, the officials of cooperative and public sector are also involved. Mostly the Cane officials of cooperative and public sector sugar mills are engaged in these activities. Hence, the mills have incurred expenditure on Travelling and Dearness allowance for Direct Benefit Transfer.

items.text: Even for verification of private sugar mills’ data, the officials of cooperative and public sector are also involved. Mostly the Cane officials of cooperative and public sector sugar mills are engaged in these activities. Hence, the mills have incurred expenditure on Travelling and Dearness allowance for Direct Benefit Transfer. Based on the problems faced by the officials of sugar mills and the Government Data Centre during the implementation of the scheme for 2017-18 and 2018-19 crushing seasons, it is suggested that.a third party consultant chosen based on a tender process, may be engaged to carry out certain processes viz., making data entry and details collected from the sugar mills, compilation of the data base in a format prescribed by the Government Data Centre, providing data entries, doing correction works, providing necessary inputs to the District Level Committee as prescribed by the Commissioner of Sugar in the form of reports, excel sheets etc for verification and compiling the UTR Nos. as evidence for disbursement of Transitional Production Incentive through Direct Benefit Transfer. 4, Cane diversion (a) In case of cane diversion, proper cane diversion order should be obtained from the Commissioner of Sugar. The cane drawing / cane sending mill should produce the order issued by the Commissioner of Sugar along with certification of concerned Assistant Director of Agriculture / Ex-Officio Cane Inspector given on Village wise cane drawal from the allotted areas to claim Transitional Production Incentive. Further, the Transitional Production Incentive will be eligible for the cane diversion made from the date of receipt of the cane diversion order / ratification order issued by the Commissioner of Sugar. (b) Certain Assistant Directors of Agriculture are designated as Ex-Officio Cane Inspectors for sugar mills.

(b) Certain Assistant Directors of Agriculture are designated as Ex-Officio Cane Inspectors for sugar mills. Cane diversion would be passed by the Commissioner of Sugar only after getting remarks of the Ex-Officio Cane Inspectors and assurance by receiving mills that Fair and Remunerative Price will be paid within the stipulated time. The Ex-Officio Cane Inspectors concerned are directed to verify the actual quantity of cane drawn out of the cane diversion claims made by sugar mills after collecting necessary documentary evidences to prove the genuineness of farmers who have diverted cane to cane receiving mill as per cane diversion order and only after ensuring the fact that the claims are true, Assistant Director of Agriculture / Ex-Officio Cane Inspector shall approve the claims forwarded by the District Level Committee. 5, Modalities suggested for the transfer [unclear figure] Transitional Production Incentive to the bank accounts of farmers : For effective implementation of the Transitional Production Incentive Scheme in a time bound manner, the following procedures may be followed :- Procedures i. Preparation of database at State level : All the Sugar Mills shall be directed to submit report on the quantity of registered cane supplied by each farmer from the concerned demarcated area of the sugar mill during 2019-20 sugarcane crushing season along with the credential documents supporting the claim including Aadhaar, revenue records for land holding, details on cane supplied, mirror accounts for Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Society and savings bank account in case of loan accounts to the office of the Commissioner of Sugar in the format specified by the Commissioner of Sugar.

The Commissioner of Sugar in consultation with the Government Data Centre, will design and create mill wise farmers’ database and through an engaged suitable third party consultant, the data received from all the mills will be compiled and a database of farmers for processing in Government Data Centre to be prepared. The district wise list of farmer's along with the required details will be sent to the District Collector concerned for field verification and certification. ii. items.text: From the Registrar, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Letter No.E1/G.O(Ms) No.171 07 Agriculture (AU) Department, dated 09.07.2018/2019 dated 02.05.2019. From the Registrar, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University Letter No. E1/G.O(Ms) No.171 amendment/2019 dated 27.05.2020 and 3K OK OK 2K OK In the Government Order 4" read above, it has been ordered that all Deemed Universities intending to open a new department in the campus or an off-campus centre / institution in Agriculture and allied (P.T.O) subjects /2/ viz., Agriculture, Horticulture, Agricultural Engineering, Forestry, Food Technology, Biotechnology, Sericulture, Home / Community Science, and Food Nutrition & Dietetics should obtain “No Objection Certification” from the State Government after getting accreditation from the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). 2. On taking up a review on the status of agricultural education being imparted in the State, by the Institutions deemed to be Universities, the following findings were emanated:- (i) (ii) (iii) Fourteen Government Colleges and 28 private colleges affiliated to the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University are imparting degree and diploma courses in Agriculture, Horticulture, Agricultural Engineering, Forestry, Food Technology, Biotechnology, Sericulture, Home/Community Science, and Food Nutrition & Dietetics, in the State.

items.text: Besides the colleges run by the Government and private colleges which are affiliated to the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, the following Institutions, which are deemed to be Universities, are also offering Agriculture and allied courses as per the available information: - 1. SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Chennai. ‘2. Vellore Institute of Technology, Vellore. 3. Kalasalingam University, Srivilliputhur. 4. Karunya University, Coimbatore. 5. Prist University, Thanjavur. 6. Bharath University, Chennai. 7. Sri Ramakrishna Mission Vidyalaya Institute of Agri. டே Rural Development, Coimbatore. 8. Amirtha Vishwa Vidhayapeetham, Coimbatore. 9. Saveetha University, Chennai. As per the Indian Council of Agricultural Research guidelines as well as the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University Act, 1971 (Tamil Nadu Act 8 of 1971) and its Hand Book for Establishing Agricultural College, any institution which intends to offer Agriculture and allied courses under the purview of the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University has to fulfill certain minimum stipulated guidelines. The guidelines include possession of 110 acres of land which should be cultivable and contiguous, obtaining No Objection Certificate from the Government of Tamil Nadu, affiliation from Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, etc., (iv) The University Grants Commission Guidelines, stipulate the following criteria to be fulfilled by the Institutions deemed to be Universities to start new departments: - “Clause 2.1: Clause 2.2:

items.text: Clause 2.2: Clause 3.4: /3/ The Deemed University intending to open a new Department in its campus or an off- campus center / institution shall approach the University Grants Commission (UGC) atleast six months prior to opening such center on a proforma prescribed for this purpose (Annexure - I). The Deemed University desirous of starting the new off - Campus center/institution or introducing a new course/programme in a professional subject, shall comply with all the requirements as required by statutory Professional Councils and obtain their prior approval before approaching the University Grants Commission. The new Departments, new off-campus center / institution shall be set up only after obtaining approval of the UGC and that of the concerned State Government where such a center is proposed to be established. The University Grants Commission shall cause spot visit/ verification of the proposed new departments, new off-Campus_ center/ institutions to verify its infrastructure facilities, programmes, faculty, financial viability, etc., before giving permission to start the centre. The report of the committee shall be considered by the Commission for its approval. XXX XXX XXX The new off-campus centre/ institution / off-shore campus shall offer only those courses which are approved by the appropriate bodies of the deemed university.

XXX XXX XXX The new off-campus centre/ institution / off-shore campus shall offer only those courses which are approved by the appropriate bodies of the deemed university. If the course to be offered in the centre is in technical / professional subject, its academic programmes shall have to be approved by the concerned statutory professional council.” 2004, (P.T.O) /4/ It is thus clear that the Institutions deemed to be Universities should have obtained No Objection Certificate from the State Government for the establishment of new Departments or off-campus centre for offering agriculture or allied courses as per the above University Grants Commission Guidelines, 2004. 3. Besides, University Grants Commission (Institutions Deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2016 provide as follows: “12.01 An_ institution deemed to [unclear figure] university — shall normally operate within its own main Campus as is declared by the Central Government ர the notification and conduct approved programmes _ of study falling within the area of its specialization. 12.02 If an institution deemed to be university, accredited by NAAC with highest grade or all eligible courses accredited with the highest grade of NBA, wishes to start new Course / Programme/ Department/ School/Centre in its existing campus / off-campus in areas and disciplines that form a part of its existing academic framework, it may do so in such allied school shall be started after the approval of the respective authorities of the Deemed to be University and the concerned Statutory Council(s), wherever required, and after creating all the necessary infrastructure and other facilities as per the norms of concerned statutory council(s)”. 4.

items.text: 4. With reference to the Government Order in the reference 4" read above, the Registrar, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University in his letters 5" & 6" read above has stated that as per Indian Council of Agricultural Research guidelines, any University/College can apply for accreditation only after one batch of students pass out from the University/College. Using this provision, the Institutions Deemed to be Universities will apply for No Objection Certificate to State Government only after the pass out of first batch of students from the College, which will take 4 years. If the said Universities attempt to get Indian Council of Agricultural Research accreditation after one batch of students pass out from the Institute after 4 years, the whole process of accreditation (viz., submission of Letter of Intent (LoI), Institutional Eligibility for Accreditation (IEA) and submission of Self Study Report (SSR) after approval of Letter of Intent and Institutional Eligibility for Accreditation by Indian Council of Agricultural Research) will take another 8 to 12 months. Hence, it may be possible for them to get Indian Council of Agricultural Research accreditation only after 5 years and then only “No Objection Certificate” of State /3/ Government can be obtained as per the conditions stipulated in the existing Government Order 4" read above. By the time they apply for No Objection Certificate to State Government after five years of starting Agriculture and allied courses, further student batches will be admitted and with this, considerable number of students would undergo the Agriculture & allied degree programmes with uncertainty of outcome of accreditation proposal submitted to the Indian Council of Agricultural Research. Hence, the Registrar, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University has requested the Government to issue fresh and comprehensive directions in this regard. 5.

items.text: Hence, the Registrar, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University has requested the Government to issue fresh and comprehensive directions in this regard. 5. The Government have carefully examined the request of the Registrar, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University in the light of the University Grants Commission’s Guidelines, 2004 and the University Grants Commission (Institutions Deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2016 and the correspondence of Indian Council of Agricultural Research. The analysis of the above does point out the need to issue further clarity on starting of Agriculture and allied courses by Institutions deemed to be Universities in order to ensure that quality education to students is assured and the students of such Universities possess degrees which are accredited by the Statutory Technical body concerned. The Government have, therefore, decided to issue fresh and comprehensive orders in supersession of the earlier orders issued in the Government Order ஆரி read above. Accordingly, the Government direct that all Institutions deemed to be Universities in the State intending to open a new Department in its campus or an off-campus centre/institution in Agriculture and allied subjects viz., Agriculture, Horticulture, Agricultural Engineering, Forestry, Food Technology, Agricultural Biotechnology, Sericulture, Home / Community Science, Food Nutrition and Dietetics, should obtain “No Objection Certificate” from the State Government before starting the above mentioned Agriculture and allied programmes in Tamil Nadu. Institutions deemed to be Universities need to also obtain ICAR accreditation as per norms. 6. There is a need to get clarity about adherence to the University Grants Commission guidelines by the Institutions deemed to be Universities which are already running the Agriculture and allied courses in Tamil Nadu.

The Government, therefore, direct that the Institutions deemed to be Universities mentioned above should submit proof of having obtained approval of the State Government for the establishment of Department / off-campus centre offering Agriculture or allied courses. If not obtained so far, in the interest of the large number of students pursuing the said courses in such Institutions, shall get approval of the Government of Tamil Nadu, within a period of six months from the date of issue of this order. items.text: 3. In the letter third read above, the Director of Agriculture has stated that Cotton crop is normally cultivated in an area of around 4.0 lakh acres with an average production of 3-4 lakh bales annually. For increasing the production and productivity of Cotton, interventions such as Production and distribution of quality varietal seeds, Micro irrigation, Mechanization, Improved agronomic practices, Integrated Irrigation, Nutrient, Weed and Pest management approaches were executed in the major cotton growing districts by the department. 4. Tamil Nadu is a pioneering State in producing Long and Extra Long Staple cotton in the country. Farmers are encouraged to grow 2 high-yielding cotton varieties with superior fibre quality like SVPR 4, SVPR 5, Co 14, Surabhi, and Suraj to get better price for cotton. The staple length constitutes the basic norm for evaluating quality of cotton in the trade by the consuming textile industry and fixation of Cotton procurement price. 5. Cotton crop not only provides fibre for the textile industry, but also plays a vital role in the cattle feed and oil industries with its seeds rich in oil and protein. Thus, cotton has been a premier agricultural crop, playing a major role in the national economy both in rural and urban sectors. Hence as a source of natural fibre, cattle feed, and oil, it is imperative to increase the Cotton production in the state. 6. The Director of Agriculture further stated that during the year 2019-20, the scheme was implemented with a financial outlay of Rs.11 Crores with an objective of increasing the area under Extra Long Staple Cotton to 30,000 Ha. 7.

Cotton crop consumes 55% of total pesticide consumption share, accounting for 40% of total production costs. This fact signifies the impact of insect pests, diseases, and increased agrochemical usage in cotton cultivation. Hence, to sustain the cotton production in the State, it is imperative that the productivity is driven by Integrated Pest Management Approaches which can be adopted easily by farmers. 8. During the Budget session, the Hon’ble Minister (Agriculture) has, interalia made the following announcement on 24.03.2020:- “பல்வேறு பயிர்பாதுகாப்பு முறைகளை உள்ளடக்கிய ஒருங்கிணைந்த பூச்சி மேலாண்மை முறைகளை பருத்தி விவசாயிகளிடையே பிரபலப்படுத்துவதற்காக 2020- 2021-ம்‌ ஆண்டில்‌ ரூ.8 கோடி நிதி ஒதுக்கீடு செய்யப்படும்‌.” 9. I. Promotion of ELS/varietal cotton 1.

Distribution of MN mixture:- The micronutrients essential to cotton are zinc, iron, manganese, copper, boron, molybdenum and chlorine. Widespread deficiencies of micronutrients are commonly observed in the intensive cropping zones of major cotton growing regions. Cotton being deep rooted removes large quantities of nutrients from the soil profile. For the long term sustainability of cotton and to increase the productivity of cotton, it is essential to replenish the soil with the balanced amount of nutrients. Hence it is programmed to distribute MN mixtures through AEC for 25,000 Hectares @ 50% subsidy amount limited to Rs. 500/- per ha, a. Physical : 25,000 Ha b. Fund required : Rs. 125.00 lakh c. Rate of subsidy : 50% of the Sale price limited to Rs.500/ per Hectare, whichever is less. 3. Distribution of Liquid Bio fertilizers Considering the escalating cost of fertilizers and the need to utilize all available nutrient sources, it is rational to use fertilizers in conjunction with appropriate biofertilizers and organic manures. In _ cotton, application of biofertilizers such as nitrogen-fixing Azosprillum and phosphorus-solublizing Phosphobacteria increases the yield by 25 per cent. Hence, it is programmed to distribute liquid formulation of biofertilizers through AEC to farmers for 25,000 Hectares @ 50% subsidy amount limited to Rs. 150/- per ha. a. Physical : 25,000 Ha b.
